commits.pr_title: [Docs] List speculative decoding methods supported by the Transformers backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

List the speculative decoding methods the Transformers modeling backend supports in its docs section.

## Claims

- EAGLE-3, DFlash, DSpark and XPress run on the Transformers backend with the same GSM8K accuracy and acceptance length as the native implementation.
- DFlash2 shares DFlash's speculator and loader, and takes the same three things from the target (aux hidden states, embedding, LM head), so it is supported by code path.
- MTP is supported for models following the Transformers MTP standard (`TransformersForMTP`).

## Validation

GSM8K, 200 questions, greedy, one B200, vLLM `abfa95d34f`, Transformers 5.23. Accuracy / acceptance length:

| Method | Target / draft | `model_impl="vllm"` | `model_impl="transformers"` |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash | `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` / `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` | 0.87 / 3.70 | 0.88 / 3.72 |
| DSpark | `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` / `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` | 0.88 / 4.20 | 0.88 / 4.19 |
| XPress | `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` / `UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16` | 0.895 / 7.78 | 0.89 / 7.78 |

EAGLE-3 is already covered in CI by `qwen3_eagle3-transformers` in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/test_eagle_correctness.py`. DFlash2 has no public target the Transformers backend can load yet (Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 use linear attention, Ripple's remote code calls SDPA directly), so it was not run end to end.

```python
llm = LLM(target, model_impl=impl, max_model_len=4096, disable_log_stats=False,
          speculative_config=dict(method=method, model=draft, num_speculative_tokens=k))
evaluate_gsm8k_offline(llm, num_questions=200)  # tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py
compute_acceptance_len(llm.get_metrics())       # tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/utils.py
```

P-EAGLE (from the speculators algorithms list) is omitted because vLLM rejects it for every backend.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MoE] Dequantize only distinct routed experts in OCP MX emulation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #68050 (merged; this branch now contains only its own changes). For MXFP4 weights with bf16 activations on ROCm, the OCP MX emulation MoE now dequantizes only the batch's **distinct** routed experts, at any batch size, without a host sync. A fused Triton gather and dequant kernel does the work and skips unused slots on the GPU. This fixes #68050's one regression (eager batches with many top-k slots but few distinct experts) and is faster than or equal to #68050 and main in every measured case. cc @jbelofamd

## Claims

- End to end, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B MXFP4 under `--moe-backend emulation` on one MI355X: **2.1x output throughput at concurrency 4**, 1.2x at concurrency 32. GSM8K is unchanged.
- MoE layer microbenchmark (256 experts, top-8): faster than or equal to #68050 and main in every measured cell (one cell at 1.01x, within noise), eager and CUDA graph, I=256 and I=2048. Examples: 0.70x at 1 token, 0.05–0.3x with skewed routing, 0.82x with dense 128-token routing.
- The dequant kernel matches quark's default `dq_mxfp4` bit for bit (apart from NaN payloads, which differ between MI300 and MI355X), and runs at about 5 TB/s vs quark's 3.9 TB/s on a full dequant.
- No host sync, CUDA-graph capturable. Other schemes and dtypes keep #68050's path unchanged.

## Validation

All on MI355X (gfx950).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k "not test_mxfp4_loading_and_execution_moe"` | 62 passed, 133 skipped (other hardware or schemes) |
| `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest "tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_vit_cudagraph_image[kimi_k3]"` | passed |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, `lm_eval --model vllm` with `moe_backend=emulation,linear_backend=emulation`, run with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | #68050: 0.3639 / 0.3040, this PR: 0.3776 / 0.3048 (flexible / strict, ±0.013) |

`linear_backend=emulation` is needed because the model's dense MXFP4 layers fail in AITer's `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` with 3-D inputs. That failure also happens on main and is unrelated to this PR.

**End to end:** `vllm bench throughput --model vllm-project/qwen_1.5-moe-a2.7b-mxfp4 --moe-backend emulation --linear-backend emulation --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 256 --max-num-seqs C`, two runs each, output tok/s:

| C | #68050 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 282 / 283 | **592 / 603** |
| 32 | 1659 / 1708 | **1998 / 2076** |

**MoE layer**, E=256, top-8, H=7168, ms/call. Median of 9×20 calls with main, #68050 and this PR interleaved; outputs bit-identical across the three.

</details>

## Details

- **`dedup_routed_experts`** uses two Triton launches. The first is a single-program histogram of ids in `[0, E)`. It writes a compacted `used[C]` (distinct experts ascending, then `-1`), where `C = min(numel, E)`, plus a rank table. The second renumbers `topk_ids` by that table across many programs; `-1` and out-of-range ids map to `-1`, which the expert alignment skips. Splitting it into two launches means the renumbering only reads the rank table after it is fully written: no intra-kernel global-memory handoff, so no barrier or fence is needed.
- **`dequant_routed_mxfp4`** uses a 2-D grid: tiles of 256 32-value blocks by `min(C, 32)` slot groups. Each program loads one e8m0 scale per block and loops over its slots until the first `-1`. Unused slots therefore cost nothing, which relies on `used` being compacted. The e2m1 decode builds fp32 bits directly, including `-0`, scale 0 as 2^-127 and 255 as inf, so the result matches quark bit for bit apart from NaN payloads (`0 × inf` under scale 255 is `0xFFC0` in quark on MI300, `0x7FFF` here; the test checks NaN positions instead). Existing e2m1 helpers in the tree are private to MiniMax-M3 and MXFP4-MLA ops, so this PR doesn't import them.
- **Gating:** the fused path requires ROCm, bf16 activations and `w_mxfp4*` weights, contiguous per-expert weights and scales, and no dynamic fp8 a2 scale. Unused slots leave the rows of `-1` ids unwritten, and a tensor-wide a2 scale would read them; quark rejects dynamic `a_fp8` today, so this only guards other entry points. Everything else keeps #68050's per-slot path (up to E/4 slots) or full dequant.
- **Races and graphs:**
  - Programs write disjoint output regions and only read their inputs.
  - Shapes depend only on `topk_ids.shape`.
  - Independent reviews found no defects across 840 dedup cases and 612 end-to-end configs (bf16/fp16; E 16/60/256; top 1/2/8; up to 2048 tokens; `-1` padding).
  - 3,000 CUDA-graph replays sharing one pool, plus a 3-layer chained graph, were bit-exact against full dequantization. Unused slots were NaN-poisoned and never read.
- **Tests:**
  - The routed test is now parametrized over bf16 (fused) and fp16 (per-slot). It NaN-poisons unused fused slots and imports quark before the sync check, because quark's import copies a lookup table to the GPU.
  - New: an exhaustive kernel check against quark (every packed byte under every scale) and dedup edge cases (one top-1 id, int64 ids, `-1` padding, out-of-range ids). Without the Triton specialization guard (`do_not_specialize`), the one-id case silently gives wrong output, so the test locks that in.
- **Limitations:**
  - Peak transient memory is `C = min(numel, E)` bf16 experts. That's never more than #68050 or main under graphs, but main's synced eager `torch.unique` allocates less for skewed batches of 32+ tokens (about 5 GB vs 21 GB at I=2048).
  - The GEMM config lookup uses `C` as the expert count, as in #68050.
  - Bit-identity is against quark's default HIP `dq_mxfp4`. With `QUARK_MXFP4_IMPL=triton`, quark flushes scale-0 blocks to 0 where this kernel keeps subnormals (about 1e-39).
- **Complexity:** about 195 lines in a new module plus about 40 lines of wiring, justified by the throughput and layer numbers above.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR covers fused routed MXFP4 dequant.

commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] Add --random-mm-video-encode-fps to random-mm
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`random-mm`'s synthetic video generator hardcodes the MP4 container encode rate at 30fps (`generate_synthetic_video`), so `--random-mm-bucket-config`'s `num_frames` does not reliably map to the frame count a target model actually processes — that depends on the model's own video preprocessing (e.g. duration-based resampling at its own native fps).

Adds `--random-mm-video-encode-fps` so the encode rate can be set to match a target model's native fps, making `num_frames` self-consistent. Backward compatible: defaults to 30.0 (the previous hardcoded value).

Companion to #65499 (synthetic audio support), which touches the same file.

## Claims

- `--random-mm-video-encode-fps` changes the actual number of frames a target model samples from a synthetic video, for the same `--random-mm-bucket-config`, by changing how much wall-clock duration those `num_frames` represent.
- `--random-mm-video-encode-fps` rejects non-positive values at argument-parse time, not deep inside `cv2.VideoWriter` during sampling.
- The Rust `vllm-bench` CLI-parity snapshot stays in sync: the new flag is allowlisted as Python-only (Rust's `random-mm` only generates images), so `VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1` delegation does not silently reject it.

## Validation

**Setup:** `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct`, vLLM (this branch), ROCm (MI350-class, `smci350-d02-21`), `--enforce-eager`, single GPU.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 8192 --enforce-eager --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 1}'
```

Same bucket config (`{(360, 420, 16): 1.0}`, i.e. 16 frames), only `--random-mm-video-encode-fps` varied:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name random-mm --num-prompts 6 --max-concurrency 2 --random-input-len 50 --random-output-len 8 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 1}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{(360, 420, 16): 1.0}' [--random-mm-video-encode-fps 2.0] --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

| `--random-mm-video-encode-fps` | Successful requests | Total input tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30.0 (default) | 6/6 | 2766 |
| 2.0 (Qwen2.5-VL's native sampling fps) | 6/6 | 9786 |

Same bucket config, same seed, only the encode fps changed — a 3.5x difference in total input tokens, confirming the flag actually changes how much video content the model samples, not just that the request succeeds. (At 30fps, 16 frames is only ~0.53s of video, which the model's own duration-based resampling undersamples relative to its ~2fps native rate; at 2fps those same 16 frames span ~8s, giving the resampler far more material to draw frames from.)

Argument validation, confirmed directly:

```
$ vllm bench serve ... --random-mm-video-encode-fps 0
error: argument --random-mm-video-encode-fps: must be a positive float, got 0.0
```

Rust parity: regenerated `rust/src/bench/tests/python_serve_flags.txt` via `tests/benchmarks/test_rust_bench_cli_parity.py` against this branch's real installed package and confirmed it now includes `--random-mm-video-encode-fps`, matching the committed snapshot exactly (no diff). The `random_mm.rs`/`cli_parity.rs` changes were reviewed directly against the crate's own type definitions for correctness; a live `cargo test` was not completed in this validation pass (environment constraint, toolchain removed mid-session) — flagging this explicitly rather than claiming more than was actually run.

### Tests

No new unit test added for the positive-float rejection specifically (the fix is a one-line `type=` change); existing `tests/benchmarks/test_random_multimodal_dataset_video.py` (13 tests) still passes unmodified on this branch.

## Details

`generate_synthetic_video`'s `fps` was a hardcoded local variable; it's now a parameter (`encode_fps`) threaded through `generate_mm_item` → `sample` → the CLI, with the previous hardcoded value (30.0) kept as the default for backward compatibility. The validation lives in a small nested `_parse_positive_float` CLI type function, following the same local-helper convention as the existing `_parse_mm_bucket_config` in the same function, rather than a module-level helper — the `cv2.VideoWriter` failure this replaces only surfaced as a generic "Failed to create video writer" deep in sampling, with no indication the root cause was an invalid fps argument.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Make test_amd_ci_fast_exit independent of inherited signal state
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Makes `tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` independent of the signal state the CI pod hands it, and logs the node, KFD topology and `SigBlk`/`SigIgn` in the AMD CI preflight. Over Nov 10-12, `:amd: (MI250) Docker Build Metadata` failed 20 times on `ci`, all on two MI250 nodes without `/sys/class/kfd` (smci250-ccs-aus-c15-03: 14, smci250-ccs-aus-c12-08: 6). It passed on every other MI250 node. For example: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101368#01a1c3e8-f928-4218-ad5d-76e31135cbbe, https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102049#01a1ce70-6993-4910-b78a-3c357dadb8be

## Claims

- On a pod whose parent left SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/SIGBUS ignored or blocked, `test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` no longer fails with `assert 0 == -SIGSEGV`.
- The AMD CI log now shows which node a pod ran on, how many KFD topology nodes it sees, and its blocked/ignored signal masks, so a bad node shows up in the log itself.

## Validation

`pytest tests/tools/test_amd_ci_fast_exit.py` on MI355X: 12 passed, before and after the change.

I simulated the bad pod with a pytest plugin that, after pytest's faulthandler is set up, leaves the fault signals ignored or blocked in the outer pytest. I also tried a wrapper that blocks or ignores them before exec.

| Parent signal state | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| SIGSEGV ignored in outer pytest | 5 failed (`assert 0 == -SIGSEGV`), same 5 tests as CI | 12 passed |
| SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/SIGBUS blocked | 6 failed | 12 passed |
| ignored + blocked | 6 failed | 12 passed |

`pre-commit` passes on both files (shellcheck included). `bash -n` passes on the script, and I ran the new preflight line by hand: `pod: node=x kfd_topology_nodes=10 SigBlk: 0000000000000000 SigIgn: 0000000000000000`.

## Details

- Root cause in the test: an ignored or blocked SIGSEGV survives `fork`/`exec`, and `subprocess` does not reset it. The child's `faulthandler._sigsegv()` at teardown is a `raise(SIGSEGV)` that then returns, so the child exits 0. `_run` now passes a `preexec_fn` that resets SIGSEGV, SIGBUS and SIGABRT to `SIG_DFL` and unblocks them. The assertions are unchanged.
- In CI, the abort case also returned -11 instead of -6. I could not reproduce that part here. Resetting SIGABRT and unblocking it covers it if the cause is inherited state too.
- What actually injects the bad state on those nodes is not proven. Only the failing pods log rocprofiler-sdk's `agent topology: no platform matched; falling back to gnulinux-kfd` and `sysfs nodes path ... does not exist`. The new preflight line will settle this the next time a pod lands on such a node. The node problem itself (no amdgpu/KFD) is being raised with the cluster owners.
- Why the MI250 copy of the step stays: `:computer: (CPU) Docker Build Metadata` runs the same files, but on the CPU image the 4 `test_kernel_symbol_map.py` HIP-compiler tests are skipped and the reporter library is built from source instead of using the image's `/usr/local/lib/libamd_ci_fault_trap.so`. The MI250 copy runs both. Moving the step to the `amd_cpu` lane is a ci-infra change, because that lane is the `no_plugin` image-build lane and native AMD test pods need a GPU device config. The step stays `no_gpu: true` on `mi250_1`.
- No user-visible change.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the failures and draft this change.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][Multimodal] Name every uncached item in the cache-miss error
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Closes #68428.

When a request skips the media data of some items and relies on their UUIDs hitting the processor cache, the processor rejects the request at the first item that missed. By then it has already found every missed item, but the error names only the first one. A client that resends that one item then meets the next miss, so it needs one more round trip for each missing item. This PR names all of them in one error.

## Claims

- The cache-miss error for items sent without data now names every such item, by modality and index, in one error.
- A request with a single missed item gets exactly the same message as before.
- The error is the same `ValueError`, raised before the cache is updated, so it is still an HTTP 400 and nothing else changes.

## Validation

The new test `test_omitted_media_cache_miss_names_every_item` in `tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/chat_completion/test_video.py` sends two videos and one image with only a UUID, none of them cached, through the OpenAI-compatible server, and checks the error message.

With main's `processor.py` (`4dbd382be`), the new test fails, because the error names only the image and neither video:

```text
    with pytest.raises(
E   AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match.
E     Expected regex: 'Cache miss for image at index 0; video at index 0, 1 but data is not provided'
E     Actual message: 'Error code: 400 - Cache miss for image at index 0 but data is not provided.'
====================== 1 failed, 22 deselected in 28.73s =======================
```

</details>

With this PR (`25fead1b8`) the new test passes, and the existing `test_omitted_video_url_requires_cached_uuid`, which checks the single-item message, still passes:

<details>
<summary>Command and output with this PR</summary>

```text
$ VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=4 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/chat_completion/test_video.py -k test_omitted -v --tb=short
platform darwin -- Python 3.12.11, pytest-9.2.0, pluggy-1.7.0
collecting ... collected 23 items / 21 deselected / 2 selected

tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/chat_completion/test_video.py::test_omitted_video_url_requires_cached_uuid[llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf] PASSED [ 50%]
tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/chat_completion/test_video.py::test_omitted_media_cache_miss_names_every_item[llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf] PASSED [100%]

================= 2 passed, 21 deselected in 205.41s (0:03:25) =================
```

</details>

I ran both on a CPU build of this branch on macOS (Apple silicon), with `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=4` because the default KV cache reservation did not fit beside other processes on that machine. CI collects this file in the entrypoints multimodal job (`.buildkite/test_areas/entrypoints.yaml`). The processor cache tests also pass with this PR: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py` gives 29 passed and 1 skipped, and the skipped test needs CUDA. `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes.

## Details

`_get_cache_missing_items` first lists every item that missed the cache, then walks that list and raised at the first item without data. It now collects every such item during the walk and raises once after it.

A request with a single missed item gets the old message exactly. With several missed items, the message still starts with "Cache miss for {modality} at index {idx}" for the first missed item. A check on that start keeps working, but a pattern for the whole old message no longer matches. Several indices are joined with commas and several modalities with semicolons. The new test gets "Cache miss for image at index 0; video at index 0, 1 but data is not provided." The image comes first because the chat path orders modalities as image, audio, video.

The engine side already follows this rule for its own cache miss: `MultiModalCacheMissError` carries every drifted hash, so "one retry then recovers the whole request, not one item per retry" (`vllm/multimodal/cache/base.py`). There the API process repairs its own state. Here only the client can repair the request, because only the client has the media, so the client needs the whole list.

This is not a duplicate. #55583 changes this same raise to `MultiModalProcessorCacheMissError` and catches it to render the conversation again with every item fetched, and it keeps the first-item message. The two PRs edit the same lines, so the one that lands second needs a rebase. If that error carried the list built here, its second render could fetch only the missing items. #44543 copies the raise into the Qwen2.5-Omni processor and would keep the old message there.

AI assistance was used to write this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Cache AiterFlashAttention K/V cache views per tensor
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Cache the K/V views that `AiterFlashAttentionImpl._split_kv_cache` builds, keyed on the `kv_cache` tensor, so ROCM_AITER_FA stops rebuilding them on every attention and KV-cache-update call. Same change as #64571 (FlashAttention) and #64890 (Triton), which do not touch this backend; tracked by #64572.

## Claims

- `_split_kv_cache` drops from 2.63 µs to 0.10 µs of host time per call on AMD EPYC 9575F, and an FP8 KV cache's call site, which also retypes the views, from 4.01 µs to 0.09 µs. In eager mode on MI325X, host time per Qwen3-8B decode step drops by 0.36 ms with 4 requests and 0.49 ms with 16.
- With `--enforce-eager`, Qwen3-8B serving throughput improves by 4.6-4.8% and TPOT by 4.2% on MI325X. On both, every server start with the change beat every start without it.
- The default compiled mode is unchanged (within 1%): uniform decode batches replay a full CUDA graph and never run this path.
- Generated tokens are bit-identical one request at a time, also with an FP8 KV cache, and GSM8K strict match is 87.41 in every run before and after.
- Outside the ROCm backend, only `clear_layer_kv_caches` changes: it also drops this cache on teardown.

## Validation

**Setup:** Qwen3-8B, 1x MI325X, TP=1, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-cf5cea2da37d3dfed27d2e0aa3041c3e553c2d57`, whose copies of both changed files match this PR's base. Before is the same container without this change.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --num-gpu-blocks-override 16000 --seed 0
```

The eager rows add `--enforce-eager`. `--num-gpu-blocks-override` gives both arms the same KV cache size.

### Host time

`_split_kv_cache` at 512 blocks, 8 KV heads, block size 16, head dim 128, bf16. AMD EPYC 9575F, one pinned core, median of 3 runs. Both versions return views with the same data pointer, shape and strides.

| Layout | Before | After | Saved per call (min, max) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default (`transpose(1, 2).split`) | 2.627 µs | 0.102 µs | 2.524 µs (2.519, 2.548) |
| shuffle (`unflatten.unbind`) | 1.914 µs | 0.099 µs | 1.815 µs (1.802, 1.834) |

With an FP8 KV cache, the call site, which also runs `.view(fp8_dtype)` on both views, takes 4.010 µs before and 0.093 µs after (saved 3.916 µs, min 3.894, max 3.958), same setup.

Per eager decode step on MI325X, in-process (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), 512 input / 256 output tokens per request, median of 4 rounds per process, processes alternating between arms, measured at 1003b5e4f:

| Requests | `execute_model` per step | Step time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 (5 processes per arm) | 8.34 -> 7.97 ms (-0.36 ms) | 8.87 -> 8.50 ms (-4.2%) |
| 16 (2 processes per arm) | 10.23 -> 9.74 ms (-0.49 ms) | 10.83 -> 10.34 ms (-4.6%) |

A CPU profile of these steps shows 72 fewer `split`, 72 fewer `transpose` and 144 fewer `narrow` calls per step, two per layer, and no other op change.

### Serving

`vllm bench serve`, random dataset, `--ignore-eos`, one warmup round with a different seed. Arms alternate on the same GPU. Medians of 8 runs per arm in eager mode (4 server starts × 2 seeds) and 9 in compiled mode (3 × 3). Eager servers are pinned to 16 cores on the GPU's NUMA node.

| Mode | ISL / OSL / conc | Total tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eager | 512 / 256 / 4 | 1310 -> 1373 (+4.8%) | 71.8 -> 71.0 ms | 8.92 -> 8.55 ms (-4.2%) |
| eager | 512 / 256 / 16 | 4304 -> 4501 (+4.6%) | 64.3 -> 65.3 ms | 10.86 -> 10.40 ms (-4.2%) |
| compiled (default) | 512 / 256 / 4 | 2120 -> 2122 (+0.1%) | 69.1 -> 68.5 ms | 5.41 -> 5.40 ms |

Without the change, throughput and TPOT varied by 1.0-3.6% between server starts, below the eager gains. TTFT and the compiled row move less than that variation. These runs predate the data pointer check, which adds 40 ns per call, and the FP8 view cache.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 0.0 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 120 --seed 1
```

Concurrency 16 uses `--num-prompts 160`.

### Accuracy: GSM8K (lm-eval, 1319 questions, 5-shot, completions)

| | Strict match | Flexible extract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 87.41 ± 0.91 | 88.02 ± 0.89 |
| After | 87.41 ± 0.91 | 87.79 ± 0.90 |

Strict match is 87.41 in all five runs (3 before, 2 after). Flexible extract moves by up to 3 questions between runs of the same arm (87.79-88.02 before). With one request at a time, all 1,152 generated tokens and their logprobs over 12 fixed prompts are bit-identical, in both compiled and eager mode.

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3-8B,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False
```

### Tests

- `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_fa_kv_view_cache.py` (CPU): 8 passed. Without this change 7 of the 8 fail, and dropping the identity check, the data pointer check, the `clear_layer_kv_caches` reset or the FP8 retype, rebuilding the FP8 views on every call, or returning copies instead of views each fails at least one.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_fa.py` on MI325X: 97 passed, with and without this change.
- FP8 KV cache on MI325X: greedy output for 8 prompts × 64 tokens, one request at a time, matches the base token for token with identical logprobs in eager mode, the default compiled mode, and compiled with `splitting_ops=[]` and the fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV pass.
- Not run: `tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py`, shuffle layout end to end, `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update` (Qwen3 never takes it), gfx950.

## Details

`_split_kv_cache` runs once for attention and once for the KV-cache update in every layer, on every eager or piecewise step. `AiterFlashAttentionMetadataBuilder` declares `UNIFORM_BATCH`, so in the default compiled mode uniform decode batches replay a full graph and only prefill and mixed batches reach it; with `--enforce-eager` every decode step does.

The cache is keyed on the `kv_cache` tensor object and its data pointer, so a tensor re-pointed in place also rebuilds its views. A layer's KV cache changes only in `initialize_kv_cache` (including the minimal profiling cache) and `extend_kv_cache`, which bind new tensors, and in `clear_layer_kv_caches` (profiling teardown and shutdown), which drops the cache. Sleep and wake, weight updates and CUDA graph pool swaps keep the same tensors at the same addresses.

For an FP8 KV cache the entry also holds the FP8 views, which `forward`, `do_kv_cache_update` and `do_rope_and_kv_cache_update` take; `do_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_update` and the MUSE fusion pass keep the raw views.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Serve the non-causal DSpark draft on TRITON_MLA under DCP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

TRITON_MLA can now serve a non-causal multi-token MLA draft (DSpark) while the MLA KV cache is sharded by decode context parallelism (DCP), on gfx942 (CDNA 3). This is a follow-up to #54546 by @YukioZzz, who asked us to take it over. His two commits are kept as authored by him, and he is co-author on ours. The PR needed more than a conflict fix, because #51065 removed the code it edited.

## Validation

**Unit tests**

Commands:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py
```

Results on MI325X:

| Suite | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_mla_noncausal.py` | 8 passed | 10 passed |
| `test_mla_backends.py` | 63 passed, 597 skipped | 63 passed, 597 skipped |
| `test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py` | 16 passed | 16 passed |
| `test_attention_selector.py` | 40 passed, 57 skipped | 40 passed, 57 skipped |
| `test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py` | 80 passed | 80 passed |

The two new tests in `test_mla_noncausal.py` fail against the variants they guard against:

- `test_dcp_noncausal_group_keeps_spec_decode_reorder_threshold` fails with main's threshold logic.
- `test_dcp_causal_group_without_varlen_support_stays_single_token` fails if the threshold honors the flag without checking that the group is non-causal.

`pre-commit` is clean, including mypy.

**End to end** (8x MI325X, gfx942)

Server command:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only -tp 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 4 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'
```

- **main:** fails at draft load:
  ```
  ValueError: Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_MLA is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['non-causal MLA attention with DCP not supported']
  ```
- **This PR:** starts with the target on ROCM_AITER_MLA and the draft on TRITON_MLA, with no tracebacks.
  - FULL graphs are captured for the target (2 sizes) and the DSpark draft (4 sizes). `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` is downgraded to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` because the model has no piecewise submodule.
  - On current main the capture sizes match the run on earlier main, and the KV cache is 590,370 tokens (591,462 on earlier main).
  - Instrumented runs on earlier main show the draft builder at `reorder_batch_threshold=8`, and every draft step running as decode with `num_prefills=0`.

GSM8K, all 1319 questions:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=4,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot {5,20}
```

Block rejection sampling. Every row runs this PR. It was first tested on earlier main (`74340c7300`) and then rebased onto current main (`77f58e5304`):

| PR rebased on | DCP | n-shot | strict-match | flexible-extract | mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| current main | 8 | 5 | 0.9560 ± 0.0056 | 0.9560 ± 0.0056 | 4.63 |
| current main | 8 | 20 | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 4.63 |
| earlier main | 8 | 5 | 0.9575 ± 0.0056 | 0.9575 ± 0.0056 | 4.62 |
| earlier main | 1 | 5 | 0.9575 ± 0.0056 | 0.9575 ± 0.0056 | 4.62 |

Mean acceptance length is `1 + accepted / drafts` from the Prometheus counters over each run. Both current-main runs used the same server, back to back.

Long context: RULER NIAH at 64k, 100 samples per task, on current main with `--max-model-len 67584`. Prompts are about 64.8k tokens and are identical at both DCP sizes.

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=4,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None,max_length=67584 \
  --tasks niah_multikey_2,niah_multikey_3,niah_multivalue \
  --metadata '{"max_seq_lengths":[65536],"tokenizer":"moonshotai/Kimi-K3"}' --limit 100
```

| Task | DCP 1 | DCP 8 |
|---|---|---|
| `niah_multikey_2` | 100/100 | 100/100 |
| `niah_multikey_3` | 100/100 | 100/100 |
| `niah_multivalue` | 100/100 | 100/100 |
| mean acceptance length | 4.71 | 4.64 |

The scores are saturated at both sizes, so as a finer check: for the two multi-key tasks, the retrieved answer is token-identical between DCP 1 and DCP 8 in 200 of 200 samples. For `niah_multivalue`, both sizes return all four values every time, sometimes in a different order.


vllm bench serve on this PR, DCP 1 vs DCP 8 (random input, 1024 output, concurrency 1)

Command: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len {8192,65536} --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 1`, with 10 prompts at 8k and 5 at 64k.

Every row runs this PR; main cannot start the DCP 8 config. The table compares DCP sizes, not main and PR. The slower 8k DCP 8 TPOT is the cost of sharding a short context: the per-layer DCP communication outweighs the small attention saving. At 64k, DCP 8 is faster than DCP 1 and holds 2.8x the KV cache.

| Input | DCP | TPOT p50 | output tok/s | KV cache (tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k | 1 | 23.8 ms | 38.0 | 430k (`--max-model-len 16384`) |
| 8k | 8 | 36.7 ms | 27.5 | 591k (`--max-model-len 16384`) |
| 64k | 1 | 30.4 ms | 26.7 | 671k (`--max-model-len 67584`) |
| 64k | 8 | 26.2 ms | 29.9 | 1.88M (`--max-model-len 67584`) |

Random inputs keep the acceptance length at 1.36–1.44, so these runs mostly measure attention and communication cost.

## Details

**Root cause.** #51065 moved the reorder-threshold setup into `MLACommonMetadataBuilder.__init__`. `_init_reorder_batch_threshold` clamps the threshold to 1 under DCP unless the builder passes `supports_dcp_with_varlen`, and TRITON_MLA does not pass it.

#54546 declared `supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp` on TRITON_MLA, which is enough for backend selection and `_validate_dspark_dcp_support`. But the draft builder would still keep threshold 1, so FULL cudagraph capture of the 7-token draft block would trip `assert m.max_query_len <= self.reorder_batch_threshold` in `build_for_cudagraph_capture`. Its logits workspace would also be sized for one row per request.

**Why not `supports_dcp_with_varlen=True` in TRITON_MLA.** That would also raise the threshold for causal TRITON_MLA groups under DCP, such as an MTP or Eagle target. Their multi-token verify would then reach `forward_mqa` and hit `assert self.dcp_world_size == 1, "causal multi-token decode is not supported with DCP"`. Today those batches run as prefill.

**Change.** The common builder keeps the spec-decode threshold under DCP for a non-causal group whose backend declares `supports_non_causal_multi_token_dcp`. This is the same capability `_validate_dspark_dcp_support` already checks for that group. TRITON_MLA declares the flag only on gfx942 (`get_cdna_version() == 3`), which is where this has been validated. TRITON_MLA reserves its workspace after `super().__init__()`, so the reservation sees the final threshold.

**Why gfx942 only.** Other ROCm targets (gfx950, gfx90a, RDNA) keep today's behavior: a forced TRITON_MLA draft under DCP is rejected at startup. On gfx950, the default DSpark draft backend is ROCM_AITER_MLA, whose non-causal ASM decode kernels already declare DCP support, so TRITON_MLA is only an opt-in fallback there. The TRITON_MLA change is chip-independent: it repeats `seq_lens` and `block_table` rows for the same `decode_attention_fwd` kernel that already runs single-token DCP decode on those targets. Widening the gate should only need a GSM8K run at DCP 8 next to DCP 1 on the new target.

**Impact on other backends.**

- FlashInfer MLA and TokenSpeed MLA: no change. They already pass `supports_dcp_with_varlen=True`.
- ROCM_AITER_MLA: changes only for a non-causal group under DCP when none of its DCP verify routes is configured. In practice that is gfx950 with `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size != 1`, because every AITER DCP verify route needs interleave size 1, and AITER rejects non-causal groups on gfx942. By code reading, this config fails on main, because the threshold is clamped to 1:
  - With FULL cudagraphs, the draft capture hits the same `max_query_len <= reorder_batch_threshold` assert as TRITON_MLA.
  - Without FULL cudagraphs, `_mtp_decode_qlen = 1` closes the persistent-schedule gate in `_build_decode`. The schedule is what carries the non-causal mask, and the builder's own comment says a closed gate makes AITER raise a `KeyError` mid-run.

With this PR, the group keeps `1 + num_speculative_tokens`, which is consistent with the capability AITER already declares. 
- Builders without the flag: no change.

**Other drafters.** Backend selection does not check the speculative method, but only K3 DSpark builds non-causal MLA layers today. `K3DSparkDecoderLayer` is the only place that passes `non_causal_multi_token_decode=True`. The other `DeepseekV2MLAAttention` users (`deepseek_eagle3`, `longcat_flash`) leave the default `False`. The other DSpark drafters do not build these layers: Qwen3, MuseSpark and Gemma4 DSpark are not MLA, and DeepSeek-V4 DSpark uses the sparse MLA backends. A future non-causal MLA drafter would get the same treatment, which is correct as long as its rows share one KV extent, which is what the flag means.

**Limitation.** The flag is evaluated per metadata builder. The draft's TRITON_MLA builder also builds metadata for the target's causal verify batches, and these are now classified as decode. Draft layers never run attention on that metadata: DSpark's context-KV precompute only writes KV. A future drafter that runs causal attention through the same builder under DCP would hit the `forward_mqa` assert above at runtime rather than produce wrong output.

This PR was created with help of AI. 

---

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Raise the bar for PR descriptions
commits.pr_body:
As discussed on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58672



## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

PR descriptions currently only ask for "test commands run and results", which leaves it unclear what evidence reviewers should expect for newly added tests. This was raised in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58672#issuecomment-6979106322, where disclosing the exact pytest summary including test time was called good practice.

This PR makes it explicit in the contributor-facing docs: for added tests, the PR description should include the exact pytest summary (with time) and the commit SHA the tests were run on.

## Claims

- `AGENTS.md` requires the reproducible pytest command and exact pytest summary line including time in AI-assisted PR descriptions.
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` Validation hint asks for the pytest summary (time of newly added and modified tests) and the commit SHA tested.
- `/pr-checklist` skill (§4.2) asks reviewers/authors to check that the commit SHA, test commands and pytest summary with time are disclosed for new tests.

Left to other PRs:
- [ ] N/A

## Validation

None.

## Details

Documentation-only change; no code paths are affected. The requirement is scoped to newly added tests to avoid adding burden to every PR.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Disagg][CI] Fix the NIXL cells broken by UCX 1.23's ROCm DMABUF default
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the DeepSeek-V3 NIXL cells (1P1D TP8, 1P1D EP8, 2P2D EP16; pull and push) on the CI image's stock UCX. Follow-up to #62007.

## Changes

- `cluster.sh`:
  - Set `UCX_ROCM_COPY_DMABUF=no`. UCX 1.23 turns on DMABUF registration for ROCm memory; with it TP8 runs out of memory and EP8/EP16 fail with HIP error 209.
  - Drop `tcp` and `lo` so KV cannot fall back to TCP, and list all ionic NICs in `UCX_NET_DEVICES`.
- `vllm_disagg.sh`: set `VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST` to the node's IP. It defaults to localhost, so decode handshakes with itself and every load silently recomputes.
- `pipeline-disagg.yaml`: run the EP8 and 2P2D EP16 cells at accuracy concurrency 32. At 1 the EP16 eval runs past the 105-minute limit. TP8 keeps the default of 1.

- `models.yaml`: fit Kimi-K3 2P2D EP16 in memory. At 0.75 the prefill KV cache goes negative, and without a sequence cap prefill fails its startup check (`num_cache_lines >= batch`). Prefill now runs at 0.82 with `--max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`; decode runs at 0.80 with `--max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 512`. gsm8k 0.9636 (1319 questions).

## Test plan

UCX environment (every node):

```bash
export UCX_TLS=rc_verbs,ud_verbs,self,rocm
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=ionic_0:1,ionic_1:1,ionic_2:1,ionic_3:1,ionic_4:1,ionic_5:1,ionic_6:1,ionic_7:1
export UCX_IB_GID_INDEX=1

export UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=yes
export UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y
export UCX_PROTO_EMULATION_ENABLE=n
export UCX_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL=inf
export UCX_UD_VERBS_RX_QUEUE_LEN=1024
export UCX_RCACHE_MAX_UNRELEASED=1024
export UCX_ROCM_COPY_DMABUF=no
export VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=$NODE_IP
```

KV config (`kv_consumer` on decode; push uses `"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector"`):

```bash
KV='{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX"],"kv_lease_duration":180}}'
```

TP8, prefill (port 8100) and decode (port 8200, `kv_consumer`):

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --host $NODE_IP --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, prefill:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --port 20005 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address $PREFILL_IP --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

EP8/DP8, decode: the same with `--data-parallel-address $DECODE_IP`, `--all2all-backend mori_low_latency`, no `--enforce-eager`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75` and `kv_consumer`.

EP16/DP16 side (2 nodes), master:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --port 20005 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address $MASTER_IP --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

The second node runs the same command with `--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 8` and the same `--kv-transfer-config`. A decode EP16 side uses `--all2all-backend mori_low_latency`, no `--enforce-eager` and `kv_consumer`.

Router (`--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` for TP8, `8` for EP):

```bash

  --prefill http://$PREFILL_IP:8100 --decode http://$DECODE_IP:8200 \
```

```bash
  --model_args model=DeepSeek-V3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True
```

## Results

GSM8K 5-shot exact_match on the image's UCX 1.23.0. With this PR every run had no failed transfers.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI][Test] Spawn the workers in the DSv4.1 mono merge AB test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #68027, `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-8]` fails on every attempt of `(MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics TP8` with `KeyError: (False, 6)` in the merge AB test hook ([build 103769](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103769#01a1ed5c-a890-4995-a3fe-c6317846e973), last green [build 103710](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103710#01a1ecad-2652-4294-b499-49fb8a435141)). This PR makes the merge AB case spawn its workers. Test only, no code change.

## Claims

Fixes `DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics TP8` on AMD (MI355).

## Validation

MI355X (TP8), `rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-75228b7e47631bd9`, base fd99b402af, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` as in CI.

`pytest -v -s "tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-8]" "tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py::test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-28]"`: 2 passed. On main, `[8-8]` fails with the same `KeyError: (False, 6)` as CI.

With the fix, the graph capture takes 1.48 GiB, as in the green CI runs; on main it takes 1.19 GiB, since the second capture never runs.

## Details

The merge AB patches are applied when the module is imported with `DSV41_MONO_MERGE_AB` set. Before #68027, the pytest process loaded AITER at import and initialized HIP, so vLLM switched the workers to spawn, and they imported the module with the variable set. Since #68027 the workers are forked and keep the pytest process's import, made without it, so `_patch_merge_ab()` never runs and `_draft_out` stays empty. Setting `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` for this case restores the old behavior without relying on that side effect.

The job did not run between builds 103737 and 103769, so the failure first showed on #67906, which is unrelated.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Entrypoint] Use tri-state for add_special_tokens in pooling entrypoint.
commits.pr_body:
## TL;DR: 
For add_special_tokens:
• Completion Requests default to default_cmpl_tok_params (which reads from mm_processor.info.default_tok_params for multimodal models, or defaults to True otherwise).
• Chat Requests default to False. 

## Overview

Use tri-state for add_special_tokens in pooling entrypoint, (True/False/None), where None falls back to the default behavior.

Part of #67180

## Claims

1. Currently, add_special_tokens in the pooling entrypoint is of type bool. While we default it to True for CompletionRequest, 

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c80c3a6aa0201d1b4f71915f90c03fd64837cec/vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/protocol.py#L212-L225


2. the renderer reads mm_processor.info.default_tok_params for multimodal models, which might evaluate to False. 


https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c80c3a6aa0201d1b4f71915f90c03fd64837cec/vllm/renderers/base.py#L537-L550


**In the case of multimodal inputs, both default_cmpl_tok_params and default_chat_tok_params fall back to mm_processor.info.default_tok_params. Currently, the entrypoint test suite assumes that cmpl_tok_params and chat_tok_params are distinct.**

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fd99b402afea698d2e4752c5502d8eac9088765d/vllm/renderers/base.py#L537-L565


PTAL #66417  #66417


3. Therefore, add_special_tokens needs to support a tri-state (True/False/None), where None falls back to the default behavior.

Unlike `CompletionRequestMixin` where `None` falls back to the model/tokenizer default in `default_tok_params`, chat templates generally add special tokens during rendering, so resolve `None` to `False` for the chat path.



## Validation

pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/

## Details

 Since TokenizeParams strictly requires add_special_tokens to be a bool, this PR refactors `build_tok_params` and `_build_pooling_tok_params` to accept `default_tok_params` and derive the request-level `TokenizeParams` from it.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] [Rust Frontend] Fix HTTP metrics for streaming and cancelled requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview


Fix Rust frontend HTTP metrics so streaming latency includes the complete response-body lifetime and cancelled requests are not omitted.

This prevents HTTP request volume and latency from being understated for streaming workloads.



## Claims

- Record HTTP request counts and durations when the response body completes or is dropped.
- Preserve existing metric names, labels, excluded routes, response status codes, and body behavior.
- Add regression coverage for SSE response lifetimes and pre-response cancellation.



## Validation

```
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server  --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast

cargo clippy  --workspace --all-targets --all-features  --locked  --  -D warnings
```



## Details

The middleware previously recorded metrics immediately after next.run(req).await. For streaming responses, that future completes when the response headers and body object are ready, before the body emits generated tokens. Cancellation before that future completed also skipped all metric recording.

The metrics state is now held by a guard created before invoking the handler. After a response is available, the guard is moved into a transparent response-body wrapper. Dropping the request future or response body records the request count and elapsed duration exactly once.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview Include `"finish_reason": null` in non-final streaming chat completion choices from the Rust frontend, matching the Python frontend. Related to #63656. This PR addresses only the `finish_reason` difference. ## Claims - Include an explicit null `finish_reason` in non-final choices. - Preserve the final finish reason and the `[DONE]` stream terminator. - Extend the existing route regression test and document the behavior. ## Validation The explicit-null regression assertion failed before the fix: `left: None`, `right: Some(Null)`. It passes with the fix. Commands run from `rust/`: - `cargo test -p vllm-server stream_without_include_usage_keeps_existing_shape -- --nocapture` — passed. - `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib` — 509 passed, 0 failed. - `cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed. - `cargo fmt -p vllm-server` — completed. Applicable pre-commit checks on the three changed files and `git diff --check` also passed. Validation exercises the HTTP route and SSE serialization using a scripted engine. No real-model evaluation was performed. ## Details `#[serde_with::skip_serializing_none]` omits `finish_reason` when its value is `None`. Adding `#[serialize_always]` to this field preserves it as JSON null, while retaining the existing omission behavior for other optional fields. The regression test checks every non-final choice for the presence of `finish_reason` with an explicit null value. It also checks the final `"stop"` reason, absence of usage when not requested, and the `[DONE]` terminator. Other streaming differences described in #63656 remain outside this PR. commits.pr_title: fix(security): default multimodal item limit to 999 for unconfigured modalities
commits.pr_body:
The Rust frontend treated modalities absent from --limit-mm-per-prompt as unlimited, diverging from Python's default of 999. This allowed a single request within the 32 MiB body limit to trigger unbounded media-task fan-out and OOM before inference.

Apply a DEFAULT_MM_ITEMS_PER_PROMPT of 999 as a fallback when no explicit count is configured, matching the Python frontend behavior and blocking the demonstrated pre-inference allocation path.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][GDN] Export Triton and AITER FlyDSL prefill checkpoints on ROCm
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let the Qwen GDN prefill (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen4Exp, Intern-S2 Mobius) export align-mode prefill checkpoints on ROCm, for both the Triton backend and the AITER FlyDSL default on MI3xx. With prefix caching on, a prompt is then no longer split at its last Mamba block boundary.

- Triton: #65186 added the checkpoint store to the Triton chunk recurrence but limited it to CUDA because it was validated only there; nothing on the path is CUDA-specific.
- AITER FlyDSL returns only the final state, so it cannot store a checkpoint. A FlyDSL step that carries a checkpoint now runs the Triton/FLA prefill, which stores it in-loop; steps without one stay on FlyDSL.

Follow-up to #65186. #60659 adds FlyDSL checkpoints a different way: it cuts each row at the checkpoint and runs FlyDSL a second time on the tails. Both were measured on MI355X (below); at the default block size they perform the same, and this approach is +13 / −4 lines instead of ~300. Thanks to yuttian1 for #60659, credited as co-author.

## Claims

- In align mode, `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` on ROCm and the AITER FlyDSL backend declare checkpoint alignment 64, as Triton does on CUDA. FlashInfer, CuteDSL, HIP and XPU are unchanged.
- The kernel (`chunk_delta_h.py`) and the layer path (`_forward_triton_prefill_with_checkpoints`, the warmup, the buffer reservation) are platform-neutral. The same Triton checkpoint kernel already runs on ROCm for GLM-5.3-Flash (#67866).
- Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B FP8 on MI355X, default FlyDSL backend: TTFT −41% / −62% / −66% at concurrency 1 / 4 / 8.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py
# 4 passed
pytest "tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2" \
       "tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py::test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2_async"
# 2 passed
```

The e2e tests run with `gdn_prefill_backend=triton` in align mode and pass their prefix-hit, unsplit-prefill and checkpoint-state checks (one-layer dummy weights). The FlyDSL handoff also passes the sync / async correctness runs on MI355X.

Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B FP8, 1x MI355X, TP1, default (FlyDSL) prefill backend, `--enable-prefix-caching` (align mode), no spec decode, ISL 8000 / OSL 64, 16 fresh prompts per point, two server launches per arm. The baseline is this PR's first commit, whose FlyDSL path is the same as main (no checkpoint, so the prompt is split). All 288 timed requests succeeded.

| `--block-size 64`, concurrency | TTFT ms, baseline | this PR (R1 / R2) | #60659 rebased (R1 / R2) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 235.75 | 135.03 / 141.99 | 132.57 / 130.73 |
| 4 | 938.31 | 332.66 / 374.75 | 328.43 / 327.09 |
| 8 | 1576.88 | 531.03 / 540.66 | 517.11 / 515.74 |

Output tok/s, baseline → this PR / #60659: 61.99 → 68.36 / 68.82 at concurrency 1, 133.54 → 186.73 / 189.18 at 4, 149.20 → 255.20 / 260.07 at 8.

At block size 64 the tail #60659 reruns is under 64 tokens, which favors it (TTFT 4–8% lower than this PR). With the default block size (576 / 544 for the two branches, from their different cache layouts) the two are within noise:

| default block size, concurrency | TTFT ms, this PR | #60659 rebased | output tok/s, this PR | #60659 rebased |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 133.72 | 132.36 | 68.73 | 68.07 |
| 4 | 334.08 | 329.36 | 186.91 | 187.37 |

This PR's two ROCm backends at head `2ea94889de`, same setup (default block size, one round of 16 prompts per point, all 96 timed requests succeeded):

| concurrency | TTFT ms, FlyDSL | Triton | output tok/s, FlyDSL | Triton |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 134.90 | 131.89 | 68.60 | 68.76 |
| 4 | 330.92 | 329.89 | 187.43 | 187.23 |
| 8 | 528.94 | 528.89 | 255.74 | 256.35 |

They match because with 8000-token prompts nearly every FlyDSL prefill step carries a checkpoint and so runs Triton.

gsm8k on MI355X, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, raw completions, temperature 0, one run per arm. With 5 shots the shared few-shot prefix crosses a Mamba block boundary, so the PR arms resume from stored checkpoints (42,400 more prefix-hit tokens than the baseline):

| arm | accuracy | prefix-hit tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| baseline (FlyDSL) | 0.8666 | 720,800 |
| this PR, FlyDSL | 0.8643 | 763,200 |
| this PR, Triton | 0.8666 | 763,200 |

FlyDSL differs from the baseline by 3 questions. No arm had empty answers or extraction failures.

CI already covers the Triton path on AMD:
- `:amd: (MI355) FLA Ops Kernels` runs `tests/kernels/fla`, including the Triton checkpoint correctness test from #65186.
- `:amd: (MI355 DPX) E2E Core Large Memory` runs `test_mamba_prefix_cache_mrv2` and `_mrv2_async` with `gdn_prefill_backend=triton`. This PR updates their expectation so that on ROCm they check the unsplit step pattern with the checkpoint saved, as on CUDA.

## Details

- With FlyDSL, a step that carries a checkpoint runs the Triton kernel for the whole step, which is slower per token than FlyDSL. With long prompts nearly every prefill step carries one; the measurements above include that cost.
- FlyDSL now reserves the same per-sequence checkpoint buffer as Triton (`max_num_seqs × local heads × 128 × 128` in the state dtype) from the shared workspace, and the builder also builds FLA's chunk metadata for checkpoint steps.
- gfx1151 defaults to HIP, which is unchanged.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation and the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Serve gpt-oss when vllm serve omits the parser flags
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b` and no parser flags, every `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions` request fails with a 500: "gpt_oss uses native Harmony output parsing; generic tool parser override `none` is not supported". Since #46359, `vllm serve` passes `none` for omitted parser flags, and the Harmony output processor only accepts `auto`, so the plain command can't serve gpt-oss at all. This PR accepts `none` there as well, like the Python frontend, which ignores the parser flags for gpt-oss. Part of #66989.

## Claims

- gpt-oss served through `vllm serve` with the Rust frontend and no parser flags now answers `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions`, including tool calls. On `/v1/responses` the output items match the Python frontend's.
- An explicit generic parser for gpt-oss (e.g. `--reasoning-parser qwen3`) is still rejected, as before.
- Non-Harmony models are unaffected: only the Harmony override check changes.

## Validation

H100 MIG 1g.24gb, `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (MXFP4) with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 4096` and no parser flags, greedy, seed 0. "Before" and "after" are local `vllm-rs` builds at `0a37f464da` without and with this change; nothing under `rust/src/chat` or `rust/src/cmd` changed between that commit and this PR's base. Rust checks ran on macOS.

**Repro** (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b`, then one request each):

| request | before | after | Python frontend |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/responses` text, `max_output_tokens: 64` | 500 | `incomplete`, reasoning + message | `incomplete`, reasoning + message |
| `/v1/responses` + one function tool | 500 | `completed`, reasoning + `function_call`, arguments parse | same |
| same, streamed | 500 | `completed`, reasoning + `function_call` | same |
| `/v1/chat/completions` text | 500 | `length`, content `"Blue"`, 64 tokens | `length`, content `"Blue"`, 64 tokens |
| `/v1/chat/completions` + one function tool | 500 | `tool_calls`, one call, arguments parse | `stop`, no tool call |

Every "before" 500 is ``gpt_oss uses native Harmony output parsing; generic tool parser override `none` is not supported``. The last row differs from Python: the Rust frontend returns the call, while the Python frontend answered without one for this request; I didn't chase that Python-side difference here. Token counts on the reasoning-heavy requests vary between runs even with greedy decoding, so the table compares structure.

Controls on the "after" build:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| gpt-oss with an explicit `--reasoning-parser qwen3` | still 500, ``generic reasoning parser override `qwen3` is not supported`` |
| Qwen3-0.6B, no parser flags, 5 requests, before vs after | byte-identical |

**Tests.** The updated unit test fails before this change and passes after:

```
# before (fix reverted, new test kept):
cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib --locked output::harmony::tests
  -> FAILED: allows_auto_and_omitted_selections; 12 passed, 1 failed
# after:
cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib --locked output::harmony::tests        -> 13 passed
cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib --locked -- --test-threads=1           -> 468 passed
cargo fmt -p vllm-chat -- --check                                    -> clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings -> clean
```

<details>
<summary>Local environment notes</summary>

In a parallel `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` run, `multimodal::audio::tests::audio_pipeline_attributes_stage_timings_to_request` fails here on both runs I did; it passes alone and in a serial run (468/468), so it's a timing-sensitive test unrelated to this change.

</details>

No model eval: the Harmony output processor and the model path are unchanged; only which parser selections the Harmony check accepts changes.

## Details

**Root cause.** `validate_harmony_parser_overrides` (`rust/src/chat/src/output/harmony/mod.rs`, from the move in #43283) accepts only `auto`, so that a generic parser override fails instead of being silently ignored. At the time, `none` could only come from an explicit `--*-parser none`. #46359 then made the Python-supervised bootstrap deserialize omitted `tool_call_parser` / `reasoning_parser` to `none`, to match Python's "no parser unless one is given" semantics. For gpt-oss that turned the default into a rejected override. Under `vllm serve`, `none` always means the flag was omitted: Python only forwards parser names it validated, and `none` isn't one.

**Change.** Accept `ParserSelection::None` next to `Auto` in `validate_harmony_override`, and say why in the doc comment. In the tests, the reasoning case of `rejects_generic_parser_overrides` now uses an explicit `qwen3` instead of `none`, and `allows_auto_auto_only` becomes `allows_auto_and_omitted_selections`, which also covers `none`.

**Tradeoff.** With the standalone `vllm-rs serve` CLI, an explicit `--reasoning-parser none` for gpt-oss is now accepted too, and Harmony parsing still applies. That matches Python, which ignores the parser flags for gpt-oss. If you'd rather keep rejecting the explicit form, the bootstrap config could carry "omitted" separately from `none`; happy to switch to that.

**Out of scope.** The documented `--tool-call-parser openai` still fails at startup, because the Rust frontend registers no `openai` tool parser (#66989, first case). The roadmap leaves parser names to maintainers, so I didn't touch it. With this change the plain `vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b` works.

**Limitations.** Real-checkpoint runs used gpt-oss-20b only. CI runs the unit tests, but no CI step serves gpt-oss on the Rust frontend yet (#66781 leaves the Harmony Responses tests out), so the table above is the end-to-end check. While validating, one plain-text `/v1/responses` request that hit `max_output_tokens` mid-message returned a 500, `harmony output parsing failed: Unexpected EOS while waiting for message header to complete`, where Python returns `incomplete` (it handles a Harmony stream that ends mid-message since #47062). It didn't reproduce in a rerun at 16, 64, 256 and 1000 tokens, so it depends on where the cut lands. The Harmony output processor itself is unchanged here, and the standalone `vllm-rs serve`, whose defaults are already `auto`, runs the same path, so this is a separate, pre-existing gap that this PR only makes reachable from `vllm serve`. It needs its own fix and isn't part of this PR.

**Relation to other PRs.** I found no PR for this. #64069 warns at startup when `auto` can't resolve a tool parser and skips gpt-oss; #63580 maps `ParserDisabled` to a 400 for non-Harmony tool requests; #58414 changes Harmony detection on the Python side.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Constrain to a single tool call when parallel_tool_calls is false
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On the Rust frontend, a request with `tools`, `tool_choice: "auto"` and `parallel_tool_calls: false` is not held to one call: the model emits several and the extras are dropped after parsing. That wastes tokens on calls that get thrown away, and the second call can be truncated when `max_tokens` lands inside it. This PR constrains the grammar to a single call in that case, as the Python frontend does (#50502).

## Claims

- On the Rust frontend, `tool_choice: "auto"` + non-strict tools + `parallel_tool_calls: false` now builds a tool grammar capped at one call, on both `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions`. `auto` still allows a plain-text answer.
- With `parallel_tool_calls` unset or `true`, nothing changes: the request stays grammar-free and byte-identical to before.
- No new grammar machinery: `tool_grammar_applies` just returns `true` for this shape, and the builder's existing `stop_after_first` (driven by `parallel_tool_calls`) does the rest.

## Validation

H100 MIG 1g.24gb, Qwen3-0.6B, `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, greedy, seed 0. "Before" and "after" are local `vllm-rs` builds at `0a37f464da` without and with this change; nothing under `rust/src/parser` changed between that commit and this PR's base `bafa5c6c30`. Rust checks ran on macOS on the rebased branch.

**Repro** (prompt "What's the weather in Paris and in Tokyo?", one `get_weather` tool, `parallel_tool_calls: false`):

| surface | before | after | Python frontend |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/responses` | `function_call` + a stray `"\n"` message item; 53 tokens | one `function_call`, no message item; 26 tokens | one `function_call`; 26 tokens |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | one `tool_call`, `content: "\n"`; 53 tokens | one `tool_call`, `content: null`; 26 tokens | one `tool_call`, `content: null`; 26 tokens |

After the change the Rust output matches Python exactly: one call, 26 tokens, no stray whitespace item.

Controls, byte-identical before and after:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `parallel_tool_calls` unset (default true), both surfaces | 2 calls + `"\n"`, 53 tokens | 2 calls + `"\n"`, 53 tokens |
| `tool_choice: required` / single-tool `auto` | 1 call, 20 tokens | 1 call, 20 tokens |

(The default-true path is untouched, including the `"\n"` item, which is #63917 item 5.)

**Tests.** A new unit test fails before this change and passes after:

```
# before (fix reverted):
cargo test -p vllm-parser --lib output_grammar::tests
  -> FAILED: parallel_tool_calls_false_constrains_auto_to_one_call
     ("auto grammar limited to one call"); 6 passed, 1 failed
# after:
cargo test -p vllm-parser --lib output_grammar::tests -> 7 passed
cargo test -p vllm-parser --locked                     -> 638 passed
cargo fmt -p vllm-parser -- --check                    -> clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings -> clean
```

No model eval: this changes grammar selection, not the sampler or logits; only a `parallel_tool_calls: false` + `auto` request gets a different (one-call) grammar, and the before/after above covers it. The constrained request is also cheaper: it compiles the same grammar `required` already builds, then generates fewer tokens instead of making two calls and dropping one.

## Details

**Root cause.** `tool_grammar_applies` (`rust/src/parser/src/output_grammar.rs`) returned `false` for `tool_choice: "auto"` unless a tool is strict, the server strict level is `function`+, or the request carries an answer format. A single-call request is none of those, so no grammar was built and `stop_after_first` had nothing to act on. The frontend then leaned on `max_tool_calls() == Some(1)` dropping the extra calls after parsing. That gives the right output, but only after the model spent tokens on calls that are discarded, with a truncation risk if `max_tokens` lands inside the second call.

**Change.** Add `|| !ctx.parallel_tool_calls` to the `Auto` arm of `tool_grammar_applies`, so a single-call `auto` request builds the tool grammar; the builder's existing `with_parallel_tool_calls` / `stop_after_first` caps it at one. One line and a comment, with no change to grammar construction or any other tool-choice arm.

**Why here.** The grammar decision belongs in `vllm-parser`'s `output_grammar`, next to the rest of `tool_grammar_applies`. The Python frontend makes the same call in `DelegatingParser._apply_structural_tag`, raising the strict level to `FUNCTION` for a single-call request (#50502). Some Rust builders already honor `parallel_tool_calls` directly (e.g. Kimi K3 `grammar.rs`); this fixes the generic path.

**Relation to other PRs.** Not a duplicate. #50502 is the Python-side fix and #59298 added the Python Responses post-parse filter; the only visible symptom today, a `"\n"` between dropped calls, is tracked as #63917 item 5. This PR is the missing grammar constraint, not that whitespace. I found no open Rust PR for it. #60815 (draft) edits the comment on the same `Auto` arm for `--always-constrain-output` but doesn't change how `parallel_tool_calls` is handled.

**Limitations.** Real-checkpoint runs used Qwen3-0.6B; the grammar decision itself is covered by the unit test. Not run on ROCm.

commits.pr_title: [Tests] Reuse single-rank parallel groups for faster GPU unit tests
commits.pr_body:
PR co-author: Tomas Ruiz @tomasruizt

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

Single-GPU layer tests do not need real distributed process groups when parallelism is irrelevant. A single-rank stand-in avoids the initialization and teardown overhead of `dist_init` when tests only need rank metadata; targeted cleanup skips further reduce unit-test runtime.

This PR extracts the existing shared-expert single-rank stand-in into `tests/single_rank_group.py` and reuses it in quantization, shared-expert, routing, expert-substitution and zero-expert tests instead of `dist_init` and individual TP rank/world-size patches. Its generator-aware decorator also supports yielding fixtures. Eligible unit tests use `skip_global_cleanup` to avoid redundant teardown.

Extracted from #67529 as a standalone PR. Searches for open single-rank/faster-parallel-test PRs found no other matching implementation. There are no production-code or user-visible behavior changes.

## Claims

- `SingleRankGroup` supplies rank 0, world size 1 and identity collectives without FileStore/backend or model-parallel group initialization. The context/decorator restores all eight groups on return or exception; yielding fixtures retain the override through teardown, with signatures preserved for pytest.
- Adoption only adds decorators/cleanup marks and removes obsolete single-rank setup. Test bodies, assertions, tolerances and platform skips are otherwise unchanged; TP>1 simulation patches remain intact.
- Eligible tests skip redundant global teardown without rewriting their existing cleanup implementations. The online FSE module retains its original cleanup, and the MoE hook recognizes decorated tests to preserve clean-entry isolation.
- The full PR is approximately 2.6× faster than the pinned main baseline on the measured selection (487.79 s → 190.87 s), with 301 passed and 63 skipped in all three configurations. Most of the gain is teardown: `dist_init` runs `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` (a full `gc.collect()`) on top of the autouse cleanup, so main pays it twice per test; the decorators remove one and `skip_global_cleanup` the other (example in Details).
- Quantization CUDA/ROCm, CUDA Quantized Models, AMD model-executor and MoE CUDA/ROCm CI jobs list the helper in `source_file_dependencies`.

Left to other PRs:
- [ ] CUDA/XPU timing and multi-rank validation are not measured here; this change targets single-rank unit-test setup, not distributed correctness.

## Validation

Unit tests ran on AMD Instinct MI355X, ROCm/torch HIP 7.15.26333, AMD clang 23.0.0git, with matching runtime dependencies and the same selection below. Main is pinned to the branch's base commit. Both PR rows tested ad4f2308116f966b9a8c8bfe3ed78c66929854c0; the middle row re-enables teardown only for newly marked tests, preserving pre-existing cleanup skips and MoE clean-entry checks.

```bash
pytest -s -vvvvv \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_nvfp4_weight_only_linear_matches_dequantized_weight \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_moe_stages_quantized_weights_for_humming \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_prequantized_compatibility \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_block_fp8_requantization_removes_source_scales \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_ignore_keeps_checkpoint_quantization_linear \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_quantization_configures_prequantized_moe \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_weight_loading_requantization_moe \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_requantized_moe_reload \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_quantization \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_quantization_targets \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_quantization_records_global_config \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py::test_models_fse_init \
  tests/quantization/test_fp8_dequant.py \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4_embedding.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py::test_online_mxfp4_moe_matches_quark \
  tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py::test_online_mxfp4_dense_matches_quark \
  tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_weight_loading_requantization \
  tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_requantized_moe_padding \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py::test_online_mxfp4_shared_expert_fse_compares_resolved_keys \
  tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py \
  tests/quantization/test_input_hadamard.py::test_online_mxfp4_hadamard \
  tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_deepseek_v41_mxfp8_scale_loading \
  tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_fp8_reloading \

  tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py::test_pluggable_router_preserves_model_bias_loading \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routing_simulator.py::test_simulated_bias_is_nonpersistent_buffer \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_expert_substitution.py::test_standard_fused_moe_model_discovers_substitution \
```
