```bash
  tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py::test_hash_routing_backend_selection \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py::test_hash_routing_rejects_monolithic_without_support \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py::test_aiter_w4a16_expert_parallel_selection
```

| Configuration | Tested SHA | Passed | Skipped | Setup | Body | Teardown | Total |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9 | 301 | 63 | 31.05 s | 118.69 s | 335.56 s | 487.79 s |
| This PR, no additional `skip_global_cleanup` | ad4f2308116f966b9a8c8bfe3ed78c66929854c0 | 301 | 63 | 29.27 s | 109.80 s | 210.61 s | 352.25 s |
| This PR, single-rank decorators and additional `skip_global_cleanup` | ad4f2308116f966b9a8c8bfe3ed78c66929854c0 | 301 | 63 | 27.55 s | 111.88 s | 49.01 s | 190.87 s |

Setup, body and teardown are summed pytest phase durations; Total is the pytest elapsed time (it also covers collection and session overhead). The three configurations ran one after another on the same device, once each; these timings are noisy and not a general performance guarantee. Direct helper checks also passed collective identity and nested/decorator exception restoration without initializing `torch.distributed`.

## Details

The stand-in was already present in the shared-expert tests:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9/tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py#L1327-L1416

Example, `tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_quantization_targets[linear_regex]` (unchanged body), median of 7 runs per configuration:

| Configuration | Setup | Body | Teardown | Total | `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` calls |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | 323 ms | 348 ms | 850 ms | 1513 ms | 2 |
| This PR, no additional `skip_global_cleanup` | 17 ms | 350 ms | 403 ms | 771 ms | 1 |
| This PR, single-rank decorators and additional `skip_global_cleanup` | 3 ms | 360 ms | 2 ms | 365 ms | 0 |

On main the test pays the cleanup twice: the `dist_init` fixture calls `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` after its `yield`:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9/tests/conftest.py#L225-L250
and the autouse `cleanup_fixture` calls it again unless `skip_global_cleanup` is set:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa6c77f5954ef22e705cd82456cc731ba67d0ae9/tests/conftest.py#L275-L279
Each call is dominated by a full `gc.collect()` (~0.4 s over ~1M live objects), while the `dist_init` setup itself is cheap once warm. The decorators remove the first call; `skip_global_cleanup` removes the second.

The aggregate gain from the decorators alone is smaller than this example suggests: only 131 of the 301 passed tests used `dist_init` on main (113 already used a fake group, 57 need neither), and run-to-run variation is large. An earlier run on a different device measured 339 s on main versus 336–363 s without the additional cleanup skips, i.e. within noise, whereas the cleanup skips gave a consistent ~2.5×.

This is deliberately test-only and does not emulate real communication or asynchronous collectives. An attempted module-wide cleanup skip in the online FSE suite caused its checkpoint-weight equality test to fail, so that module retains its original cleanup policy. No AITER finalizer rewrite or assertion changes are included.

commits.pr_title: [Model Loader] Direct reload reruns post-load processing on the cold-start modules (LoRA)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) reruns post-load processing (PWAL) over `model.named_modules()` as the model is at reload time. LoRA wraps layers after cold start (`ColumnParallelLinear` → `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, the original layer kept as `base_layer`), and the wrappers forward their base layer's `quant_method`. The rerun therefore visits both the wrapper and the base layer and processes the same weights twice, so direct reload refuses LoRA today.

Layerwise reload does not have this problem because it reruns processing only on modules recorded at cold start. This PR gives direct reload the same rule instead of special-casing LoRA.

Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477): LoRA is one of the setups F7 (removing layerwise reload) needs in direct mode, and one of the refusals #68041 carries.

## Change

- `record_checkpoint_layout` (cold start, right before PWAL) records `model._ckpt_modules`, the modules cold-start PWAL runs over.
- `process_weights_after_loading` iterates `_ckpt_modules` when recorded, else `named_modules()`. At cold start both are the same list; on a reload, modules added after cold start are left out. A LoRA base layer is the same object under its wrapper, so it is still processed once.
- Drop the LoRA refusal from `VllmConfig._verify_direct_reload_compat`.
- `test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe` runs in both reload modes.

LoRA adapter weights are not touched by a reload; only base weights are updated, as with layerwise reload.

## Validation

GB200, nightly image with this tree's Python files overlaid: `test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe[layerwise]`, `test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe[direct]` (Qwen3-30B-A3B w4a16 with a LoRA adapter, prompt logprobs before and after a reload match, with and without the adapter), `test_direct_reload.py`, `test_reload_lifecycle.py`: 50 passed.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Serve the scale-out render routes on the main server
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--enable-scale-out`, Python serves `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/completions/render` next to `/inference/v1/generate`. The Rust main server answered them with a 501 placeholder (#62432); only the engine-free `vllm-rs render` server rendered them. This PR serves both routes on the main server by reusing the render handlers through `RenderContext`, the trait #65994 added so the gRPC Render service runs on both servers.

Fixes #55994. Supersedes #65180 by @vineoy, credited as co-author: same feature, rebuilt on `RenderContext`, which landed after it was opened.

## Claims

- With `--enable-scale-out`, the main server renders chat and completions requests into `GenerateRequest`s with the processors it already holds for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`. No second model load. The output is the same as the standalone render server's, and its `max_tokens` check uses the engine's `max_model_len`.
- The requested model resolves against the loaded LoRA adapters, like `/inference/v1/generate`. An unknown model returns 404.
- Without `--enable-scale-out`, both routes answer 403, like the other scale-out routes. Messages and Responses render, derender, and abort keep their placeholders.
- Render no longer rejects `n` above `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES`. Render only copies `n` into the request it returns, and `/inference/v1/generate`, which fans out the samples, already rejects it. This applies to both servers and removes the hidden `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` binding from `vllm-rs render`.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd`: 814 passed; `cargo clippy -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --all-targets` is clean.
- New tests:
  - `scale_out_render_routes_follow_scale_out_gate`: the two routes render on the main server, and the engine window bounds `max_tokens`. With scale-out off, both return 403.
  - `scale_out_render_accepts_loaded_lora_adapter`: a loaded adapter renders and an unknown model returns 404.
  - Both fail before the change: the first against the 501 placeholders, the second when the main server resolves only base model names.
- `n_limit_follows_max_n_sequences_option`: its render part now renders `n = 3` on both routes with the limit at 2, then posts each result to `/inference/v1/generate`, which returns the `n` 400.
- Live run: `vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-scale-out` against `vllm-mock-engine`. Both routes rendered, and each rendered request ran on `/inference/v1/generate` unchanged; a chat render with `n = 2` came back with 2 choices. An unknown model returned 404, render passed `n = 20000` through, and generate rejected it with the `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` 400. Without `--enable-scale-out`, both routes returned 403.

  <details><summary>Chat render, decoded prompt, and generate</summary>

  ```
  $ curl -s $B/v1/chat/completions/render -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"max_completion_tokens":8,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false},"n":2}'
  {"request_id":"chatcmpl-45c1d6bc","model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","token_ids_len":13,"sampling_params":{"n":2,"max_tokens":8},"reasoning_parser_kwargs":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}}   # summarized with jq
  $ curl -s $B/detokenize -d '{"tokens": <token_ids>}' | jq -r .prompt
  <|im_start|>user
  Hello<|im_end|>
  <|im_start|>assistant
  <think>

  </think>

  $ curl -s $B/inference/v1/generate -d @chat_render.json   # summarized with jq
  {"choices":2,"finish":["length","length"]}
  ```

  </details>

## Details

- **One trait for both servers.** `RenderContext` moves next to `RenderState` (pure move, first commit). Its `is_served_model(&str) -> bool` becomes `resolve_model(Option<&str>) -> LoraModelResolution`, because HTTP lowering needs the resolution, not just a yes or no. The gRPC model check uses the same resolution. The HTTP handlers become generic over `RenderContext` and are mounted on both routers.
- **Scale-out gate.** The implemented scale-out routes are one `(path, handler)` table, so a route is either its handler or 403.
- **Divergence from Python.** Python's render also rejects `n > VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES`, but only because building `SamplingParams` runs that check. Render fans out nothing, and the generate request it returns is checked when it is submitted.
- Not covered here: `parse_context` on the render output (`output_mode: "derender"`) is not implemented by either Rust render server yet.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Pass multimodal embeddings to NemotronH MTP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Pass the target model's image and audio embeddings into the Nemotron-H MTP drafter, so it receives the same inputs as `Nemotron3_5TranscribeMTP` and the multimodal Eagle drafters. This is a consistency change: end-to-end runs show no measurable change in acceptance length or output quality. Closes #68152.

## Claims

- `NemotronHMTP` now implements `SupportsMultiModalEmbeddings` and merges external embeddings in `embed_input_ids`.
- On a multimodal target, `DraftModelSpeculator` passes those embeddings to the drafter instead of logging the text-only fallback.
- A text-only target still drafts from text embeddings, because the speculator enables this path only when the target also supports multimodal inputs.

## Validation

The new tests fail on the parent of this commit and pass with it.

Without this change:

```text
FAILED test_draft_model_multimodal_embedding_capability[NemotronHMTP-True]
AssertionError: assert False is True
  where False = supports_multimodal_embeddings(NemotronHMTP)

FAILED test_nemotron_h_mtp_merges_multimodal_embeddings
AttributeError: type object 'NemotronHMTP' has no attribute 'embed_input_ids'
```

With this change:

```text
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py::test_draft_model_multimodal_embedding_capability tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py::test_nemotron_h_mtp_merges_multimodal_embeddings tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py::test_mm_capable_drafter_merges_multimodal_embeddings
9 passed
```

The merge test checks three cases: text ids stay on the embedding table, two multimodal positions are replaced by the supplied embeddings, and embeddings without `is_multimodal` raise `ValueError`.

### End-to-end server check

`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b` (NVFP4) on B300, MTP with 3 speculative tokens. The baseline is the precompiled wheel for this PR's base commit `c84273be3`; the PR is an editable install of this branch on the same wheel. Both servers use identical serve flags, one GPU each, with greedy sequential requests. AL is computed per request from the spec-decode counters (`1 + accepted / num_drafts`).

| Workload | Base AL | PR AL | Paired diff (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image: 24 real photos × 4 prompts (96 requests) | 3.112 | 3.118 | +0.005 [−0.013, +0.023] |
| Image-heavy: 6 photos per request, ~2.7k prompt tokens (36 requests) | 3.115 | 3.103 | −0.012 [−0.042, +0.018] |
| Video: 6 clips × 5 prompts, 32 frames, ~4.1k prompt tokens (30 requests) | 3.303 | 3.316 | +0.016 [−0.045, +0.069] |
| Text only (24 requests) | 3.120 | 3.110 | −0.018 [−0.073, +0.033] |

- The baseline logs `Draft model NemotronHMTP does not support external multimodal embeddings ... using text-only draft inputs`. With this PR the warning is gone, and the server logs no errors.
- Per-position acceptance is unchanged (about 0.86 / 0.71 / 0.55).
- First draft after prefill only (`max_tokens=2`, thinking off, prompts whose first tokens depend on the image): AL is already 3.0–3.5 on the baseline for single image, multi-image, and video, and this PR does not change it beyond noise.
- AL is unaffected on every workload. The MTP input is `eh_proj(cat(enorm(embed), hnorm(target_hidden)))`; without this PR only the embedding half is a placeholder at multimodal positions, and the target hidden state already carries the image or audio context.

`tests/v1/worker` is already selected by the V1 Executor + Worker CI step.

## Details

`DraftModelSpeculator.load_model` sets `supports_mm_inputs` only when both the target supports multimodal inputs and `supports_multimodal_embeddings(draft_model)` is true. Otherwise it warns and drafts from text token embeddings. `NemotronHMTP` did not implement the interface, so every multimodal Nemotron-H target hit that fallback. `Nemotron3_5TranscribeMTP` already did; this change puts the same merge on the shared class.

The MTP block is trained on the target decoder's input stream, so passing the vision or audio embeddings at placeholder positions matches training and removes the text-only fallback warning. `TargetDependentARSpeculator._run_model` already calls `embed_input_ids` and forwards `inputs_embeds` when the flag is set. `NemotronHMultiTokenPredictor.forward` already prefers `inputs_embeds` over `input_ids`.

`Nemotron3_5TranscribeMTP.embed_input_ids` is left in place. It has the same merge and a different missing-mask error string.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Use the model's default temperature when a gRPC request omits it
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A gRPC `GenerateRequest` that omits `temperature` now samples at the model's default temperature, exactly as an HTTP request that omits it. Until now the gRPC server forced an omitted temperature to 0.0 (greedy), although `inference.proto` documented it as defaulting to the model-specific default and omitted `top_p`, `top_k` and `min_p` already inherited the model's values.

**Motivation.** [Dynamo](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo)'s vLLM sidecar serves OpenAI-style chat and completions requests through the gRPC API. It does not have access to the model's default temperature: neither `ServerInfo` nor `ModelInfo` reports it, and the sidecar should not re-derive it from `generation_config.json`, because vLLM's flags (`--generation-config vllm`, `--hf-config-path`, `--revision`) change the result. Because an omitted temperature means greedy over gRPC, the sidecar has to fill in 1.0 for every model when a user omits temperature. For Qwen3 that combines the model's `top_p` 0.95 and `top_k` 20 with temperature 1.0 instead of 0.6, so the output differs from `vllm serve` for the same request. With this change the sidecar can omit `temperature`, and vLLM resolves the model's default the same way the HTTP API does, instead of the client having to treat 1.0 as the default.

## Claims

- An omitted gRPC `temperature` resolves the same way as on the HTTP API: the model's generation-config temperature, or 1.0 if it sets none or the server runs with `--generation-config vllm`. For `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (generation config temperature 0.6, `top_p` 0.95, `top_k` 20) a gRPC request now samples at 0.6 with the model's `top_p` and `top_k`, instead of greedy.
- Explicit temperatures, including 0, are unchanged. HTTP behavior is unchanged.
- **Behavior change for gRPC clients:** a client that omitted `temperature` to get greedy decoding must now send `temperature: 0`.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (run from `rust/`):

- `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib grpc::`: 95 passed. New test `unary_generate_without_temperature_uses_model_default` sends a `GenerateRequest` without `temperature` to a backend whose generation config sets 0.6 and asserts that the engine-core request carries temperature 0.6. With the old `temperature.or(Some(0.0))` restored, it fails (`left: 0.0`, `right: 0.6`). The 1.0 fallback and `--generation-config vllm` are the HTTP path's shared lowering, already covered in `vllm-text`.
- Removed `unset_temperature_defaults_to_greedy`, which asserted the old default.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

**Live run** on 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` in the `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.34.0` image. Before: the image's own `vllm-rs`. After: `vllm-rs` built (debug) from `v0.34.0` with this PR's `build_sampling_params` change applied, mounted into the same image. No other patches. Temperature handling in `build_sampling_params` and `rust/src/text/src/lower.rs` is identical at `v0.34.0` and at the base of this PR; `build_sampling_params` differs only in structured-output decoding.

```bash
vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8151 --grpc-port 50151 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --max-model-len 4096
```

A Python client sent the same prompt with `seed=1234` and 48 max tokens through gRPC `Generate` (stubs generated from `rust/proto/inference.proto`, temperature omitted) and through HTTP `/v1/completions` with temperature omitted, 0.6, 1.0 and 0, then compared the generated text. Prompt: `"Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper who finds a message in a bottle."`

```text
=== before (v0.34.0)
grpc omitted == http temperature omitted: False
grpc omitted == http temperature=0.6: False
grpc omitted == http temperature=1.0: False
grpc omitted == http temperature=0 (greedy): True
=== after (v0.34.0 + this change)
grpc omitted == http temperature omitted: True
grpc omitted == http temperature=0.6: True
grpc omitted == http temperature=1.0: False
grpc omitted == http temperature=0 (greedy): False
```

<details>
<summary>Generated text</summary>

```text
=== before (v0.34.0)
grpc temperature omitted: " The story should include the following elements: the lighthouse keeper's name, the bottle, the message, and the lighthouse's location. The story should be in the first person. The story should be around 500 words."
http temperature omitted: " The message is in the form of a riddle. The riddle is a cryptic message that leads to the story's resolution. The story should include a character named Sam, who is a lighthouse keeper in a coastal town. The"
http temperature=0.6: " The message is in the form of a riddle. The riddle is a cryptic message that leads to the story's resolution. The story should include a character named Sam, who is a lighthouse keeper in a coastal town. The"
http temperature=1.0: " The message is in Arabic. How does the lighthouse keeper interpret the message, and what are the consequences of the story's message on society, or what message did it transmit? The story should have a plot that starts with an action scene"
http temperature=0 (greedy): " The story should include the following elements: the lighthouse keeper's name, the bottle, the message, and the lighthouse's location. The story should be in the first person. The story should be around 500 words."
=== after (v0.34.0 + this change)
grpc temperature omitted: " The message is in the form of a riddle. The riddle is a cryptic message that leads to the story's resolution. The story should include a character named Sam, who is a lighthouse keeper in a coastal town. The"
http temperature omitted: " The message is in the form of a riddle. The riddle is a cryptic message that leads to the story's resolution. The story should include a character named Sam, who is a lighthouse keeper in a coastal town. The"
http temperature=0.6: " The message is in the form of a riddle. The riddle is a cryptic message that leads to the story's resolution. The story should include a character named Sam, who is a lighthouse keeper in a coastal town. The"
http temperature=1.0: " The message is in Arabic. How does the lighthouse keeper interpret the message, and what are the consequences of the story's message on society, or what message did it transmit? The story should have a plot that starts with an action scene"
http temperature=0 (greedy): " The story should include the following elements: the lighthouse keeper's name, the bottle, the message, and the lighthouse's location. The story should be in the first person. The story should be around 500 words."
```
</details>

No accuracy evaluation: requests with an explicit temperature are unchanged, and requests without one now match what the HTTP API already serves for the same model.

## Details

**Root cause.** `build_sampling_params` in `grpc/convert.rs` replaced an omitted temperature with 0.0 before lowering, so `lower_sampling_params` never applied `SamplingHints.default_temperature` to gRPC requests. The HTTP routes leave it unset, and lowering resolves `temperature.or(default_temperature).unwrap_or(1.0)`. This PR removes the override, so both protocols use that one rule, as gRPC already did for every other sampling field.

**Compatibility.** The wire schema is unchanged; only the meaning of an omitted `temperature` changes, now matching the proto comment's original intent (the comment is reworded to state the rule exactly). Clients that need greedy decoding must send `temperature: 0`. In-repo gRPC tests and clients were checked; none relied on the old default. `ServerInfo.proto_version` does not identify this behavior (vLLM v0.34.0 already reports 0.7.0), so a client that must support older servers can check `ServerInfo.engine_version` for the first vLLM release that includes this change.

**Documentation.** The proto comments are the reference for gRPC fields; there is no rendered docs page that documents `GenerateRequest` defaults.

**Related work and duplicates.** Searched open and merged vLLM PRs on 2026-11-17, including every open PR that touches `grpc/convert.rs`; none changes the omitted-temperature default. Two open PRs assume the current greedy default and would need a small update if this merges first: #66078 (gRPC parallel sampling) documents "The default temperature is `0.0` (greedy)" in `rust/README.md`, and #56776 (native sampling parameters) moves the greedy fill into `validate_sampling_params`. #56364 (RFC to split `Control` by caller) touches the gRPC server but not sampling defaults.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write and validate this change.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Stream diarized_json transcriptions as segment events
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Allow `stream=true` with `response_format=diarized_json` on `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. Each finalized segment emits `transcript.text.delta` followed by `transcript.text.segment`, then the stream ends with `transcript.text.done` and `[DONE]`.

## Claims

- Each delta carries its segment ID and the language-dependent separator, so concatenating deltas equals the final text. These are segment-level deltas, not token-level partial text.
- Native MOSS emits a segment when the next header arrives, with a bounded marker scan and no retained completed bodies. The default parser buffers fragments and joins once after generation completes, avoiding per-delta copies of the accumulated transcript.
- Native MOSS keeps valid segments visible before malformed output. Engine errors and aborts produce a stream error rather than successful done; the diarized response closes its active engine iterator on disconnect.
- Done-event usage counts rendered prompt tokens once, including audio positions, and sums prompts across engine requests.

## Validation

Latest revision: `6e09546d2`, based on `b1bbd26fe`. Linux validation used one RTX 6000 Ada, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 and Transformers 5.23.0. The official CUDA wheel came from `9986df412`, whose wheel-blocking compiled paths match the source base.

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib -q \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_audio.py::test_diarized_stream_parser_buffers_transformers_output \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_audio.py::test_diarized_stream_parser_rejects_unparsable_transformers_output \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_audio.py::test_transcription_output_parsing
# 66 passed in 21.10s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib -v -s \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_validation.py::test_transformers_backend_audio
# 1 passed in 38.50s
```

The six new fallback cases use the real VibeVoice processor and explicit expected segments. They cover Unicode, empty intermediate deltas, an empty or non-empty final delta, and unparsable output. These cases and the existing output-parsing test also pass with the test changes applied to `04ba5e123`, confirming unchanged semantics. The 59 native MOSS parser tests use explicit timestamps, speakers, text and failure prefixes rather than comparing two entry points into the same parser.

The GPU test serves `microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF` at `f22241c2062b3b25272bf117397e03d73381037a`, with eager execution, a 2,048-token context and prefix caching disabled. Through `RemoteOpenAIServer` and the OpenAI SDK, it checks ordinary transcription, non-streaming diarization, delta/segment/done order, matching IDs and text, and token usage against engine metrics.

The native MOSS server regression passed in 44.63 s on `04ba5e123`, using `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize` at `704aa4a9c304e8520be88901e0d1960158ef5b15`, eager execution, a 4,096-token context and disabled prefix caching. It was not rerun for this default-buffer-only revision; the native parser remains covered by the 59 CPU tests above. Native scanning and retained-text evidence is summarized in [the previous reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65779#issuecomment-6945239299).

Earlier local fault injection covered engine errors/aborts, ASGI disconnect/send failure and external cancellation. Those lifecycle checks are outside the contributed suite; the real-model server tests cover successful requests. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy. Existing multimodal-processing and speech-to-text CI steps select the tests. Upstream Buildkite has not run this revision.

<details>
<summary>Default parser accumulation benchmark</summary>

This CPU-only check exercises the actual default `StreamingDiarizedTranscriptParser` with eight-character deltas. It uses a real MOSS parsing hook to verify the assembled text after finalization; the VibeVoice processor and GPU checks above validate the Transformers path. The timings isolate accumulation, not the final model-specific parse. Median of three runs in the same Mac/Python 3.13 environment:

| Transcript size | 04ba5e123 | 6e09546d2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 256 KiB | 0.0693 s | 0.00491 s |
| 512 KiB | 0.264 s | 0.00984 s |
| 1 MiB | 1.229 s | 0.0197 s |
| 2 MiB | 8.627 s | 0.0408 s |

The final join and parse are measured separately; the new 2 MiB case took about 0.0034 s for that step. Run this in each checkout with the same environment:

```python
from statistics import median
from time import perf_counter
from vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces import StreamingDiarizedTranscriptParser
from vllm.model_executor.models.moss_transcribe_diarize import (
    MossTranscribeDiarizeForConditionalGeneration as Model,
)

for size in (256 * 1024, 512 * 1024, 1024 * 1024, 2 * 1024 * 1024):
    text = "[0][S01]" + "x" * (size - 11) + "[1]"
    samples = []
    for _ in range(3):
        parser = StreamingDiarizedTranscriptParser(Model, None)
        start = perf_counter()
        for pos in range(0, len(text), 8):
            assert list(parser.process_delta(text[pos:pos + 8], False)) == []
        samples.append(perf_counter() - start)
        segments = list(parser.process_delta("", True))
        assert [(s.start, s.end, s.speaker, s.text) for s in segments] == [
            (0.0, 1.0, "S01", "x" * (size - 11))
        ]
    print(size, median(samples))
```

A separate retained-input check found 262,144 characters still owned by the old parser after successful finalization, and 18 after malformed input failed. Both checks fail an empty-buffer assertion before the fix and pass with zero retained input afterward. The default parser still buffers the whole unfinished transcript; memory grows linearly with its content and fragment count.

</details>


## Details

- `get_streaming_diarized_parser_cls()` mirrors the existing streaming post-processor hook and receives raw output and `model_config`, matching #65735. The default implementation keeps the unfinished transcript as fragments, joins once at finalization and clears the fragments before model parsing. It still buffers the complete output; it does not add early parsing for Transformers models.
- MOSS scans the new delta plus at most 33 carried marker characters. Timestamp-to-speaker whitespace is tracked separately and restored to the open body if a candidate is rejected. Each completed body is joined once and released before yielding. Non-streaming MOSS parsing uses the same parser, checked against independent expected values.
- The response wrapper applies only to streamed `diarized_json`. Other response formats retain their current paths; the input-token correction is limited to the new format.
- Multi-audio-chunk parsing preserves main's raw-text concatenation behavior. This does not add global timestamp offsets or cross-chunk speaker reconciliation for models that cannot already provide them.
- #48543 added MOSS diarized JSON; the earlier streaming proposal #35260 was closed. #49119 covers delta/done events for existing text/JSON streams, #64007 audio duration, and #67091 word timestamps. They do not implement diarized segment streaming. #49119 shares response type names, which need reconciliation if it merges first. The duplicate scan found no other open PR for this feature.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support --override-generation-config
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support `--override-generation-config` in the Rust frontend, so `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve ... --override-generation-config '{...}'` starts instead of failing on an unsupported argument. The flag was listed in `rust/src/cmd/src/cli/unsupported.rs`; I noted I was taking it in #44280.

## Claims

- The override merges over the sampling defaults like Python's `get_diff_sampling_param`: on top of the model's generation config with `--generation-config auto`, on its own with `vllm`. A `null` value clears that default.
- An override `max_new_tokens` caps every request's `max_tokens`, including client-provided values, like Python's `override_max_tokens`.
- Works on both the `vllm-rs serve` path and the Python-supervised `--args-json` path. `vllm-rs serve` also forwards the flag to the managed engine, which reads it too (e.g. Llama 4 attention temperature tuning).

## Validation

**Tests**

| Test | Checks |
|---|---|
| `override_generation_config_merges_over_model_defaults` | Loads a model dir and snapshots `SamplingHints`: `auto` keeps the model's `top_p`, `vllm` does not, `null` clears `top_k`, override `max_new_tokens` becomes the default and the cap, and a bad value fails at startup |
| `chat_generation_config_overrides_reach_engine` | A chat request with no temperature and `max_tokens: 50` reaches the engine as `temperature 0.25, max_tokens 5`. Fails with `max_tokens 50` when the cap is removed |
| `resolve_max_tokens_applies_the_server_cap_to_client_values` | Cap applies to client and default values; the context window still wins when tighter |
| `override_generation_config_reaches_frontend_and_engine` | clap, `--args-json`, and forwarding to the managed engine |

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-text -p vllm-managed-engine -p vllm-server` pass, except `routes::tests::chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample`, which also fails on current main.


**Live check** against `vllm-mock-engine`, which decodes until `max_tokens` (setup from `rust/src/mock-engine/README.md`):

```bash
vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size-local 0 \
  --handshake-port 29550 --port 8765 \
  --override-generation-config '{"temperature":0.25,"max_new_tokens":5}'
vllm-mock-engine --handshake-address tcp://127.0.0.1:29550 --log-requests
```

| Chat request | `completion_tokens` | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| no `max_tokens` | 5 | Override is used as the default |
| `max_tokens: 50` | 5 (50 without the flag) | Cap applies to client values |
| `max_tokens: 3` | 3 | Smaller client values pass through |

## Details

`HfTextBackend` now loads `generation_config.json` as raw JSON, merges the overrides key by key (`merge_sampling_defaults`), then parses the result into the sampling defaults. EOS resolution still uses the unmodified file. The override `max_new_tokens` is kept separately as `SamplingHints::max_tokens_cap` and applied in `resolve_max_tokens`.

Deviation from Python: `skip_special_tokens` is not taken from this config (left as a TODO). The Rust frontend does not read it from `generation_config.json` either, so it can follow separately.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Reduce the shared expert for MegaMoE without sequence parallelism
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3 with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --enable-expert-parallel` and `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` serves garbage: no crash, normal throughput, wrong tokens.

`KimiMoE` builds the shared expert with `reduce_results=False`, and the MegaMoE branch of `forward` adds its output locally through the replicated up-projection, with no collective. That is correct under sequence parallelism, where the shared expert is replicated (or does its own reduce-scatter). With PP > 1 sequence parallelism is off (`pipeline_parallel_size == 1` in `use_sequence_parallel`), so the shared expert is TP-sharded and its partial outputs are never reduced: each rank continues with a different, incomplete hidden state.

This PR lets the shared expert reduce its own output in that case. Sequence-parallel and non-MegaMoE paths are unchanged. DeepSeek-V4 already does the same (`reduce_results=self.use_native_mega_moe`).

Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue covers this. #54347 enables sequence parallelism under PP for Kimi-K3, which would avoid this path, but it is a feature PR and does not fix the fallback; this fix is still needed while SP is off under PP.

## Test Plan

4x GB200 nodes (16 GPUs), `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro`, aggregated serving. The runs used nightly `9bc16ae6a3` with this one-line change overlaid; the changed line is identical on current `main`.

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"<Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark>","num_speculative_tokens":4,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

- GSM8K: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 64`
- Long-context recall: 18 prompts of 3.7k to 78k tokens, each a list of `The code for item i is <random>.` lines followed by a question about one item (temperature 0).
- Reference: same model at TP16 x DCP16, no PP (sequence-parallel MegaMoE path, untouched by this PR).

No unit test: the failure needs a multi-GPU MegaMoE launch, and a CPU test could only restate the flag expression.

## Test Result

| Engine | GSM8K accuracy | GSM8K invalid | Recall |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 x PP2, `main` | 0.011 | 19.5% | 0/18 |
| TP8 x PP2, this PR | 0.958 | 0.1% | 18/18 |
| TP16, no PP (reference) | 0.952 | 0.2% | not run with this config |

Isolation on TP8 x PP2 without the fix (recall): dropping the draft model 0/18, dropping DCP 0/18, dropping `--enable-expert-parallel`/MegaMoE 18/18.

Not claimed: any performance change. Without sequence parallelism every rank still sends all tokens through MegaMoE, so PP > 1 prefill stays slow; that is what #54347 addresses.

AI assistance was used (Claude Code) for the investigation, the change and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Prevent repeated PD KV fetches after decoder preemption
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

After decoder preemption or a partial promotion caused by a full CPU primary tier, the KV Offload P2P tier still reports PD cache hits that trigger an unsatisfiable second fetch and wait for the 30-second timeout. Track the initial nonempty PD fetch submission and return MISS on subsequent PD lookups so missing KV is recomputed.

## Claims

- Prevent unsatisfiable second PD fetches after decoder preemption or a partial promotion caused by a full primary tier.
- After a partial promotion, PD-tier lookup returns MISS for the unpromoted tail on a deferred rescan, even if primary capacity has become available.
- Preserve initial PD loading and local/other-tier cache lookup without additional control messages.

## Validation

The original fix was validated with real-engine checks on one NVIDIA GB10 with bf16, TRITON_ATTN, and ZMQ/NIXL. The PD request uses a 513-token prompt and 1,024 output tokens; each competing request uses 1,025/800 tokens. Decoder KV capacity is 32 blocks of 64 tokens.

| Model / scheduling | Preemptions in both runs | Failed promotions, before → after | PD completion (s), before → after | Matching tokens (all requests) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SmolLM2-135M-Instruct / FCFS | 1 | 3 → 0 | 45.99 → 13.52 | 1,824 / 1,824 |
| SmolLM2-135M-Instruct / priority | 2 | 10 → 0 | 49.06 → 27.71 | 2,624 / 2,624 |
| OPT-125M / priority | 1 | 10 → 0 | 45.00 → 15.14 | 1,824 / 1,824 |

Each row is one before/after pair. Completion time excludes engine initialization; outputs are compared with batch invariance enabled.

Regression coverage checks nonempty and empty PD fetches, symmetric P2P lookups, fresh request state, and partial promotion through a real `P2PSession` with fake transports.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu UV_NO_SYNC=1 PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_PLUGINS='' \
  uv run --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py \
  -k 'pd_lookup_misses_after_first_fetch or pd_partial_promotion'
```

**5 passed.** Without the fix, the partial-promotion test fails because the unpromoted tail returns `HIT_PENDING` instead of `MISS` after primary capacity is freed. With the fix, only fetch round 0 is sent. The full P2P suite reports **408 passed**. Scoped pre-commit checks passed. The model results above validate the original fix; the review updates were validated with the regression tests and full P2P suite.

## Details

1. The decoder's first nonempty PD fetch uses round 0. All PD stores on the prefiller also bind to round 0.
2. After preemption, the decoder looks up missing KV again. This can also happen without preemption: a full CPU primary tier stops the initial promotion partway through the prompt, then a deferred rescan reaches the unpromoted tail after capacity becomes available.
3. Another PD HIT would submit fetch round 1. The prefiller cannot supply that round, so it waits for the load timeout.

Record the first nonempty PD fetch submission in the request's `P2PSourceInfo`, then return MISS for later PD-tier lookups. Available primary-tier or other-tier KV can still be loaded; missing blocks are recomputed. Symmetric P2P probing is unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Honor activation scheme in MXFP8 linear selection
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The MXFP8 selector can choose a backend that internally quantizes activations even for a weight-only request. This fix filters kernels by the requested activation scheme, selecting Marlin or emulation for weight-only checkpoints. Quark activation-key forwarding is now provided by upstream #59460. Fixes #65193.

## Claims

- Explicit weight-only requests skip W8A8 kernels; forcing an incompatible backend fails during selection.
- Callers that omit the activation key retain existing W8A8 selection and A16 fallback behavior.
- Regression coverage includes real Quark layer construction and checkpoint loading through `LLM.generate`.

## Validation

**Latest conflict resolution (November 18):** head `171befb806` merges main `81a8cb063e`. The only conflict was the Eagle default-device cleanup: upstream #68350 now provides a restoring fixture, so this PR retains that upstream implementation and removes its redundant scoped-device change. The MXFP8 fix and DeepSeek ModelConfig fixture are preserved. Targeted pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check --cached` passed. [Buildkite #103776](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103776) passed on the previous head `4e33d548724b`; GPU tests have not been rerun on this merge commit.

**November 18 CI follow-up:** head `d8a2876fb3`, following CI merge `cfa14f05935e`. [Buildkite #103760](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103760) exposed two test setup problems:

- Four DeepSeek MXFP8 scale-loading cases used `SimpleNamespace(dtype=...)` as the model config. Activation override resolution reads `quantization_config`, which this stand-in lacks. The test now constructs a real `ModelConfig` from a local Llama config with an explicit architecture; assertions and parameter coverage are unchanged.
- AMD Model Executor 4/4 failed the Qwen3 Omni audio no-sync test twice. In that same process, the earlier Eagle test sets the global default device to CUDA without restoring it. Qwen's intended host lengths then inherit CUDA, and `int(chunk_num.sum())` synchronizes. The Eagle test now uses a scoped `torch.device` context. These paths were unchanged from the merged main parent; the full failure has not been reproduced separately on main.

Validation of this follow-up: `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/quantization/test_fp8.py tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py` and `git diff --check` passed. A local PyTorch CPU/meta check demonstrated the unscoped device leak and restoration on both normal and exceptional context exit; this is not a GPU test. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_deepseek_v41_mxfp8_scale_loading -q` still stops during collection: after installing missing `tblib` and Pillow, the next missing dependency is `zmq`. No GPU tests were rerun on this head. Maintainer-triggered CI is still required, including the ordered Eagle then Qwen tests in AMD Model Executor 4/4 and NVIDIA quantization 4/5. No tests were skipped or assertions relaxed.

The integration retains #59460's activation-fallback checks and the upstream requantization placeholder. The H200 results below apply only to the explicitly named earlier commit.

Tested patch: `392d905e03`; base: `e8570ef757`. One physical H200 NVL, Torch `2.14.0+cu132`, with precompiled vLLM binaries pinned to the base.

| Check | Red 1: base | Green: patch | Red 2: fix removed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MXFP8 + MXFP4 selection | 11 failed, 64 passed | 75 passed | 11 failed, 64 passed |
| Real Quark checkpoint + LLM | 1 failed: backend assertion | 1 passed | 1 failed: backend assertion |

All three stages used identical tests and binaries; only five production Python files changed. On H200, both red runs selected Humming and failed the weight-only backend assertion; green selected Marlin and generated two tokens.

[Full logs, exit codes, source hashes and replay scripts](https://gist.github.com/anhtud/1fffb3879b97711ea8b50245f8c3b588).

Additional checks passed: three Quark-to-Marlin GEMM shapes against a BF16-activation reference, pre-commit hooks (including Ruff, mypy and test tethering), and `git diff --check`. The Buildkite quantization job includes the new E2E regression.

**Remaining validation:** physical Blackwell execution and trained-model accuracy/perplexity evaluation. SM100/103/120/121 selection uses simulated hardware capability. The synthetic checkpoint validates dispatch and generation, not trained-model accuracy. No throughput benchmark was run.

**Draft status:** human line-by-line review and representative model evaluation remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands, checkpoint setup and output</summary>

Full revisions:
- Base: `e8570ef757b67805797b005b59fcd6600d939421`
- Tested patch: `392d905e035015e673ecd033b54f5bbee87bed34`

Run from the source checkout using the isolated environment's Python:

```bash
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py -q
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/quantization/test_mxfp8.py::test_quark_mxfp8_weight_only_checkpoint -v -s
```

The E2E test creates a seeded tiny Llama safetensors checkpoint with Quark weight-only MXFP8 metadata, loads real weights through `LLM`, checks the selected kernels, and generates two tokens. Setup and replay scripts are included with the logs.

Condensed output:

```text
red1 / red2, Quark SM100 selection:
assert isinstance(scheme.ocp_mx_linear, expected)
E assert False
E ... FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel ... MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel
11 failed, 64 passed

red1 / red2, real H200 checkpoint:
Using HummingMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
Exception: Call to collective_rpc method failed: assert False
... check_kernels ...
1 failed, 6 warnings

green, selection:
75 passed

green, real H200 checkpoint:
Using MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
1 passed, 6 warnings
```

Both suites returned exit code `1 → 0 → 1`. Source hashes confirm identical tests across stages and that the green source matches the tested commit.

The numerical check used `(M,N,K) = (1,128,128), (17,256,256), (3,130,256)`. Observed maximum absolute error was `0.0` for all three shapes; assertion tolerances were `rtol=0.02`, `atol=0.02`.

</details>

## Details

- **Compatibility:** the selector/config default is `kMxfp8Dynamic`; explicit `None` requests weight-only execution. Selection reuses the existing activation override resolution and adds a `_supports_quant_scheme` gate.
- **Backend support:** `input_quant_key()` describes external input/fusion support and does not identify internal activation precision. Marlin and emulation explicitly accept weight-only requests and retain the existing A16 fallback for W8A8. Other MXFP8 implementations default to requiring dynamic MXFP8 activations. The gate adds no inference hot-path work or synchronization; backend performance can differ and was not benchmarked.
- **Closed duplicate:** [#65394](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65394#issuecomment-6958552300) was closed without merging in favor of this PR. Its author noted this PR's broader backend coverage and E2E test. Its diff was reviewed; no additional fix was needed from it.
- **Related work:** the pre-submission duplicate check found no open PR directly fixing #65193. #63378 covers MoE and leaves dense MXFP8 for follow-up; #59460 covers fallback reporting/enforcement and identifies this missing key as a gap. #59460 has landed; the November 16 rebase preserves its activation-fallback checks and the upstream requantization placeholder. The issue author had announced a staged implementation, but no matching open PR was found at submission.

AI assistance was used to implement the change, run validation and prepare this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][XPU] Forward num_splits to the XPU flash attention kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The XPU flash attention shim in `vllm/_xpu_ops.py` accepts `num_splits` and then
drops it: it is listed in the "not used in xpu kernel currently" block and never
forwarded to `vllm_xpu_kernels.flash_attn_interface.flash_attn_varlen_func`. So
the `max_num_splits = 1` that `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` sets in
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py` never reaches the kernel, which keeps
choosing its own split count via `get_num_splits()`. This PR forwards it as
`num_splits_kv` and moves the parameter out of the stale comment block that made
the omission look deliberate.

The determinism suite could not catch this. `_random_prompt(10, 50)` in
`tests/v1/determinism/utils.py` only pads when the target exceeds 50 words, so it
returns roughly 16 tokens: the KV of every request fits inside a single kernel
block and no backend has a split to be inconsistent about. This PR adds
`_prompt_with_tokens(target_tokens)`, which tokenizes with the test model to hit
an exact token count, and uses ~2k-token prompts in the bs=1 vs bs=N test.

A residual violation survives this fix and is a **separate** defect, not
addressed here: the XPU kernel serves decode (`max_seqlen_q == 1`) from
`cutlass_paged_decode_interface` and prefill from
`cutlass_chunk_prefill_interface`, and those two reduce over KV differently
(the decode path has its own FP32 `max_logits`/`exp_sums` and a cross-sub-group
SLM epilogue). A prefix-cache hit that leaves a single query token therefore
disagrees with the cold prefill whatever the split count is, so no argument to
this shim can align them. That belongs in `vllm-xpu-kernels`; XPU users who need
batch invariance should keep using `TRITON_ATTN`, as
`docs/features/batch_invariance.md` already documents.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #55881 also concerns XPU batch invariance but only touches
  `vllm/platforms/xpu.py` backend selection; it does not touch
  `vllm/_xpu_ops.py`, and the dropped `num_splits` is unfixed on `main`.
- #55958 is the ROCm equivalent of the backend-selection change, not the shim.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "num_splits_kv"`
  returns nothing.

## Test plan

XPU (Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics, single card, `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`):

- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN pytest -sq
  tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN`
  with the longer prompts: 21-23 of 32 prompts mismatch before this change,
  1-2 of 32 after it. (FLASH_ATTN has to be forced; it is not the batch-invariant
  backend for XPU.)
- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest -sq
  tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_decode_logprobs_match_prefill_logprobs`
  on `TRITON_ATTN`: 1 passed in 151.18s.
- Instrumented shim: all 364 kernel calls in a batch-invariant run now receive
  `num_splits_kv=1`, including the 112 decode-shaped calls with
  `max_seqlen_q=1`; the remaining decode-vs-prefill residual (~9e-02) is
  reproducible and deterministic, which is what identifies it as the separate
  kernel-side defect described above.

CUDA (NVIDIA L40S, single card, vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev609+gc69d5d72a):
`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest -sq ...::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN`
passes on all 6 params (FLASH_ATTN/FLEX_ATTENTION/TRITON_ATTN x flex block
shapes) both before and after this change; 417.50s -> 435.93s, i.e. the longer
prompts add 4.4% to that test.

No model-quality impact is expected on CUDA: the source change is inside the XPU
shim only, and the test change only lengthens prompts.

🤖 Co-written with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.pr_title: [CI] Upgrade to pytest 9.2 and fix the tests that break on it
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Raises the test requirement to `pytest >= 9.2.0` and fixes the tests that break on it. Before 9.2, undoing `monkeypatch.setattr(instance, name, ...)` for an attribute the instance inherits from its class writes that attribute onto the instance (pytest-dev/pytest#10644). That leak caused #67664, which #67752 fixed for the one file that triggered it; with 9.2 the same leak cannot come back from the other tests that patch `current_platform` and similar singletons on the instance.

## Claims

- Test requirement `pytest >= 9.2.0` in `requirements/test/{cuda,rocm,xpu}.in`. The locks change pytest 9.1.0 -> 9.2.0 and pluggy 1.5.0 -> 1.7.0.
- `schemathesis >= 4.26.2`, the first release that supports pytest 9.2. 4.21.6 reads `item._nodeid`, which pytest 9.2 removed, so `test_openai_schema.py::test_openapi_stateless` failed. The lock moves to 4.26.2, not the latest 4.33.4, to keep the test-generation changes small. hypothesis-graphql and jsonschema-rs move with it, and hypothesis-jsonschema, junit-xml and starlette-testclient drop out (nothing in the repo imports them).
- `test_minicpmv.py` and `kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py` patch the class instead of an instance built with `object.__new__`. pytest 9.2 undoes an instance patch with `delattr`, and `nn.Module.__delattr__` raises `AttributeError: ... no attribute '_parameters'` because `__init__` never ran.
- `test_xpu_model_runner.py` uses vLLM's `fork_new_process_for_each_test` instead of `@pytest.mark.forked`. pytest-forked (1.6.0 and the latest 1.7.5) cannot marshal the `TestReport._id` (a `NodeId`) that pytest 9.2 adds, so every forked test fails ("unmarshallable object"). The upstream fix, pytest-dev/pytest-forked#112, is not released yet. This was the only `@pytest.mark.forked` test.
- `test_backend_xgrammar.py`: `@pytest.fixture` now sits above `@classmethod`, so pytest 9.2 collects the class fixture (commit from BugenZhao).

## Validation

Local runs used the vLLM CPU wheel on aarch64, comparing the old test code (before) with this PR (after):

| check | pytest 9.2.0, before | pytest 9.2.0, after | pytest 9.1.0, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/model_executor/test_minicpmv.py` | 3 errors (the CI `_parameters` error), 11 passed | 11 passed | 11 passed |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_xpu_model_runner.py` | 1 failed, `ValueError: unmarshallable object` | 1 passed | 1 passed |
| the `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod` patch from `_make_unquantized_flashinfer_test_layer`, copied into a CPU test (the module itself needs CUDA) | teardown error | passed, and the class is restored | passed |
| `schemathesis.pytest.from_fixture` + `parametrize` on a small schema | 4.21.6: `'Function' object has no attribute '_nodeid'` | 4.26.2: passed | n/a |

In CI, the jobs that failed for these tests on this PR's previous build (102877) run the changed tests on GPU: `(B200) Kernels Shard 2/3`, `(MI300) Model Executor Shard 3/4`, `Entrypoints Integration (OpenAI API completion)` (H200 and MI355) and `V1 Executor + Worker Shard 2/2` (H200 and MI355). The remaining failure in that build, `E2E Core Shard 1/2` (`test_hisparse.py`), was a main breakage fixed by #67753.

Earlier SM120 validation of the leak itself (before #67752 landed): in the failing shard's file order, pytest 9.1.0 gave 2 failed (the #67664 `PicklingError`) and 9.2.0 gave 82 passed.

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files; the locks come from the repo's `pip-compile` hooks.

## Details

- Duplicate check: no other open PR bumps pytest or schemathesis. #67752 is the narrow fix for #67664, and this PR keeps it.
- Patching the class keeps `monkeypatch` scoping, works on both pytest versions, and matches #67752. Assigning the attribute directly on the throwaway instance would also work, but mypy enables `method-assign` for `tests.*`.
- The `--forked` hints in a few `tests/quantization` module docstrings will not work on pytest 9.2 until pytest-forked ships #112. CI does not use `--forked`.
- Docs: test-only change, nothing user-visible.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate and write this change; I reviewed every line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Report failed pulls per request with several KV cache groups
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On a model with several KV cache groups whose transfer groups are all full attention, one failed NIXL KV pull stops the decode engine. HiSparse decode is such a model: it adds KV cache groups that take no part in the transfer (`enable_kv_transfer=False`). The worker reports the failed request's block IDs in `invalid_block_ids`, and `Scheduler._handle_invalid_blocks` raises for any model with more than one KV cache group. This reports those failures through `failed_recving` only, so the request fails (or is recomputed) and the engine keeps serving.

Related: #53779 (transfer groups), #53781 (HiSparse host-resident groups), #52232 (HMA receive failures).

## Claims

- With more than one KV cache group, a failed pull is reported only in `failed_recving`. `invalid_block_ids` stays empty, so the scheduler no longer raises, and the request ends as `FINISHED_ERROR` (or is recomputed under `kv_load_failure_policy: recompute`).
- With one KV cache group nothing changes: the request's block IDs are still reported.
- HMA layouts are unchanged; they already skip `invalid_block_ids`.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `test_transfer_setup_failure_returns_finished` gains a case with a second KV cache group outside the transfer, the shape HiSparse adds. On main the new case fails with `assert {7, 8, 9} == set()`: the block IDs the scheduler then rejects. With this change it passes.

```text
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k transfer_setup_failure_returns_finished
# main: 1 failed (test_transfer_setup_failure_returns_finished[True-False]), 3 passed
# this branch: 4 passed

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
# main:        366 passed, 3 failed
# this branch: 368 passed, 3 failed (the 2 new cases)
```

The 3 failures are the same on both: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]`, `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None]` and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` start an engine and need a GPU and a model download.

**Production, GLM-5.3 on H100.** P/D with NIXL 1.5.0, decode TP8 with HiSparse, vLLM main `d6aca837c3` plus three unrelated PRs. On 2026-10-13, 15 decode engines died in 4 hours, each with `RuntimeError: A KV connector reported block-level load failures (invalid_block_ids) which is not supported for models with multiple KV cache groups` right after a pull failed with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`. The condition in this change has run as a startup patch on every decode engine started after 15:56 UTC, all 36 by 20:15 UTC. None has died this way since. Two engines of one decode group failed 101 requests on pulls from two prefill workers between 18:46 and 19:33 UTC and kept serving. Why those connections fail is a separate issue; #61500 recovers from it.

## Details

Path of the failure, decode side:

1. The scheduler admits a request with remote KV and allocates blocks in every KV cache group, including the HiSparse groups outside the transfer.
2. `NixlConnectorWorker.start_load_kv` posts the read for the transfer groups. The read fails (`NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, or `transfer_setup_failed`).
3. `get_transfer_results` lists the request in `failed_recving`. Because `_is_hma_required` is derived from the transfer groups only (all full attention here), it also puts the request's group-0 block IDs in `_invalid_block_ids`.
4. `Scheduler.update_from_output` handles `failed_recving` (`_handle_failed_recving`), then `invalid_block_ids`. `_handle_invalid_blocks` raises because `kv_cache_groups` has more than one group, and the engine core dies.

The change gates step 3 on `len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups) == 1`, the same group set and condition the scheduler checks. Step 4 then only sees `failed_recving`.

Not a duplicate. Open PRs found with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for "invalid_block_ids", "failed_recving", "nixl hma failed transfer" and "kv load failure hybrid":

- #52232 propagates HMA receive failures per request. It keys on `_is_hma_required`, which is false in this case, and has merge conflicts with main, which has since gained `failed_recving`.
- #54733, #48216, #50742, #45497 and #56135 make the scheduler recover failed block loads for hybrid models. Each would let the scheduler accept these block IDs in some form. This change keeps the NIXL worker within the scheduler's current contract and does not depend on them.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Restore the default device after test_fc_layer_quant_config_usage
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_fc_layer_quant_config_usage` in `tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py` sets the default device to the GPU and never restores it, so every later test in the same pytest process creates tensors on the GPU by default. Since #68099, `test_qwen3_omni_audio_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync` runs after it in the `(MI300) Model Executor` shard and fails on every run, retries included:

https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780#01a1ed8d-81ae-4bfb-8a0f-cfb78d4a1232

```text
RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
```

This sets and restores the default device in a fixture, the same way `test_ernie45_vl_mrope.py` and `test_paddleocr_vl_mrope.py` already do.

## Claims

- `test_fc_layer_quant_config_usage` no longer leaks the GPU as the default device into later tests.
- `test_qwen3_omni_audio_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync` passes when it runs after it, as it does in CI.

## Validation

On one MI300X, main @ `bffbfccb7e`.

The new test passes on its own on main:

```text
$ pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py::test_qwen3_omni_audio_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync
1 passed, 17 warnings in 8.43s
```

After the eagle test, as in the CI shard, it fails on main:

```text
$ pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py::test_qwen3_omni_audio_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync
FAILED tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py::test_qwen3_omni_audio_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync
1 failed, 5 passed, 17 warnings in 4.00s
```

With this change:

```text
$ pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py::test_qwen3_omni_audio_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync
6 passed, 17 warnings in 7.71s

$ pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_eagle_quantization.py
5 passed, 16 warnings in 2.94s
```

## Details

With the GPU as the default device, even `feature_lens = torch.tensor([950, 130])` in the Qwen3-Omni test lands on the GPU, so the audio encoder gets device lengths instead of the host lengths it expects and reads them back at `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:480`. The encoder itself is fine with host inputs, so only the test that leaks the device needs a change.

Only AMD CI shows it because the NVIDIA Model Executor job is currently disabled.

Not a duplicate: there is no open PR touching these tests.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Test] Check the AITER delayed mHC pre against the residual it wrote
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter[True-2|7|128]` fails on MI300 (gfx942): AITER's `module_mhc` truncates the bf16 residual there, the torch reference rounds to nearest even, and the pre collapsed from the reference residual drifts by up to 0.25. This checks the pre outputs against the residual the op wrote, as AITER's own seam test does; the residual itself is still checked against the torch reference at one bf16 ULP.

## Claims

- The test passes on gfx942 with AITER's truncating residual and with an RNE-rebuilt `module_mhc`; gfx950 unchanged
- The residual is still checked against the torch reference at the same tolerance

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), local, `pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`:

| AITER `module_mhc` rounding | Before | After, 10 runs |
|---|---|---|
| Installed (truncation) | 3 failed, 84 passed | 87 passed every run |
| Rebuilt with `-DOPUS_FP32_to_BF16_DEFAULT=5` (RNE) | | 87 passed every run |

## Details

On gfx942 the residual is the truncated fp32 sum in every element (about half are one ULP smaller in magnitude than RNE); against a collapse of that residual, `layer_input` is bit-exact. The test came with #56513, and CI runs `kernels/mhc` only on MI355, where the conversion rounds to nearest even, so it never failed there. The truncation itself is AITER's (opus defaults to truncation on gfx94x, and the gfx942 ASM seam packs its residual the same way to stay bit-exact with `mhc_post`); fixing that is AITER work, tracked separately. This change only stops the test from comparing against a residual the op does not produce.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Optimize DeepSeek V4/V4.1 vision operations with Triton kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reduce DeepSeek V4/V4.1 image-encoding latency by fusing vision RMSNorm pointwise operations, Q/K rotary embeddings, and packed spatial merging with Triton. Preserve the reference reduction and rounding behavior.

## Claims

- Reduce full vision-tower + aligner CUDA graph latency by **13.4–21.0%** on the four existing test images, and **15.8%** when all four images are packed together, on one NVIDIA H20-3e.
- Preserve exact encoder outputs with real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights across all tested images and component ablations.
- Keep the shared V4/V4.1 integration and the existing PyTorch fallback for non-CUDA platforms.

## Validation

**Encoder benchmark:** NVIDIA H20-3e, BF16, TP1, FlashAttention; all 32 vision blocks and the aligner loaded from `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `314113f8a7dadb388215396ba5fbee2c610a04d6`. PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, CUDA 13.2, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.3, Transformers 5.22.1, driver 580.105.08.

Baseline: `8ca766326652caf4b8e50d1b9118d8a22f6adc73`. Candidate: `3e141117d55329a18ad425c2a97cf348300fdcb7`. The encoder harness restores the three original methods for its baseline and changes one component at a time for ablation.

| Input | Original size | ViT tokens | Baseline | Candidate | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| image1.png | 400 × 80 | 1,566 | 19.850 ms | 15.676 ms | 21.03% |
| image2.png | 400 × 80 | 1,566 | 19.849 ms | 15.679 ms | 21.01% |
| rgba.png | 800 × 600 | 2,494 | 31.884 ms | 25.825 ms | 19.00% |
| hato.jpg | 3082 × 2048 | 8,400 | 156.730 ms | 135.701 ms | 13.42% |
| Packed batch | All four images | 14,026 | 219.783 ms | 185.123 ms | 15.77% |

`image1.png`, `image2.png` and `rgba.png` come from `tests/multimodal/assets/`; `hato.jpg` comes from `tests/v1/ec_connector/integration/`.

Three independent encoder processes were run, reversing case and ablation order in the second run. Each variant uses three warmups, three graph replays for warmup, and five CUDA-event samples of five replays each. Baselines bracket the ablations. The table reports the median across runs, using the mean of the two bracketing baseline medians in each run. The range of run medians divided by their median is at most 0.72% for either arm. These timings cover ViT + aligner on GPU-resident inputs; image preprocessing, H2D copies, metadata construction, image delimiter assembly, and language decoding are outside this measurement.

Median CUDA graph latency across the same three runs. Each column enables only that component.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Measure process-local GPU memory in the Qwen3-VL leak test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #66409. The Qwen3-VL leak test now measures only its own process's GPU memory, and on ROCm it runs on all three decoder backends (`TRITON_ATTN`, `ROCM_ATTN`, `ROCM_AITER_FA`) instead of pinning `TRITON_ATTN`.

## Claims

- `test_no_memory_leak` no longer fails when another process on the same GPU allocates or frees memory.
- On ROCm, `@pytest.mark.parametrize("attention_backend", ATTENTION_BACKENDS)` covers `TRITON_ATTN`, `ROCM_ATTN` and `ROCM_AITER_FA`. `ROCM_AITER_FA` is skipped off gfx9. Other platforms keep a single run on their default backend.
- There is no leak in `ROCM_ATTN` or `ROCM_AITER_FA`. The `TRITON_ATTN` pin in #66409 was hiding a measurement problem, not a backend bug.

## Validation

Run on MI355X (gfx950) with idle GPUs, one GPU per backend:

| Backend | Runs | Passed |
|---|---|---|
| `TRITON_ATTN` | 30 | 30 |
| `ROCM_ATTN` | 30 | 30 |
| `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 30 | 30 |

```bash
pytest "tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_memory_leak.py::test_no_memory_leak[image_urls0-<BACKEND>]"
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_memory_leak.py -m core_model   # 4 passed, 82 s
```

- Each case logs `Using <BACKEND> backend (selected via --attention-backend)`.
- A copy of the test with a leak injected on purpose still fails, so the process-local check catches real leaks.
- Repro of the old failure: a side process on the same GPU allocating 256 MiB/s made the device-wide check fail (`gpu_growth=1024 MiB`) under `ROCM_ATTN`. Meanwhile this process's allocated memory, reserved memory and segment count stayed flat.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_gpu_used_bytes()` took total minus free for the whole device (`hipMemGetInfo`) and allowed 0 MiB of growth, so it counted every process on the GPU.
- The `ROCM_ATTN` failures seen in #66409 match outside activity: a +2 MiB step is exactly one extra HIP context from another process, and a 4.8 GB run started from a baseline already about 0.5 GB above normal.
- The `ROCM_AITER_FA` failure (1 of 45 runs) showed about 53 GiB of "growth", more than the device holds, while torch memory stayed flat.
- In 60+ clean runs, `memory_allocated`, `memory_reserved`, segment count and allocation retries were byte-identical from warmup to the last round on both ROCm backends.
- The 2/20 against 0/13 split between `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN` is not statistically significant (Fisher p ≈ 0.4–0.5).

**Fix.** Assert zero growth separately on `torch.accelerator.memory_allocated()` and `memory_reserved()`:
- Reserved covers this process's share of what the device-wide reading measured.
- Allocated also catches live-tensor leaks that cached free blocks would hide.

**Limitation.** Leaks of device memory allocated outside PyTorch within this process (for example a raw `hipMalloc` in a custom op) are no longer caught. vLLM's only large allocation of that kind, the KV cache, is made once at startup.

**CI cost.** The AMD job runs `test_no_memory_leak` three times instead of once, adding about 1 minute.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `test_memory_leak.py`.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Bound completed hypothesis histories in online beam search
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Online beam search returns at most `beam_width` hypotheses, but retains every completed hypothesis until generation ends. Each saved EOS hypothesis carries its token and logprob history. A long generation that keeps finding EOS candidates can therefore retain histories whose total length grows quadratically with decoding steps.

## Claims

- Keep the best finished hypotheses between steps using the existing final ranking key. A finished hypothesis never changes score, so once there are `beam_width` better finished hypotheses it cannot enter the result. The stable sort keeps earlier hypotheses first on equal scores, as the final sort already does.
- The active search, engine requests and offline implementation keep their existing behavior. This targets Python host memory in online serving.

## Validation

In an editable checkout with the vLLM test dependencies:

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py
```

The two new parameterized cases fail against the original implementation: at the start of a later step four completed hypotheses are still alive for width two. The patched file passes all 66 cases. One new case forces a tie across lengths and EOS IDs; the other requires a later completion to displace an earlier one. The existing Buildkite samplers step selects this module.

**API comparison.** Two NVIDIA A10s, one independent HTTP server per version, same seeded two-layer BF16 Llama checkpoint and tokenizer, eager execution. Twelve `/v1/completions` requests varied width (1, 3), length penalty (0, 1, 2) and `ignore_eos` (off/on). The 24 response choices matched field-for-field, including token IDs, logprobs and stop reasons; four ended with stop and twenty with length.

**Peak Python allocations.** Same deterministic engine-client fixture on both sides, EOS available each step, width 4, three runs per cell. Mean ± sample SD in MiB from `tracemalloc`:

| Max output tokens | Original | Patched |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 1.025 ± 0.007 | 0.136 ± 0.007 |
| 256 | 3.027 ± 0.001 | 0.233 ± 0.001 |
| 512 | 10.037 ± 0.001 | 0.436 ± 0.001 |

The table above isolates Python allocations when EOS appears every step.

**Pretrained model with unrestricted EOS.** One RTX 3080 per comparison, FP16 [SmolLM2-135M-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct/tree/12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac), online `/v1/completions` with chat-formatted prompts, width 4, length penalty 1, max 96 new tokens, eager, one request at a time. No token whitelist or forced stops. Each prompt ran three times per version. Immediately after each pruning point we counted finished hypotheses and the shallow bytes of their distinct token and logprob lists (deduplicated by list identity). These are retained list containers only. They exclude the referenced Python objects, server RSS and GPU memory.

| Workload (12 prompts each) | Old version exceeded width | Largest retained count, base → patch | Median per-request peak list bytes, base → patch |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| QA, translation, summary and short generation prompts written for this check | 10/12 | 68 → 4 | 26,932 → 4,256 |
| [Dolly-15k](https://huggingface.co/datasets/databricks/databricks-dolly-15k/tree/bdd27f4d94b9c1f951818a7da7fd7aeea5dbff1a), three prompts each from open QA, summarization, closed QA and creative writing | 7/12 | 36 → 4 | 8,716 → 5,320 |

Counts repeated across all three passes. All 288 returned choices matched field-for-field across versions (24 distinct prompts × four choices × three passes). One Dolly request went from 36 retained completions and 63,600 bytes to four and 6,496 bytes. Five Dolly prompts never exceeded the width. These samples show modest, workload-dependent host-memory savings at 96 steps.

To reproduce the Dolly inputs, use zero-based JSONL rows `4118, 4582, 11294, 12390, 14466, 3313, 14114, 5333, 14633, 3243, 5069, 13760` at the linked revision. Join nonempty `instruction` and `context` with a blank line, apply the model's chat template with a generation prompt, and pass the token IDs to the endpoint. The memory probe sums `v.__sizeof__()` for unique lists `v` in `(c.tokens, c.logprobs)` across finished sequences `c` after each step, before the final merge with active beams.

<details><summary>Dolly HTTP timing and output check</summary>

Two uninstrumented servers shared one RTX 3080, processed requests serially, and alternated which version ran first. After one warmup pass per server, three measured passes gave mean client wall time per request of 3.801 ± 0.030 s (base) and 3.701 ± 0.074 s (patch), reporting the sample SD of pass means. This small, single-host test measures serial requests.

**Resolved timing-run mismatch (Dolly row 5069).** One of 36 timed pairs differed. We recovered both full responses from fresh runs and verified their SHA-256 hashes against the original timing record. All four choices ended at 96 tokens; their token IDs and text first differ at output token 50.

Two independent RTX 3080 runs of the original retention algorithm each reproduced **both hashes on the same server** with overlapping requests. For all four matching traces there were **zero EOS completions and zero prunes** over all 96 search steps. A parallel calculation of the capped finished list on those very same engine outputs selected the identical four sequence objects in order. At search step 65 the active top-four cutoff reversed: candidate token 4334 ranked ahead of 59 (cumulative logprobs −31.3063 vs −31.3202) on one run and behind it (−31.3331 vs −31.3206) on the other. The change in active candidates selected continuations of different earlier prefixes. This explains why the returned texts can first differ before step 65. The differing response is reproducible with the original code, on a request that never uses finished-hypothesis pruning.

For a deterministic output comparison, set `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` before starting each server. Using the same row, seed, beam width and token limit, both uninstrumented versions returned the same full choices hash in all six replays per version with varying companion requests. The full online beam-search test module also passed again (66 tests).

</details>

## Details

The complexity trade-off is an extra stable sort on steps that collect more finished hypotheses than can be returned. A separate CPU fixture timing at 256 steps (without tracing; seven measurements after three warmups) gave original/patched means of 15.29/15.39 ms at width 1, 32.64/29.46 ms at width 4, and 61.49/53.73 ms at width 10. These timings exclude inference.

Tested using vLLM wheel `0.34.0rc1.dev139+gd9f94a98b` with the patch applied to the online module. The original module and original test file match the blobs checked on upstream main at `df7ce08e959c`. This is a source-audit finding. Related #60550 covers sibling-task cleanup on failure; #19347 optimizes active candidate construction. Neither changes retention of finished histories. No dedicated tracker was found for this retention issue.

- [x] Included the ranking invariant, baseline failure, test command, API comparison and measurement limitations.
</details>

commits.pr_body:
Give each rank its own CPU region outside the replicated layout, using logical worker ranks consistently with #58497. Count per-rank page padding against the full CPU budget and check aggregate shared-memory and cgroup headroom before any rank allocates. ## Tests

- With the previous CPU spec source (`980cf33256`), the focused capacity regressions produced 4 failures and 3 passes; the updated source passes all 7 cases.
- An injected capacity failure on `5303672870` reproduced the missing readiness barrier; the updated regression passes and preserves the capacity error.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

Historical validation on 4× H200, using `16d4ac4ba3` with the original per-rank change:

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: startup fell from 63.6 to 22.6 s (22.8 and 22.4 s in two runs), and pinning from 20.8 to 3.3 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
