commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Report FS-tier short writes as a likely full disk instead of EIO
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #66239. When the filesystem behind the `fs` offload tier fills up partway through a block, write(2) returns a short count and sets no errno.
The C store path reported that as EIO, which reads as a device error. Both store paths now raise an error that says it was a short write and names the likely cause: 
```
Encountered short-write error when writing <path>. This could be a hardware error or the filesystem may be full (ENOSPC)
```

## Claims

- A short write is reported as such on both the C and the Python store path, with the same message. Before, the C path raised `[Errno 5] Input/output error` and the Python path raised "Short write: expected N bytes, wrote M" without a likely cause.
- Each block is still written once and a failed store is accepted, as on main (no retry). Errors from write(2) itself keep their errno unchanged.
- No change on the success path or to the on-disk format.

## Validation

`test_store_short_write_names_likely_cause` in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py` sets RLIMIT_FSIZE below the block size in a subprocess, which produces a real short write on both paths.

On main (fs_io_C rebuilt), 2 failed:

    C path:      5 [Errno 5] Input/output error: '.../block.bin'
    Python path: None Short write: expected 196608 bytes, wrote 65536

With this PR:

    $ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py
    49 passed

End-to-end serving run: RTX 4090, Qwen2.5-0.5B, OffloadingConnector with a 256 MiB CPU tier and an `fs` tier on tmpfs filled to ~64 MiB free, 150 distinct ~2.5k-token prompts. 150/150 requests succeeded in both runs.

| commit | failed stores | EIO | ENOSPC | "Short write ... (ENOSPC)" |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main 2f58f98 | 337 | 329 | 8 | 0 |
| this PR | 321 | 0 | 2 | 319 |

Per-failure logs and the timeline are in the comment below.

## Details

write(2) on a regular file returns a short count when it runs out of space partway through a buffer, and sets no errno. On tmpfs (as used for /dev/shm-backed tiers) this is the usual way a full tier shows up; overlay and ext4 rejected the whole write with ENOSPC in my runs, which main already reports correctly.

An earlier version of this PR retried the short write to get ENOSPC from the kernel. Per review, it now writes once and reports the short write explicitly instead.

Related: #61780 (back-pressure on failed stores), #54363 item 4 (errno classification).

commits.pr_title: [Multimodal] Add TorchCodec image decoding backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in TorchCodec image decoding backend (`--media-io-kwargs '{"image": {"image_backend": "torchcodec"}}'`) and bump the torchcodec floor to 0.16, its first release with image decoders. 1/3 of a stack: #PR2 converts tensor images for processors that need PIL so it works everywhere, #PR3 makes TorchCodec the default on the models that natively accept tensors.

## Claims

- JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF images are decoded by TorchCodec into CHW `uint8` tensors that HF image processors consume directly, skipping their PIL-to-tensor conversion.
- `pixel_values` are bit-identical to the Pillow backend.
- Decode + preprocessing is 1.05-1.33x faster on CPU for Qwen2.5-VL / InternVL3.5 / Mistral-Small-3.1 (see Validation).
- Default behavior is unchanged (`pil`).

## Validation

**Unit tests** (`tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py`): bit-exact parity with Pillow for JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF × RGB/grayscale × all 8 EXIF orientations; Pillow is used for transparency, CMYK, 16-bit, GIF, animated and non-RGB targets; limits are enforced before decoding; fallback to Pillow on TorchCodec errors (corrupt input still returns 400); hash parity; `video/jpeg` frame lists.

```
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py tests/multimodal/test_hasher.py tests/multimodal/media/test_video.py
```

**Microbenchmark**: bytes → `pixel_values` through `ImageMediaIO` and the HF image processor (1 torch thread, median of 21 interleaved runs, transformers 5.20, torchcodec 0.17):

| Model | Image | Pillow (ms) | TorchCodec (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 15 MP | 681.5 | 602.4 | 1.13x |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 4.4 MP | 181.0 | 172.1 | 1.05x |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 2.8 MP | 110.8 | 90.5 | 1.23x |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 1.1 MP | 26.1 | 23.3 | 1.12x |
| InternVL3.5-8B-HF | 15 MP | 265.9 | 201.8 | 1.32x |
| InternVL3.5-8B-HF | 4.4 MP | 56.4 | 45.5 | 1.24x |
| InternVL3.5-8B-HF | 2.8 MP | 26.9 | 20.8 | 1.29x |
| InternVL3.5-8B-HF | 1.1 MP | 11.1 | 8.9 | 1.25x |
| Mistral-Small-3.1 | 15 MP | 275.3 | 207.4 | 1.33x |
| Mistral-Small-3.1 | 4.4 MP | 78.3 | 68.9 | 1.14x |
| Mistral-Small-3.1 | 2.8 MP | 47.8 | 41.8 | 1.14x |
| Mistral-Small-3.1 | 1.1 MP | 25.1 | 22.5 | 1.12x |

Both the decode (10-25% faster for JPEG) and the processor (no PIL-to-tensor conversion) contribute.

**Model outputs**: since `pixel_values` are bit-identical, model outputs are unchanged; no GPU end-to-end serving benchmark was run (the change only affects API-server preprocessing).

## Details

- Pillow still opens the image first (header only), so the format allowlist, `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` and the decoded-bytes budget are enforced before TorchCodec decodes anything; TorchCodec has no header-only probe yet.
- Images whose TorchCodec output would differ from the Pillow path stay on Pillow: transparency (TorchCodec drops alpha instead of compositing onto `rgba_background_color`), CMYK, 16-bit, animated images, and `image_mode != "RGB"`.
- AVIF is decoded single-threaded, at the same per-thread cost as Pillow (45.7 vs 44.9 ms for 1080p). Pillow's AVIF plugin uses all cores by default, so a single isolated AVIF request decodes faster with Pillow (~19 ms), but under concurrent load one thread per image avoids oversubscribing the media thread pool. GIF stays on Pillow: TorchCodec's GIF decoder is ~1.7x slower than Pillow's (single-threaded on both sides).
- Any TorchCodec exception falls back to Pillow, which either decodes the image (e.g. codecs disabled in a source build of torchcodec) or raises the usual client error.
- The hasher treats a 3D tensor in `MediaWithBytes` like a PIL image (bytes + `io_config`), so the cache key doesn't depend on the backend.
- `video/jpeg` frame lists decoded through `ImageMediaIO` are converted back to HWC.
- Packaging: floor `torchcodec >= 0.16` (CUDA/CPU/XPU); lockfiles now resolve 0.17.0. s390x builds torchcodec 0.17 with scikit-build-core (0.16+ dropped `setup.py`) and `TORCHCODEC_BUILD_IMAGE=0`, so it uses Pillow; **I couldn't build the s390x image locally**. ROCm still builds torchcodec 0.10 from source and uses Pillow.
- Limitation: some processors call PIL-only methods on images (vLLM's InternVL, DeepSeek-VL2/OCR and Step3-VL processors, remote-code ones like Kimi-VL, ...), so they fail with `image_backend="torchcodec"`. The docs say so; #PR2 converts tensors to PIL for them.
- Torchcodec bundles its own libjpeg/libpng/libwebp, so security fixes for those come through torchcodec releases.
- Duplicate check: no open PR or issue proposes TorchCodec image decoding.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix][DSv4.1] Build the gfx942 top-512 extension from a copy in its build directory
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On gfx942, DeepSeek-V4.1 with `--monokernel` builds `topk512_gfx942.cu` at startup with `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`, which writes the hipified `topk512_gfx942.hip` next to its input in the installed vLLM tree. A server that cannot write the install (non-root, as in #40275's `vllm-openai-nonroot` image or an OpenShift arbitrary UID) fails that write, the build fails, and every top-512 hook of the sparse indexer falls back to vLLM's ops. This builds from a copy of the source in the extension's build directory.

## Claims

- A non-root server with a read-only install uses the gfx942 top-512 again. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI325X TP4, AgentX trace replay at concurrency 16: median TPOT -10% and -18%, p50 E2E-normalized interactivity +10% and +19%, total tok/s +4% and +5% in the two PR runs against `main`.
- Root servers build and load the same extension as before.
- The new test fails on `main` and passes with this PR.
- No measurable accuracy change on GSM8K or GPQA Diamond.

## Validation

MI325X (gfx942), vLLM nightly `0.34.0rc1.dev398+g153dc0464` with `topk.py` from `main` (`543cb51c07`) or from this PR, AITER 0.1.29, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0.

```
$ pytest -v tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_topk.py -k "writes_nothing or failed_build"
# main
test_build_writes_nothing_beside_the_installed_source FAILED
E       AssertionError: assert not True
E        +  where True = <function exists>('.../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/topk512_gfx942' + '.hip')
test_failed_build_leaves_the_top_k_to_vllm PASSED
# this PR
test_build_writes_nothing_beside_the_installed_source PASSED
test_failed_build_leaves_the_top_k_to_vllm PASSED
```

`topk.build()` in a new process, as root and as UID 65534 with its own empty cache:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| root, cold / warm cache | True, 21.0 s / 0.5 s | True, 21.0 s / 0.4 s |
| non-root, cold / warm cache | False, 6.2 s / 6.1 s | True, 21.3 s / 0.6 s |

On `main` the non-root build logs `Failed to save .../topk512_gfx942.hip with "Permission denied"`, then `Error building extension 'dsv41_topk942'`. With this PR, eight non-root processes building into one empty cache at once, as the ranks of a TP8 server do, all load the extension and leave no partial copy.

End to end, the server below runs as UID 65534 with a read-only vLLM install, 3,600 s per run, a fresh server per run. `main` logs `building topk512_gfx942.cu failed, so vLLM's top-k ops run instead` on all four ranks; this PR does not.

| run | p50 intvty | p90 intvty | total tok/s/GPU | TPOT mean / median (ms) | TTFT mean / median (ms) | E2EL p90 (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main 1 | 170.7 | 81.1 | 25,505 | 6.20 / 5.21 | 399 / 141 | 14.99 |
| main 2 | 173.0 | 83.1 | 26,077 | 5.96 / 5.14 | 319 / 142 | 13.30 |
| PR 1 | 189.7 | 84.1 | 26,826 | 5.54 / 4.64 | 425 / 141 | 12.18 |
| PR 2 | 205.0 | 93.2 | 27,185 | 5.10 / 4.24 | 295 / 137 | 11.67 |

Accuracy on the same non-root servers with the recipe's DSpark verification (`rejection_sample_method` `block` instead of the synthetic acceptance above), temperature 0, one run each, all items. GSM8K is 5-shot with up to 4,096 generated tokens; GPQA Diamond is `gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot` with up to 16,384, where 37 (`main`) and 30 (PR) of the 198 responses end inside their reasoning. Both differences are within one standard error.

| | GSM8K strict / flexible | GPQA Diamond flexible |
|---|---:|---:|
| main | 0.9742 / 0.9735 ± 0.0044 | 0.7525 ± 0.0307 |
| this PR | 0.9727 / 0.9719 ± 0.0045 | 0.7828 ± 0.0294 |

<details>
<summary>Server command</summary>

```bash
AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51}'
```

This is InferenceX's `dsv41flash-fp4-mi325x-vllm-agentic-dspark` TP4 concurrency-16 point, checkpoint revision `314113f8`.

</details>

## Details

`load()` hipifies a source outside its build directory in place. The copy goes to `_get_build_directory("dsv41_topk942")`, the directory `load()` builds in (it honors `TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR`), so the `.hip` lands there; AITER's JIT copies its sources to `~/.aiter` for the same reason. Concurrent TP ranks copy through `os.replace`. ninja compiles the hipified file, which hipify rewrites only when its content changes, so an unchanged source is not rebuilt.

Only DeepSeek-V4.1 with `--monokernel` on gfx942 builds this extension. The restored kernels are the default path, and the existing tests in this file assert that they choose the same top-512 as vLLM's ops. A server without a working compiler still falls back. CI runs as root, which can write the install, so the test checks that nothing is written next to the source.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find, measure and write this change; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Fuse the MXFP8 input quant of fused_wqa_wkv and the shared expert into their producers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview On gfx950 (AITER FlyDSL MXFP8 path, #67377), DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP8 linears quantize their bf16 input in a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` launch. This PR moves that quant into the producing kernel for three linears: - **① `fused_wqa_wkv`**: AITER Mega-MHC also writes its attention-seam layer input as MXFP8. - **② shared expert `gate_up_proj`**: likewise for the FFN-seam layer input. - **③ shared expert `down_proj`**: a new Triton kernel fuses `silu_and_mul_with_clamp` with the MXFP8 quant. Outputs are bit-identical to the unfused path. ## Claims - Removes three standalone MXFP8 quant launches per layer, and the bf16 round trip of the shared expert's activation. - On 2x MI355X DEP2, the forward step is 0.23-0.38% faster for 8k / 16k-token prefill and 768-token decode steps. - Bit-identical outputs; GSM8K unchanged. - ROCm-only change; other backends keep their current path. ## Validation **Unit test (MI355X)**: both producers are bit-identical to the unfused path (22 passed). ```bash pytest tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_mxfp8_input_fusion.py ``` **Forward step time** (`vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 2x MI355X, DEP2, AITER MegaMoE, fp8 KV, DSpark k=5). The times are per DP rank, median graph-replay time of one full step, including the sampler and drafter. | Case (per DP rank) | Base | This PR | Δ | |---|---:|---:|---:| | prefill-16k: 1 × 16384-token prefill | 393.36 ms | 392.46 ms | −0.23% | | prefill-8k: 1 × 8192-token prefill | 214.41 ms | 213.62 ms | −0.37% | | decode-128: 128 × verify (1 + 5 drafts), KV ≈ 16k | 71.81 ms | 71.54 ms | −0.38% | ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \ torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \ -dp 2 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend aiter_mega_moe --all2all-backend mori \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \ --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 65536 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --routing balanced \ --case prefill16k=16384 --case prefill8k=8192 --case "decode128=128*6@16384:5" ``` End to end on AgentX (c256, DEP2), throughput and interactivity before and after the fusion are on par. **Trace before / after (prefill step, one full-length layer)** ① (before fusion): ① (after fusion): ②③ (before fusion): ②③ (after fusion): **Accuracy (GSM8K)**: 8-shot, all 1319 questions, settings of `.buildkite/lm-eval-harness/configs/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4.yaml`, against a DEP2 server. | Run | strict-match | flexible-extract | |---|---:|---:| | Base | 0.9257 | 0.9272 | | This PR | 0.9265 | 0.9272 | ```bash lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args "model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,tokenizer_backend=None,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False" \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8 --limit 1319 --batch_size 1 ``` ## Details `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` already reads a `QuantizedActivation` with row-major `[M, K / 32]` E8M0 scales, so the producers hand over the quantized copy and the GEMMs are unchanged. - **① / ②:** `mhc_pre_delayed_mxfp8` runs the Mega-MHC seam with `out_dtype="mxfp8"`. It attaches the `QuantizedActivation` to the bf16 layer input as an attribute (`attach_mxfp8_input`), which `fused_wqa_wkv` and the shared expert's `gate_up_proj` read back. Any reshape, slice or gather drops the attribute, so a consumer only sees the copy of the rows it projects. The bf16 input stays available for the router, compressor, indexer and MegaMoE, and the shared `forward` signatures are unchanged. - **③:** `silu_and_mul_mxfp8` computes the clamped SiLU-and-mul in fp32, rounds it to bf16 as the unfused path does, and quantizes it with `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel`'s arithmetic. **When it applies:** gfx950 with AITER, the consumer linear on `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` / `AiterFlyDSLMxfp8LinearKernel`, and no sequence parallelism. In addition: - ① / ② need Mega-MHC; ② also needs MegaMoE with an unfused shared expert. - Decode steps of at most 128 tokens per rank inside FULL graphs use the mHC overlap path, where ① / ② do not apply. **Other backends:** only ROCm-only modules change (`vllm/_aiter_ops.py`, `models/deepseek_v4/amd/`, `models/deepseek_v41/amd/`). Shared layers are untouched, so CUDA, XPU and CPU are unaffected. DeepSeek-V4 shares `DeepseekV4MLP`, but its linears are not MXFP8, so it keeps its current path. **Not a duplicate:** open PRs #66572 / #65837 (q-norm quant before `wq_b`) and #63821 / #66856 (`wo_a` epilogue quant before `wo_b`) fuse different quants. ---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Muse Spark: finalize the token-sharded MoE reduction in one reduce-scatter
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm under TP, `MuseSparkTopKWeightAndReduce` finalizes the MoE output of a batch of at least 256 tokens in three steps: reduce-scatter, per-rank `fused_post_expert_finalize`, then all-gather. It does this in 1024-token chunks. With `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16` (set by every AMD command of the recipe) the chunks bound no memory, so this PR finalizes the whole batch with one reduce-scatter and one all-gather per MoE layer. The all-gather runs in place when no padding is needed.

**Relation to #64461.** #64461 replaces this reduce-scatter for the MXFP4 (AITER) experts at TP prefill (eager batches of >= 1024 tokens): stage 2 runs column-sharded on the gathered MXFP4 intermediate, so those layers no longer reach this path. The two PRs touch different branches of the finalize and merge cleanly in either order. Which one a MoE layer takes under TP (no EP), for batches above 1024 tokens:

| Checkpoint | MoE layers | Experts | Column-sharded stage 2 on (default) | Column-sharded stage 2 off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | all | Triton | this PR | this PR |
| MXFP4 | first and last (BF16) | Triton | this PR | this PR |
| MXFP4 | the others | AITER | #64461 | this PR |

The column-sharded stage 2 is off with `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_COLUMN_SHARDED_DOWN=0` (about 9% more KV cache at TP8), or with an AITER without the two-stage API. It does not pay off for the Triton experts: their BF16 intermediate is as wide in bytes as the reduce-scatter it would replace, and a second BF16 `w2` would not fit. This PR changes nothing under TP + EP, or for batches of 1024 tokens or fewer.

## Claims

- Scope: the MoE layers marked "this PR" in the table above. TP + expert parallel is unchanged. The measurements below are on the MXFP4 checkpoint on `main` (without #64461), where every MoE layer takes this path.
- TP8 + DSpark on `main` (`0f6b261910`), recipe plain-TP settings: single-request TTFT drops 7–8% for 2k / 8k / 16k-token prompts and for a burst of four 8k prompts. On an earlier base it was 9–13%.
- Concurrency sweep, random 8k in / 1k out: output throughput +2.0 to +4.0% at c16 and +6.0 to +6.9% at c32. Mean TTFT drops 7–10% and mean TPOT drops 2–5%.
- Finalize alone, 8 GPUs: 14–29% faster above 1024 tokens. Up to 1024 tokens the output is bitwise identical to the base, and so is the output for the fp32 reduce dtype and the unfused-norm path at every size. Above 1024 tokens with the bf16 reduce dtype, RCCL sums the partials in a different order; the error against an fp32 reference is the same.
- The peak extra memory of the finalize goes down or stays within the profile run's footprint (64 MiB per GPU at 8192 tokens). The KV cache size is unchanged.
- Accuracy: GSM8K shows no significant difference (paired p = 0.74 and 0.86). TP8 + EP8 outputs are bitwise identical to the base, because this path is not taken under EP.
- No new flag or environment variable. The change takes effect with `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16`; under the default `fp32` the chunks are kept and the output is bitwise identical.

## Validation

### Configuration

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | 8×MI355X |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:muse-spark-open`, Python tree replaced by the base or this PR |
| Models | `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4` + `Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark` (7 speculative tokens) |
| Env | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1` |
| A/B | base and PR arms back to back on the same node; each pair measured on two nodes, in alternating arm order |

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 --served-model-name musespark \
  --tokenizer-mode hf --config-format auto --load-format safetensors --generation-config vllm \
  --language-model-only --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --reasoning-parser musespark1x --tool-call-parser musespark1x --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'
# TP8 + EP8: add --enable-expert-parallel
```

Throughput sweep (one warm-up of 16 prompts at concurrency 8 first; each concurrency run twice with different seeds and averaged):

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model musespark \
  --tokenizer amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0.0 \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts $((4 * C)) --max-concurrency $C \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed $((1000 * R + C)) \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Single-request TTFT: a burst of `k` concurrent fresh random-token prompts with `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`. We report the median wall time of the burst over 12 / 16 / 8 / 6 bursts for 2k / 8k / 16k / 4×8k, with the first burst dropped.

### TTFT on `main` (TP8 + DSpark)

Base `main` (`0f6b261910`) → this PR rebased on it, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-e4a5b5537344b103ed10de7764378ef09604ef3d` (Python tree replaced), recipe plain-TP settings (`--max-num-seqs 32`). Four arms on one node in the order base, PR, PR, base; each value is the mean of the two arms' medians.

| Config | Input / output tokens | Concurrent requests | TTFT (ms), median |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| TP8 + DSpark | 2048 / 1 | 1 | 116.5 → 108.3 (−7.0%) |
| TP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1 | 1 | 356.1 → 328.0 (−7.9%) |
| TP8 + DSpark | 16384 / 1 | 1 | 720.4 → 665.2 (−7.7%) |
| TP8 + DSpark | 8192 / 1 | 4 (burst) | 1397.5 → 1289.8 (−7.7%) |

The two arms of each side agree within 3% (2k) and 1% (others). KV cache: 6,846,396 tokens in all four arms.

### TTFT (TP8 + DSpark, earlier base `6c2549be42`)

| Metric | node A: base → PR | node B: base → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TTFT 2k, ms | 117.8 → 102.2 (−13.2%) | 119.0 → 108.8 (−8.6%) |
| TTFT 8k, ms | 353.6 → 318.3 (−10.0%) | 359.8 → 320.3 (−11.0%) |
| TTFT 16k, ms | 718.2 → 649.4 (−9.6%) | 728.0 → 654.2 (−10.1%) |
| 4×8k burst, ms | 1397.2 → 1256.2 (−10.1%) | 1408.4 → 1269.4 (−9.9%) |
| KV cache, tokens | 6,350,664 → 6,350,664 | 6,350,664 → 6,350,664 |

Burst min–max spread is below 2%.

### Concurrency sweep (TP8 + DSpark)

This sweep was measured on an earlier base, `0626d646d0`. There, `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/muse_moe_runner.py` (the only file changed here) is byte-identical to the one on `main`. It used the previous revision of this PR, which differs only in gathering into a new buffer and copying instead of gathering in place; the outputs of the two are bitwise identical and the in-place one takes 1% less finalize time. The TTFT deltas measured in the same sessions match the table above: 8k −9.5% / −9.8%, 16k −10.1% / −9.4%.

All values are the mean of 2 runs; AL is the mean DSpark acceptance length.

| Run | Conc. | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT, ms | P99 TTFT, ms | Mean TPOT, ms | AL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| node A, pair 1 | 16 | 1058.7 → 1097.9 (+3.7%) | 1208.9 → 1116.6 | 5788 → 5230 | 12.38 → 12.07 | 2.82 / 2.78 |
| | 32 | 1299.1 → 1388.2 (+6.9%) | 2026.7 → 1834.4 | 11378 → 10273 | 20.56 → 19.69 | 2.79 / 2.77 |
| node A, pair 2 | 16 | 1045.3 → 1087.3 (+4.0%) | 1230.7 → 1118.8 | 5778 → 5240 | 12.57 → 11.96 | 2.75 / 2.79 |
| | 32 | 1315.8 → 1394.7 (+6.0%) | 2019.0 → 1821.1 | 11359 → 10307 | 20.50 → 19.58 | 2.79 / 2.80 |
| node B | 16 | 1037.3 → 1057.6 (+2.0%) | 1245.6 → 1149.0 | 5806 → 5274 | 12.66 → 12.38 | 2.72 / 2.67 |
| | 32 | 1306.6 → 1390.9 (+6.5%) | 1998.2 → 1854.4 | 11416 → 10354 | 20.67 → 19.67 | 2.80 / 2.80 |

The gains come from the steps that carry 8k-prompt prefill chunks: they set TTFT, and at c16 / c32 they are interleaved with decode, so they also stretch TPOT. Mean TPOT further depends on AL, which varies by about ±0.1 between runs, so AL is listed per arm. The sweep covers c16 and c32 only. At c1 / c4, decode steps carry 8–32 tokens, below the 256-token token-sharded threshold, so this change does not affect them; their TPOT would mostly reflect AL.

### Finalize alone (8 GPUs, real collectives)

`MuseSparkTopKWeightAndReduce.apply` at TP8 with `[T, 8, 4096]` bf16 partials and the fused norm, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. Times are medians of 20 eager calls. Peak is the extra memory over inputs and output (max over ranks). Two nodes agree within 1%.

| T (bf16 reduce dtype) | base µs | PR µs | base peak MiB | PR peak MiB | output |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 256 | 162.4 | 157.2 | 4.2 | 2.0 | bitwise equal |
| 1024 | 298.6 | 295.6 | 17.0 | 8.0 | bitwise equal |
| 1031 | 316.4 | 313.2 | 17.0 | 8.0 | bitwise equal |
| 2047 | 599.2 | 493.3 (−17.7%) | 81.1 | 15.9 | reduction order |
| 4100 | 1089.0 | 850.1 (−21.9%) | 17.0 | 32.0 | reduction order |
| 8191 | 2148.2 | 1561.0 (−27.3%) | 81.0 | 63.9 | reduction order |
| 8192 | 2104.5 | 1540.9 (−26.8%) | 17.0 | 64.0 | reduction order |
| 16384 | 4156.2 | 2961.3 (−28.7%) | 17.0 | 128.0 | reduction order |

- "Reduction order" rows: each token is reduced on a different rank than in its 1024-token chunk. The mean error against an fp32 reference is 1.44e-3 for both base and PR, and every rank holds the same output.
- Above 1024 tokens the PR peak is the reduce-scatter output `[T/8, 8, H]`. At the profile run's 8192 tokens that is 64 MiB per GPU, so it is accounted for; the KV cache size does not change.
- fp32 reduce dtype: the output is bitwise equal at every T, time is 0.5–1.7% lower, and the peak drops from 153 to 144 MiB when no padding is needed.

### Accuracy

| | node A: base → PR | node B: base → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K strict / flexible (5-shot, 1319) | 94.92 / 94.92 → 94.69 / 94.69 | 94.84 / 94.84 → 94.69 / 94.69 |
| Paired (base-only / PR-only correct, exact McNemar p) | 20 / 17, p = 0.74 | 17 / 15, p = 0.86 |

Noise reference: two base runs on the two nodes differ in 14 / 15 questions (p = 1.00). The GSM8K command is `lm_eval --model local-completions ... num_concurrent=32,max_gen_toks=512 --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`. At 32 concurrent requests its 256-token DSpark decode steps exercise the in-place all-gather inside captured CUDA graphs.

Greedy outputs:
- TP8 + DSpark: both arms reproduce only the prefill token across repeated requests in one server, because later tokens depend on speculative acceptance. So the first token's logprob is compared.
  - It is bitwise equal to the base for prompts of 45, 1024 and 1031 tokens.
  - For prompts of 4096–8193 tokens it differs by 0.0002–0.33 nats (reduction order).
  - Prompts of 4100 / 8185 / 8191 / 8193 tokens complete normally.
- TP8 + EP8 + DSpark: all greedy outputs (10 prompts × 2 passes, logprobs included) are bitwise identical to the base.

### Tests and checks

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py` plus the other Muse Spark kernel and loading tests: 115 passed on `main` (`544f182d9f`); after the rebase onto `0f6b261910`, the Muse Spark ROCm kernel and model tests pass with the nightly image above (90 passed, the rest skipped as CUDA-only).
- The finalize-alone A/B rerun on `main` matches the table above within 1%, with the same peaks and bitwise results.
- With `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on `main`, the TP8 + DSpark server starts and serves 19 requests with prompts of up to 8193 tokens, which exercise the new paths (whole-batch reduce-scatter with the in-place all-gather, and the reduce-scatter + all-reduce tail). No sync is reported.
- `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

**Why the chunks exist and why they can go.** `_FINALIZE_CHUNK_ELEMS` bounds the reduce-dtype copy of the per-route output `[T, top_k, H]`: 1 GiB at 8192 tokens with the fp32 default. With the bf16 reduce dtype, `.to()` copies nothing. The chunks then only split one reduce-scatter / all-gather pair into eight (at 8192 tokens), in each of the 62 MoE layers. When the per-route output is already in the reduce dtype, the whole batch is now one chunk. With a real copy (fp32), the chunks are kept.

**Non-TP-divisible batches.** A chunk larger than one default chunk reduce-scatters its TP-divisible prefix. The remaining (< TP) tokens take the existing all-reduce + fused finalize, the path already used below 256 tokens. Padding such a chunk would copy all of it (512 MiB at 8191 tokens). Chunks of up to one default chunk are padded as before (at most 64 MiB, cheaper than an extra all-reduce launch), so the output for batches of up to 1024 tokens is unchanged.

**In-place all-gather.** When a chunk needs no padding, each rank finalizes straight into its rows of the output. Then `torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor(out, out_local, group=get_tp_group().device_group)` runs in place (`out_local` is the rank's slice of `out`, the in-place layout NCCL/RCCL support). This replaces gathering into a new `[T, H]` buffer and copying it. vLLM's `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` has no output argument; on ROCm it calls the same `all_gather_into_tensor` on the same device group (`CudaCommunicator.all_gather` defers to the base class there). The call sits inside the MoE custom op, like the existing reduce-scatter / all-gather calls of this class. `sparse_attn_indexer` and `flashmla_sparse` call `all_gather_into_tensor` directly in the same way, into preallocated buffers on `get_dcp_group().device_group`.

**Scope.** This changes only `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/muse_moe_runner.py`: +42 / −20 lines, no new helper, flag or env var. The fp32 reduce dtype, the unfused-norm path, batches below 256 tokens and EP (MoE `tp_size == 1`) behave as before.

**Tests.** The new paths are covered by real collectives rather than a mocked unit test. @mawong-amd ran TP2 and TP4 on MI300X over the oversized/tail path, the padded path and the FP32-reduce control (TP2 BF16 bitwise identical, TP4 within tolerance), and [CI build 101405](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101405) passed. The padded path is also covered by the existing tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py`.

**Limitation.** Above 1024 tokens with the bf16 reduce dtype, TP outputs are not bitwise identical to the base (RCCL reduction order, same error). A follow-up could use AITER's custom reduce-scatter / all-gather for 256–1031 tokens (7–32% faster finalize in our measurements); it is not part of this PR.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Avoid host synchronization in the Dots3Note vision tower
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Dots3Note vision tower reads back to the host in two places. Both are
rejected by the repository's GPU-sync checker (`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, baked
into the CI image) and both stall the host on every vision step:

1. `prepare_meta()` and `rot_pos_emb()` build small tensors on the host and move
   them with `Tensor.to(..., non_blocking=True)`. The sources are pageable, so
   those copies are not asynchronous.
2. `VisionAttention` and `VisionSdpaAttention` build a block-diagonal mask by
   looping over `cu_seqlens` and using its elements as Python slice bounds. A
   CUDA scalar as a slice bound is a host read, so this syncs once per segment.

Stage the metadata through pinned memory with `async_tensor_h2d`, and derive the
per-token segment ids on the device with `searchsorted` so the mask becomes one
vectorized comparison.

## Claims

- `prepare_meta()` / `rot_pos_emb()` no longer perform blocking H2D copies.
- `VisionAttention` / `VisionSdpaAttention` no longer read `cu_seqlens` on the
  host.
- No behaviour change: the tower output is byte-identical before and after.

## Validation

Environment: RTX 3090 24 GB (sm_86), torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM 0.33.0, with
`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` armed around the vision path.

The two fixes are independent, so the check fails twice on the way to green --
which is also the evidence that both are needed:

| code | result |
|---|---|
| current `main` | `RuntimeError` at `vision.py:614` |
| metadata fix only | `RuntimeError` at `vision_attention.py:211` |
| both fixes | no sync reported; output unchanged |

<details>
<summary>Failure output for the two stages</summary>

Metadata stage:

```
File ".../dots3_note/nvidia/vision.py", line 614, in prepare_meta
    cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens_cpu.to(self.device, non_blocking=True),
RuntimeError: Tensor.to: a non_blocking H2D copy that may be silently
  synchronous (the CPU tensor is not pinned). Implicit GPU<->CPU sync detected
  - use a pinned, densely laid out CPU tensor, or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
```

Mask stage (after the metadata fix):

```
File ".../dots3_note/nvidia/vision_attention.py", line 211, in forward
    cu_seqlens[i - 1] : cu_seqlens[i],
RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()
```

</details>

Numerics are unchanged: the tower output checksum is `4.776419` in every run,
including a reference run made with the checker disabled, so only the copy path
changed.

## Details

### Scope

Only the two implementations that materialise a dense mask are touched.
`VisionAttentionV2` splits the batch per segment instead of building a mask, and
the FlashAttention implementations pass `cu_seqlens` straight to the kernel, so
neither reads it on the host.

`VisionAttentionV2` keeps a `torch.diff(cu_seqlens).tolist()` fallback for
`seqlens is None`, but `prepare_meta()` always supplies the CPU-side `seqlens`
when it resolves to `eager_v2`, so that branch is defensive only and is left
alone here.

### Related work

Same class of host sync as #66243 (dots.ocr), which was fixed in #66390. The two
models do not share code, but they trip the same `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`
checker and take the same remedy (`async_tensor_h2d`), which the Qwen VL towers
(`qwen2_5_vl.py`, `qwen3_vl.py`) already use for their position ids.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the existing `async_tensor_h2d` helper and the
      established pinned-staging pattern; the mask change replaces a scalar loop
      with one vectorized comparison on the device.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** The change is validated end to end on real
      hardware with the checker armed, as shown above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Small, local changes; comments kept short.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Summary, root cause, scope limits and the
      before/after runs are all included above.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][gpt-oss] Split streamed MXFP4 experts in whole blocks across TP; keep the caller's w2_bias
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

gpt-oss reload fixes for direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) and weight transfer. PR 10 of the direct weight reload stack (#54477).

1. gpt-oss experts streamed one at a time (#52209) are split across TP the way the full-checkpoint loader splits them.
2. gpt-oss stops zeroing the caller's `w2_bias` tensor.

The FlashInfer bmm-scale and TRTLLM prefill k/v-scale fixes that were in this PR moved to their own PR (#68032).

## Claims

- **Streamed gpt-oss MXFP4 experts at TP > 1 now match a fresh start.** The per-expert loader narrowed each rank's slice by the parameter's padded size. The MXFP4 backends pad each rank's intermediate size, so every rank but rank 0 took the wrong checkpoint rows. It now splits in whole MXFP4 blocks, as `_load_weights_mxfp4` does. Unquantized and NVFP4 experts use the same split with a block size of 1.
  - gpt-oss-20b, TP2, direct reload through IPC, every expert sent under its own name: on main 240 expert tensors differ from a fresh start after every sync. With this PR none do.
- **A dimension of length 1 is not split.** A channelwise `w2_weight_scale` (one value per output channel) has no intermediate extent, so every rank loads it whole. On main, rank 1 got an empty slice. New test `test_streamed_channelwise_w2_scale_is_not_split[0,1]`.
- **gpt-oss no longer zeroes the caller's `w2_bias`.** On TP ranks other than 0 the three loaders (`mxfp4`, `quark`, `other`) called `zero_()` on the incoming tensor. Under IPC weight transfer that tensor is the trainer's buffer. They now use `torch.zeros_like`, in cold start, layerwise reload and direct reload alike. The change is mechanical and has no dedicated test: reaching these loaders needs a stubbed `GptOssModel` with parallel-state monkeypatches, which `tests/AGENTS.md` rules out.
- Small: the inverted `is_checkpoint_format` text in the kernel-format warning in `reload/inplace.py`.

## Validation

GB200, nightly wheels with each arm's Python files overlaid.

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py::test_streamed_mxfp4_expert_splits_like_the_checkpoint_loader[w13,w2]` (new; w13: TP rank 0 of 2, 4 blocks, padded to 3; w2 packed: TP rank 1 of 2, 3 blocks split 2 + 1) | 2 failed. w13: rank 0 also writes rank 1's rows into its padding. w2: rank 1's slice is empty | 2 passed |
| `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py::test_streamed_channelwise_w2_scale_is_not_split[0,1]` (new) | `[1]` fails (empty slice) | 2 passed |
| rest of `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py` | 9 passed | 9 passed |
| `test_direct_reload.py` | 37 passed | 37 passed |

Jobs 49811 (after merging main at 416ea4ef34: `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py` 13 passed on the PR / 10 on main, which lacks the new tests; `test_direct_reload.py` 37 / 37) and 50789 (this split, on aoshen02/vllm#321: `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py` 13 passed, `test_direct_reload.py` 37 passed). The code in this PR is identical to aoshen02/vllm#321.

**End to end: streamed MXFP4 experts.** gpt-oss-20b, TP2 (`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16`), `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, real IPC weight transfer. The trainer sends the checkpoint with every expert tensor under its own name (`...mlp.experts.<e>.gate_up_proj_blocks`, ...), 4923 names in all, as a trainer streaming one expert at a time does. "Differing" counts device tensors whose digest differs from a fresh real start.

| main | 240 / 240 | 240 |
| this PR | 0 / 0 | 0 |

- The streamed gpt-oss loader doesn't route the WNA16 zero-point / weight-shape / input-global-scale suffixes.

commits.pr_title: [RL][Model Loader] Direct reload: check that an update loaded every parameter
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) now checks at `finish_weight_update` that the update loaded every parameter cold start loaded. If any is missing, `finish` raises and names it, before post-load processing runs. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477, F2).

On main, a parameter the update leaves out keeps its runtime bytes. `begin` views them as checkpoint bytes, and `finish` reruns post-load processing over them. That is silent corruption whenever the processing changes the layout or isn't idempotent (transposes, requantization, packing). Padded MoE parameters are worse: `begin` zero-fills them (`padding_fill_params`), so leaving one out serves zeros.

## Design

- **Required:** the parameter names cold start's `model.load_weights` returned (`track_loaded_params`, recorded by `record_checkpoint_layout`).
- **Delivered:** the names this update's `load_weights` calls returned between `begin` and `finish`, plus the tensors written without `load_weights`:
  - M2N's in-place writes;
  - the load plan's direct copies (`load_planned`, #65235).
  
  Both report through `mark_loaded`. The load plan's trace of `load_weights` loads nothing, so it is kept out of the record.
- Names are resolved to parameter objects before comparing, so a tied parameter counts under either name. Fused and per-expert checkpoint names both count, because `load_weights` reports parameter names.
- **Exempt:** parameters matching `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`. Level 2 sleep keeps exactly the tensors an update doesn't rewrite, so they are the ones an update may leave out (e.g. the DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables). There is no new knob.
- **Dummy start:** cold start loaded nothing, so the first update sets the record and isn't checked itself. Requiring every parameter would reject correct updates, because some parameters are never sent: online-quantization scales are filled as a side effect of loading the weight, and fp8 KV-cache scales may be absent from the checkpoint.
- A `load_weights` that returns `None` turns the check off for that model.

**Not caught:** a partial shard or expert inside a parameter that the update did write, and wrong values. Checksums (#59371) cover values.

**Behaviour change.** Partial direct updates that ran on main now raise. For example, a trainer that keeps the vision tower frozen and doesn't send it must either send it or list it in `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`. After a refused finish the model needs a new full update, as after any failed finish.

Cold start, layerwise reload and non-direct mode are unaffected.

**Also fixed:** the NCCL trainer now resends its metadata after a failed update. Without that, the full update the error message asks for, sent after a refused one, was decoded with the refused update's names (see Validation).

## Validation

**Unit tests** (GB200, nightly 60bd6dd2 with each arm's Python files overlaid; PR vs main on the same node):

`test_direct_reload.py`, `test_load_plan.py`, `test_reload_lifecycle.py` and `test_reload.py` (job 51741, head 3e3b2df4da; same counts as job 51474 on 099ed99c13):

| Arm | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 173 | 1 |
| main ea8f3140ef | 170 | 1 |

The failure, `test_reload.py::test_kv_scale_reload`, is the same on both arms. The 3 extra passes are this PR's new tests.

- `test_direct_reload.py::TestUnsent`:
  - a parameter left out raises before post-load processing, and a following full update repairs the model;
  - after a dummy start the first update sets the record, and a later partial update raises;
  - a parameter matched by `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names` may be left out and keeps its bytes.
- `test_load_plan.py::test_planned_update_is_checked_for_completeness`: a full update through the load plan passes; one that leaves out a direct name raises.

`test_weight_transfer.py -k nccl` (job 51742): PR 76 passed, main 75 passed. The extra one is `test_nccl_trainer_resends_metadata_after_a_failed_update`, for the fix below.

**End to end** (GB200, same image and overlay as the unit tests; both arms run with `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`). Setup:

- A `vllm serve` with TP2, `--enable-sleep-mode` and the NCCL weight transfer (packed).
- One GPU plays the trainer, streaming the BF16 checkpoint.
- Every update runs the RL cycle: level 2 sleep, wake weights, pause, `start_weight_update` / NCCL broadcast / `finish_weight_update`, resume, wake KV cache.

Each successful step has GSM8K (chat, all 1319 questions, greedy) and per-parameter byte digests on every rank. The digests are compared with a real cold start; cold-start digests are identical across arms and jobs.

"Leave out" means the trainer does not send that one checkpoint tensor in that update.

Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (BF16 MoE), 870 parameters (435 per rank). PR at 3e3b2df4da: jobs 51712 and 51674 (preserve case). main ea8f3140ef: job 51675.

| Case | Arm | Updates (GSM8K after each; cold first) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 2: real start; full, leave out `layers.5.self_attn.o_proj.weight`, full | PR | 0.9196 → 0.9227 → refused → 0.9219 | Full updates: 0/870 digests differ. The partial update's `finish` raises `the update did not load 1 parameters cold start loaded (e.g. ['model.layers.5.self_attn.o_proj.weight'])` from `_check_update_complete`, before `process_weights_after_loading`. At that point the MoE `w13` and `w2` of all 48 layers on both ranks (192 tensors) are still in checkpoint layout: post-load processing did not run. The next full update repairs the model (0/870). |
| | main | 0.9181 → 0.9196 → **0.9204 (accepted)** → 0.9204 | The partial update succeeds silently. `o_proj` on both ranks no longer holds checkpoint bytes, and GSM8K does not show it. The next full update repairs it. |
| 3: dummy start; full, full, leave out, full | PR | – → 0.9181 → 0.9196 → refused → 0.9174 | The first update sets the record and passes; the second full update passes the check. The partial update is refused; the next full update repairs (0/870 vs the real cold start). |
| | main | – → 0.9212 → **0.9219 (accepted)** → 0.9219 | Silent, as above. |
| 4: real start, `use_load_plan`; full, leave out, full | PR | 0.9204 → 0.9196 → refused → 0.9196 | Same as case 2 through the load plan (direct copies report via `mark_loaded`). |
| | main | 0.9212 → 0.9204 → **0.9227 (accepted)** → 0.9189 | Silent. |
| 5: `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names model.layers.5.self_attn.o_proj.weight`; leave it out, full | PR | 0.9189 → 0.9257 → 0.9249 | Accepted. Level 2 sleep kept the bytes: 0/870 differ. |

Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (dense, `lm_head` tied to `embed_tokens`), 580 parameters, job 51713 (both arms):

| Case | Arm | GSM8K (cold → full → partial → full) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| leave out `layers.5.self_attn.o_proj.weight` | PR | 0.8878 → 0.8878 → refused → 0.8878 | Refused, naming it. Repaired (0/580). |
| | main | 0.8878 → 0.8870 → **0.8514** → 0.8863 | Accepted silently, corrupted. |
| leave out `embed_tokens.weight` (tied) | PR | 0.8855 → 0.8878 → refused → 0.8878 | Full updates pass, so the tied `lm_head` counts under `embed_tokens`. The partial update is refused, naming `model.embed_tokens.weight`. Repaired. |
| | main | 0.8855 → 0.8870 → **0.0** → 0.8878 | Accepted silently; the model outputs garbage. |

**Bug found and fixed (3e3b2df4da):** the repair after a refused update failed. On 4B it was refused again, still missing `o_proj`. On 30B it hung in the broadcast (job 51696).

The NCCL trainer recorded the metadata it sent only after `finish_weight_update` succeeded, but the workers cache the metadata of every update they receive. After a refused partial update, the next full update matched the metadata from before it and shipped empty update info. The workers then decoded the broadcast with the partial update's names.

The fix records the sent metadata before `finish`, and forgets it while an update with new metadata is in flight. Test: `test_weight_transfer.py::test_nccl_trainer_resends_metadata_after_a_failed_update`. Jobs 51696 / 51697 ran before the fix; the results above are after it.

**Pre-existing, not changed here:** with TP > 1, a worker RPC that raises leaves the other ranks' replies queued (`MultiprocExecutor.collective_rpc` raises on the first failed rank without dequeuing the rest). Every later collective RPC then reads the previous call's reply on those ranks. The first one, here the `resume` after the refused update, raises the stale error. Generation is unaffected (it reads rank 0 only), and the harness reads digests twice after a refusal. This needs its own fix.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KDA] Export Triton prefill checkpoints for Kimi-Linear
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let the shared Kimi GDN layer (`KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention`, used by Kimi-Linear and AliceAI) export align-mode prefill checkpoints from its Triton prefill, on the per-sequence buffer path of #67866 / #68106. With prefix caching on, a prompt is then no longer split at its last Mamba block boundary.

It also fixes an engine crash that Kimi-Linear hits on any prompt containing a tokenizer-only token id, which the random-dataset benchmark used to validate this change does.

Follow-up to #67866 and #68106. No open PR covers this layer's checkpoints. #53977 masks out-of-range ids inside `VocabParallelEmbedding` for spec-decode padding; it would hide this input bug as a silent zero embedding instead of rejecting the request, so it is not a substitute.

## Claims

- `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention` declares checkpoint alignment 64 and exports the checkpoint after its Triton prefill, through the shared helpers from #68106. It reserves the buffer only in `align` mode.
- The Kimi-K3 ROCm `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (which this layer calls on ROCm) forwards `checkpoint_state` / `checkpoint_offsets`; before, its `**kwargs` would have silently dropped them.
- Token ids past the model's vocab are rejected with a validation error for text-only models, instead of killing the engine.
- Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B TP1 on GB300: TTFT -22% / -23% / -15% at concurrency 1 / 4 / 16; gsm8k with prefix-cache hits unchanged.
- Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B TP1 on MI355X (ROCm KDA wrapper): TTFT -30% / -23% / -12% at concurrency 1 / 4 / 16.

## Out-of-vocabulary crash

Kimi-Linear's tokenizer has 163,842 ids (`<|reserved_token_163840|>`, `<|reserved_token_163841|>`), but the model's embedding has 163,840 rows. `validate_token_ids` accepted any id up to max(tokenizer, model) vocab, so a prompt with id 163,840 or 163,841 reached `F.embedding`, hit a device-side assert and killed the engine. Taking the max was meant for multimodal placeholders, which are replaced before the embedding lookup; the fix keeps it only for multimodal models.

## Validation

GB300:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/llm/test_prompt_validation.py
# 7 passed
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_checkpoint_exporter.py tests/kernels/fla
# 1932 passed, 7 skipped
```

- `test_token_past_model_vocab` (new) sends an id past the model vocab but inside the tokenizer vocab through `LLM`: on main it kills the engine (`EngineDeadError`), with the fix it raises `VLLMValidationError`.
- `test_triton_kda_checkpoint_correctness` now also runs the ROCm `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (on CUDA). Its checkpoints match a naive fp32 recurrence, and its output and final state match the run without checkpoints.

`moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` (BF16), 1x GB300, TP1, `--enable-prefix-caching` (align mode, block size 1920), 8192-token step budget. The baseline is main at `c84273be38` plus only the renderer fix, since main crashes on this benchmark; two fresh servers per arm, interleaved, mean of both.

| ISL 8000 / OSL 32, concurrency | TTFT ms, base → PR | total tok/s, base → PR | TPOT ms, base → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 117.7 → 91.7 (-22%) | 42,657 → 48,297 | 2.27 → 2.40 |
| 4 | 279.3 → 216.1 (-23%) | 72,328 → 79,490 | 4.94 → 5.74 |
| 16 | 576.0 → 490.1 (-15%) | 98,125 → 103,156 | 23.15 → 23.92 |

Without a checkpoint, the scheduler ends an 8000-token prompt's first step at 7680 (4 × 1920) to save the state, and the prompt needs a second step. With a checkpoint, it runs in one step. There were no prefix-cache hits in either arm. The random dataset samples the two reserved token ids, so 3 of 64 prompts at concurrency 4 and 12 of 256 at concurrency 16 are rejected by the fix in both arms; the table averages the completed requests. The unsplit prefill delays other requests' decode steps, so TPOT rises 16% at concurrency 4 and 3% at 16.

| `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 20` (fixed few-shot prefix, 54% of prompt tokens hit), 4 runs per arm | base | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| accuracy | 0.8901 / 0.8901 / 0.8893 / 0.8946 | 0.8954 / 0.8969 / 0.8931 / 0.8886 |

Same model on ROCm: 1x MI355X, TP1, BF16, same workload and flags. PR head `0c7f093b75` (this branch merged with main) against main `26acafd3a5` plus only the renderer fix; two fresh servers per arm, mean of both.

| ISL 8000 / OSL 32, concurrency | TTFT ms, base → PR | total tok/s, base → PR | TPOT ms, base → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 167.1 → 116.7 (-30.1%) | 27,619 → 33,430 | 3.87 → 3.89 |
| 4 | 328.9 → 255.0 (-22.5%) | 57,680 → 63,563 | 6.76 → 7.55 |
| 16 | 519.1 → 455.5 (-12.2%) | 82,471 → 86,662 | 33.10 → 32.72 |

TPOT at concurrency 4 rises 12% in both rounds, as on GB300. The prefix-hit counts are the same in all four servers (537,600 of 2,458,693 prompt tokens), and both arms complete and reject the same requests. Rejected reserved-token prompts get HTTP 400, and later requests still succeed. On MI355X, `test_triton_kda_checkpoint_correctness` passes (6 / 6); its two `kimi_amd` cases fail on main as expected. The other AMD KDA tests give 131 passed, 7 skipped in both arms.

`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` server on this branch: checkpointed prefills and prefix-hit resumes from the stored checkpoints (1920 / 3840 / 7680 cached tokens), no sync errors.

## Details

- Buffer: `max_num_seqs × local heads × 128 × 128` in the state dtype, reserved from the shared grow-only workspace. On MI355X this lowers the KV cache from 19.85M to 19.08M tokens (-3.9%).
- An unsplit prefill can delay other requests' decode steps in that step, as with FlashKDA.
- The token-id check made one existing test invalid: the predictable dummy model in `tests/v1/kv_connector/extract_hidden_states_integration` declared a 1000-token vocab but tokenizes with TinyLlama (32000 ids). Its vocab now matches the tokenizer.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation and the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Pixtral (HF): honor the processor's size override
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

For HF-format Pixtral checkpoints (`LlavaForConditionalGeneration` with a Pixtral vision tower, e.g. `mistral-community/pixtral-12b`), vLLM computes the image placeholder grid from `vision_config.image_size` and ignores the image processor's `size`. Passing `mm_processor_kwargs={"size": {"longest_edge": N}}` (flat or under `images_kwargs`) shrinks the image in the HF processor but not the placeholders, and the engine dies on the count mismatch. Mistral3 had the same bug and was fixed in #52874; this applies the same approach to Pixtral (HF).

## Claims

- With a `size` override, Pixtral (HF) requests now run, and vLLM's placeholder tokens are identical to the HF processor's.
- Default kwargs give the same placeholders as before (the checkpoint's `longest_edge` equals `vision_config.image_size`), and Mistral3 / LightOnOCR behave as before.

## Validation

End to end with `mistral-community/pixtral-12b` (bf16) on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (Colab), with the vLLM nightly wheel `0.34.0rc1.dev509+g0431c0f73` as main and the same install with this PR's diff applied. `LLM.chat(..., mm_processor_kwargs=kw)`, the `stop_sign` image asset resized to 1024x768, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=32`, a fresh process per kwargs set. HF: `AutoModelForImageTextToText` + `AutoProcessor` with the same kwargs, transformers 5.23.0.

| `mm_processor_kwargs` | HF prompt len | main | this PR: prompt len | this PR: text vs HF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{}` | 3131 | 3131 | 3131 | same description, wording differs from the 4th word (main's text is identical to this PR's) |
| `{"size": {"longest_edge": 512}}` | 803 | `EngineDeadError` | 803 | identical |
| `{"images_kwargs": {"size": {"longest_edge": 640}}}` | 1241 | `EngineDeadError` | 1241 | identical |

Root error on main (`longest_edge=512`):

```
ValueError: Attempted to assign 768 = 768 multimodal tokens to 3072 placeholders
```

New test, `test_pixtral_hf_processor_size_override` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py`. It compares the placeholder tokens from vLLM's prompt updates with the HF processor's, for `{}`, a flat `size` and a scoped `images_kwargs.size`, with kwargs at init and per request:

```
$ pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py -k pixtral_hf

# main
FAILED ...test_pixtral_hf_processor_size_override[True-mm_processor_kwargs1-768]
FAILED ...test_pixtral_hf_processor_size_override[True-mm_processor_kwargs2-768]
FAILED ...test_pixtral_hf_processor_size_override[False-mm_processor_kwargs1-768]
FAILED ...test_pixtral_hf_processor_size_override[False-mm_processor_kwargs2-768]
E         At index 32 diff: 10 != 12
E         Left contains 2328 more items, first extra item: 10
4 failed, 2 passed

# this PR
6 passed
```

With this PR, `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py -k "size_override or lightonocr or scoped"` passes (32 passed; this includes the existing Mistral3 size-override tests and `test_lightonocr_keeps_vision_config_image_size`), and so does `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k "pixtral or Mistral-Small-3.1 or LightOnOCR"` (12 passed). The ruff (check/format), mypy, typos and test-tethering hooks pass on the changed files.

CI: `tests/models/multimodal/processing` runs in the CPU `Multimodal Processing` step (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_multimodal.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause: `PixtralHFMultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates` built `PixtralHFEncoderInfo(hf_config)`, whose `get_image_size()` is `vision_config.image_size` (1024 for pixtral-12b). The HF `PixtralImageProcessor` resizes to `size["longest_edge"]` instead, so any `size` override changed the number of patches the vision tower produces but not the number of placeholders (for a 1024x768 image with `longest_edge=512`: 768 image tokens from HF, 3072 placeholders in vLLM).

Fix:
- `PixtralHFEncoderInfo` takes an optional `image_size` (default `vision_config.image_size`, so other callers such as `get_vision_encoder_info()` and LightOnOCR are unchanged).
- `PixtralHFProcessingInfo.get_vision_encoder_info(mm_processor_kwargs)` resolves `longest_edge` from the processor's `size` and the merged `mm_processor_kwargs`, exactly as `Mistral3ProcessingInfo.get_vision_encoder_info` does, and `_get_prompt_updates` uses it. Profiling (`get_image_size_with_most_features`) also follows an init-time `size` override.
- `Mistral3HFEncoderInfo` drops its own `__init__` / `get_image_size`, which the base class now provides.

The test sits next to the Mistral3 size-override tests and reuses their helpers, since both models use `PixtralProcessor`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EPLB][Hardware][Ascend] Set device_index for NPU in async EPLB worker
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Initialize `EplbState.device_index` for Ascend NPU (`device.type == "npu"`), matching the existing CUDA/XPU path, so async EPLB worker threads do not abort on `assert device_index is not None`.

Fixes #66377

## Claims

- Removes the NPU hole in the `device_index` allowlist (`("cuda", "xpu")` → `("cuda", "xpu", "npu")`).
- CUDA/XPU code path is unchanged aside from sharing the same allowlist.
- Diff is one device-type string (plus a short comment) in `EplbState.__init__`.

## Validation

**What was observed (pre-fix, production-like Ascend log):**

```text
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928) Exception in thread Thread-11 (thread_target):
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928) Traceback (most recent call last):
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928)   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/threading.py", line 1045, in _bootstrap_inner
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928)     self.run()
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928)   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/threading.py", line 982, in run
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928)     self._target(*self._args, **self._kwargs)
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928)   File "/opt/vllm/vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py", line 33, in thread_target
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928)     assert device_index is not None
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928)            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(Worker_TP2_EP2 pid=1928) AssertionError
```

- Same assert on all 16 local TP/EP ranks in that log (TP0–TP15).
- Correlates with upstream code: `device_index` is only set for `cuda`/`xpu`, so NPU leaves it `None` before `start_async_worker`.

**What this PR changes (code review):**

- With `"npu"` included, `device_index` is taken from `device.index` or `torch.accelerator.current_device_index()`, same as CUDA/XPU.

**Post-fix Ascend runtime (2026-11-09):**

- Topology: Ascend A3, 505B W4A8 PD disagg `4P8-1D8`, `--enable-eplb`, `eplb_config.use_async=True`, communicator `hixl`.
- Image note: deploy image field is still named `cuda_device_index` (1031-lineage); applied the **same allowlist change** as this PR: `device.type == "cuda"` → `device.type in ("cuda", "npu")` in container `/opt/vllm/vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py`. commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Probe AITER mHC support when the op is built, not at import
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, `mhc.py` imported aiter at module import to set three capability flags, and importing aiter initializes HIP. Quantization config lookup imports `mhc.py` in the API process, so for quantized models vLLM had to spawn EngineCore and its workers instead of forking them. This moves those probes into the op constructors, which run in the worker. Follow-up to #67821, which removed the other source of HIP initialization in ROCm tests.

**Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68089 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68090.** With aiter no longer initializing HIP in the API process, ROCm engines for quantized models fork instead of spawn, which exposes two fork-only bugs: stale AITER env flags in forked workers (#68089) and a HIP range-check bug in sleep-mode cuMem unmap (#68090). Without them `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool_aiter_fused_ar_group_quant` fails ([build 103307](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103307/list?jid=01a1e6f7-66d5-4e33-b27f-879f48c1962d)); with both, it passed 10/10 locally. Draft until they merge.

## Claims

- Creating an `LLM` for a quantized model on ROCm no longer initializes HIP in the API process, so EngineCore and workers fork ("We must use the `spawn` ... Reasons: CUDA is initialized" is gone)
- The probed values are unchanged on MI300X, and the ops' dispatch is unchanged; CUDA, XPU and CPU are untouched (`HAS_AITER_MHC` is False there)

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), local.

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_pp_equivalence_middle_stages` (PP=4), 3 runs each, Kolibri1 | median 157 s, spawns | median 82 s, no spawn |
| same, Ministral3 | median 137 s, spawns | median 65 s, no spawn |
| `kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py`, 10 runs | 83 passed, 3 failed | 83 passed, 3 failed (same 3 as before) |
| DSv4/DSv4.1 model and kernel tests on MI300 | | 439 passed, 14 skipped |

Probe values before and after on gfx942: `_has_aiter_mhc_fused()` True, `mhc_pre` and `mhc_fused_post_pre` accept norm True, the others unchanged. The three `test_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter[True-*]` failures are a tolerance miss in `MHCPreDelayedOp`, which this does not touch.

## Details

The HIP initialization comes from aiter itself: `aiter/ops/triton/utils/_triton/arch_info.py` runs `_probe_arch()` at import, which asks Triton for the current target. The chain from `LLM()` is `ModelConfig._verify_quantization` -> `get_quantization_config` -> `import vllm.models.deepseek_v41` -> `deepseek_v4/amd/dspark.py` -> `mhc.py`. `_has_aiter_mhc_fused` and `_aiter_mhc_op_accepts_norm` are now cached and called from `MHCPreOp.__init__` / `MHCFusedPostPreOp.__init__`; `forward_hip` reads instance attributes, which keeps the import out of the traced forward. The flags that never import aiter stay module-level. The tests construct the ops instead of patching the removed module constants.

No open PR changes how mhc.py probes aiter (searched `HAS_AITER_MHC`, `mhc aiter import`, `mhc lazy`).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] float64 reference + specialized decode format primitives (T1 of #68016)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

An AMD monokernel fuses most of a decoder layer into a single launch. When one comes out wrong, the symptom shows up far from the cause, and the checks we have today cannot localise it: they compare the monokernel against vLLM's own ops, and both sides reach for the same rounding and packing helpers. A shared bug cancels.

This adds the bottom layer of a float64 reference instead, so each piece is checked against a closed-form definition rather than against another implementation.

**Where this sits in the plan.** This is tier **T1 (primitives)** of the testing RFC, #68016. T1 is a *debugging aid*, not the numerical contract. It reaches into a model's internals on purpose, so it cannot survive a kernel rewrite. The contract is **T2 `DecodeNumerics`**, which compares a decode at its public entry point, sweeps widths, and holds however the kernel is written; it lands separately per that RFC. Reviewing T1 as "the specification" would be reviewing it for a job it is not meant to do.

Groundwork originally split out of #63486 so the reference library could be reviewed on its own rather than inside an 11k-line test rewrite. Follows #67073, which collected the monokernel steps into the file this wires into.

## Changes

Three files, in the layout #68016 asks for: the model-agnostic halves under `tests/models/common/specialized_decode/`, the DeepSeek-V4.1 half under the model's own test directory.

**`tests/models/common/specialized_decode/reference.py`** (new, 125 lines) - plain-torch float64 definitions of the formats the kernels use, written from the model definitions, never from a vLLM, AITER or Triton kernel. This is the formats and rounding half only:

| group | symbols |
|---|---|
| constants | `F64`, `FLT_MIN`, `E2M1_VALUES` |
| scale codes | `e8m0`, `ceil_code`, `mx_code_vllm` |
| dequant | `dequant_fp8` |
| rounding | `round_float`, `bf16_rne`, `f32_rne`, `to_e4m3_rne` |

The layer math (RMSNorm, RoPE, MLA, MoE) and the error metrics land here next, shared rather than once per model, so the `DecodeNumerics` contract measures every model the same way. Nothing is added without a caller in this PR: an earlier revision carried AITER's `e8m0_roundup6` rule, which only Kimi-K3 defines on the device side, so it matched nothing and has been dropped until that model lands.

**`tests/models/common/specialized_decode/primitives.py`** (new, 258 lines) - the machinery a primitive test needs, with no model in it: a `HelperSet` over a model's device modules, a thin map kernel that calls a helper on every lane, the input generators that make a rounding rule observable (the ties, the subnormals, the overflow edges), and an exact assertion.

Nothing here re-implements a rounding. `run` only moves words onto the GPU, hands them to the helper under test, and brings the result back.

It assumes only that the helpers are FlyDSL device functions a test kernel can call. A model whose kernels emit their instructions inline, with no callable helper to import, cannot be checked at this tier at all and relies on T2 plus a stage-level check instead.

**`tests/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono/test_primitives.py`** (new, 247 lines) - the DeepSeek-V4.1 half: which helpers to check and what to compare them against. It names its own helper sets and asserts against `reference.py`.

```python
_PKG = "vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono"
_LIBS = {
    "dsv41": H.HelperSet(_PKG, ("common.ops", "common.mx", "common.gfx942",
                                "stages.moe", "stages.seam")),
    "dsv41_attn": H.HelperSet(_PKG, ("attention.device",)),
}
```

The model carries two copies of these helpers, one on the MoE and seam side and one on the attention side, and each is checked on its own: a bug fixed in one is not fixed in the other. Another model's helpers belong in a file under its own `tests/models/<model>/` directory, over its own `_LIBS`, reusing both common files unchanged.

Every assertion is exact. Roundings, packings, scale codes and data movement have a closed form, so a tolerance would only hide a wrong one. The tolerance-bearing tests (transcendentals, reductions, MFMA) are not in this PR; they are #67977.

**`.buildkite/test_areas/monokernels.yaml`** - wired into both architectures, since the device helpers differ between them:

| step | agent | arch |
|---|---|---|
| `dsv41-mono-decode-numerics-amd` | mi355_4 | gfx950 |
| `dsv41-mono-decode-gfx942-amd` | mi300_1 | gfx942 |

Both steps already build `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`, so this is one more command, no new step and no new blocking reservation. Both gain `source_file_dependencies` for the three new files, and the MI300 step's command stays an explicit file list.

The test file opens with a module-level `current_platform.is_rocm()` guard (`allow_module_level=True`) plus `pytest.importorskip("flydsl")` and `pytest.importorskip("aiter")`, so on a box where either is missing the whole file skips and the blocking step still goes green. Both are present in the ROCm CI image, which is where the step runs. Flagging it because a silent skip on a blocking step is the failure mode this series exists to remove, and it should be a known cost rather than a discovery.

## Test plan

MI355X (gfx950), single GPU, after the move to the new layout:

```
10 tests collected
10 passed, 17 warnings in 31.67s
```

```
test_bf16_round_and_pack[dsv41]        test_bf16_round_and_pack[dsv41_attn]
test_fp8_clamp_and_pack[dsv41]         test_fp8_clamp_and_pack[dsv41_attn]
test_scale_codes[dsv41]                test_scale_codes[dsv41_attn]
test_fp8x8_bf16[dsv41_attn]            test_ocp_to_fnuz[dsv41]
test_fp4x8_fnuz[dsv41]                 test_scale_index[dsv41]
```

Nothing is `[NOTSET]`: every registered helper has a real case behind it, so no parametrisation is silently empty. The collected ids are byte-identical to the ones from before the harness split and before the move, so neither refactor changed what runs.

Earlier full runs on the pre-move file, same ten ids:

MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1ca0c` - 10 consecutive runs, `10 passed` each, 8.04s to 8.67s.
MI300X (gfx942), same image - 10 consecutive runs, `10 passed` each, 7.31s to 9.81s.

The gfx942 arm is not a second copy of the gfx950 one. `GFX942` is true there, so `FP8_MAX` is 224 and `test_fp8_clamp_and_pack`, `test_fp8x8_bf16` and `test_fp4x8_fnuz` compare against FNUZ E4M3 instead of OCP. Those paths had not been on hardware before this series.

And the step the file joins, `dsv41-mono-decode-gfx942-amd`, issued as CI issues it: `264 passed in 94.57s`. 254 of those are the seven files already in the step. Interleaved against those same seven without the new file: 113.7s and 84.4s before, 98.0s and 94.6s after. The difference is run-to-run noise, and the step's 30-minute timeout is nowhere near.

The assertions are not vacuous. Mutating the reference's bf16 mantissa width, FNUZ maximum, FNUZ exponent floor, `ceil_code` round-up and E8M0 exponent bias each made the corresponding test fail, and restoring each made it pass again.

Also clean: `pre-commit run --files` on all changed files (the `mypy` hook fails on main as well, on an unrelated `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/.../attn_fi.py` 3.10-syntax error), and `check_test_tethering.py` passes with the three new paths.

## Deliberately not in scope

- The tolerance-bearing primitives (transcendentals, reductions, MFMA) - #67977.
- T2 `DecodeNumerics`, the actual contract, and the CI gate that makes a specialized decode without one red - #68016.
- Three helpers in the author's version of this file (`test_fp4_dequant`, `test_fp4_quant`, `test_fp8x8_bf16_pk`) exercise device code that exists only in MiniMax-M3 and Kimi-K3. They land with their models.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Remove the failure mechanisms of two flaky tests
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes the failure mechanism behind two intermittently failing CI tests, one commit per test. Both still fail on main and on PRs as of 2026-11-16.

## Claims

- `test_memory_leak.py::test_consumed_cpu_inputs_released_during_generation`: no more setup errors with "pipeline model parallel group is not initialized".
- `responses/test_structured_output.py`: greedy decoding instead of sampled output under exact-match asserts.

No assertion is loosened.

## How often they fail

Counted from Buildkite logs of failed runs (ci.vllm.ai run lists), matching the test and its error, 2026-11-03 to 11-16:

| Test | CI step | Failures (main / PR) | Newest |
|---|---|---|---|
| memory_leak | (H200 MIG 35GB) Multimodal Models (Standard) 4 | 11 / 36 (≈0.5% of main runs) | 11-16, main |
| Responses structured output | (H200 MIG 35GB) Entrypoints Integration (Responses API) | 25 / 51 (≈4% of main runs since 11-06) | 11-16, main |

Every Responses failure is `test_structured_output_with_parse` asserting `'going to a science fair' == 'science fair'`. It started on 11-06; there were none on main on 11-03 to 11-05.

## Validation

**Memory leak**, RTX 4090 and H200 NVL, vLLM wheel of 83630ab85e, tests from that commit ("main") vs this branch ("fix"):

| Injection | main | fix |
|---|---|---|
| none | 2 passed on 4090; on H200 1 error in 7 runs (the CI error, unprompted) | 2 passed, 7/7 runs on H200 |
| old LLM released right after the new engine creates its parallel groups | **1 passed, 1 error**: `AssertionError: pipeline model parallel group is not initialized` | **2 passed** |

```bash
PYTHONPATH=<plugins dir> python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -p inject_late_release -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_memory_leak.py
```

<details>
<summary>inject_late_release.py</summary>

```python
import gc
import vllm.entrypoints.llm as llm_mod
import vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker as gw

HELD = []
_orig_init = llm_mod.LLM.__init__
def _init(self, *a, **k):
    _orig_init(self, *a, **k)
    HELD.append(self)
llm_mod.LLM.__init__ = _init

_orig_ensure = gw.ensure_model_parallel_initialized
def _ensure_then_release(*a, **k):
    _orig_ensure(*a, **k)
    if HELD:
        HELD.clear()
        gc.collect()
gw.ensure_model_parallel_initialized = _ensure_then_release
```
</details>

**Responses structured output**, server started with the test's args (Qwen3-1.7B, qwen3 reasoning parser, xgrammar), requests sent one at a time:

| Setup | Request | default sampling | `temperature=0.0` |
|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 4090, base 83630ab85e | both, 2000 total | 4/2000 failed | 0/2000 failed |
| H200 NVL, nightly 60bd6dd2e (11-16) | `parse` | 30/30 passed | 30/30 passed |
| H200 NVL, nightly 60bd6dd2e (11-16) | `create` | 30/30 passed | 30/30 passed |

Greedy returns `event_name="science fair"` on both GPUs. The 11-06 failure mode did not reproduce on the full H200 with default sampling in 60 requests, so this does not show the fix removes it on the CI MIG slice.

Limitations: CI runs both tests on H200 MIG slices, which were not available; the H200 runs used the full GPU.

## Details

**Memory leak test.** The fixture runs the engine in-process and leaves its shutdown to `InprocClient`'s `weakref.finalize`. `EngineCore.shutdown()` calls `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()`, which destroys the process-global parallel groups. If the last reference to the old `LLM` goes away while the next fixture's `LLM` is starting (between `ensure_model_parallel_initialized` and model runner construction), the old finalizer destroys the new engine's groups. In CI the first test passes and the second errors in setup with exactly this assertion. The fix calls `llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown()` in teardown, as other in-process tests do, which detaches the finalizer; `del` and `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` run in `finally` so a failing shutdown still releases the rest. The underlying hazard, a garbage-collected in-process engine tearing down process-global groups it no longer owns, is in `InprocClient`/`EngineCore.shutdown()` and affects other in-process tests too; it is left for a separate change. Limitation: on the 4090 the old engine is finalized right at `del llm`, so why the release comes late in CI is inferred, not observed; the fix does not depend on it.

**Responses structured output.** The tests check free-text fields exactly but sampled with Qwen3-1.7B's generation_config defaults (T=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20). Pinned to `temperature=0.0`, as other tests in that directory already are. Qwen3 advises against greedy decoding in thinking mode because it can loop; no loop was seen (greedy output ≤235 tokens). Since #66781 this file also runs against the Rust frontend, which passes `temperature` through to sampling; that path was not run.

**Not duplicating existing work.** Searched open PRs and issues for each test name and error string; none address these. Fixes for `test_prompt_logprobs_e2e_server` and the MoRIIO heartbeat test were dropped from this PR because neither has failed since late October.

**AI assistance** (Claude Code) was used for CI log mining, reproductions and drafting. This PR stays in draft until the submitter has reviewed every changed line and the validation above.
