commits.pr_title: [Direct reload] Flag padded params with fill_on_reload at construction
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

At begin, a direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`) zero-fills MoE expert padding that the loaders skip (#64352). Today the decision is a module method, `padding_fill_params()`. `record_checkpoint_layout` calls it once at cold start and snapshots the result as `(module, name)` pairs.

`MergedColumnParallelLinear` (`padding_size`, #66784) implements the same method for its output padding rows (Kimi-K3 KDA, Qwen4Exp hyper-connection).

This PR replaces both with a per-Parameter boolean, `fill_on_reload`, set when the layer is built. `begin_direct_reload` zero-fills every tensor the model owns that carries the flag. Part of the load plan work (#64418).

- **Same coverage as today.** The flag is set under the same conditions, on the same parameters: `RoutedExperts` with the same per-expert-scalar exclusion, and `MergedColumnParallelLinear` `weight`/`bias` when `padding_size > 0`.
- **Opt-in per layer.** Any layer whose loaders skip padding can set the flag on its Parameter at construction. No hook or method name to implement. Other layers (vocab rows, sinks) are left for later, model by model. See Known limitations (b).
- **The decision is made before post-load processing.** It is made at construction, which is before post-load processing rewrites `moe_config`, as the snapshot was. Nothing is stored on the model.

## Changes

- `RoutedExperts`:
  - `padding_fill_params()` becomes the private `_flag_padding_for_reload()`, which sets `p.fill_on_reload = True`.
  - It runs once, at the end of `__init__`, after `create_weights` and online staging. The flag is set on the Parameter object, never on a view, so `replace_parameter`, `.data` rebinds, sleep and EPLB keep it.
- `MergedColumnParallelLinear`: `padding_fill_params()` is removed. When `padding_size > 0`, the constructor sets `fill_on_reload = True` on `weight`, and on `bias` if present. The loader-side `_zero_output_padding` and `weight_loader_numel` stay.
- `FusedMoEFactory` gets an optional keyword `intermediate_size_unpadded` (last in the signature): the global size the checkpoint holds when `intermediate_size` is padded. The factory divides it by the MoE TP size of the `moe_parallel_config` it already builds (TP x DP x PCP without EP, the same divisor `FusedMoEConfig` uses for `intermediate_size_per_partition`) with `divide`, so an uneven split fails loudly. It passes the result as `intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded`. `FusedMoEConfig` is unchanged; when the argument is unset, the default is unchanged.
- Kimi-K3 (NVIDIA `model.py`, AMD `linear.py`):
  - On main, Kimi-K3 overrides `intermediate_size_per_partition_unpadded` after the experts are built, so construction sees no padding. Today's record-time snapshot still catches it; a construction-time flag would not.
  - Kimi-K3 now passes `intermediate_size_unpadded=moe_intermediate_size` to the factory, and the post-construction override is gone. The experts see their padding when they are built, so no caller re-flags.
  - This also changes what the unpadded per-rank size is divided by, from the attention TP size to the MoE TP group. With DP = PCP = 1 the value is the same as before. Backend support checks that run at construction (b12x MXFP4, Marlin) now see the real unpadded size instead of the padded one.
  - Pre-existing bugs in the construction-time zero of the padded experts, fixed in separate commits:
    - `FusedMoEFactory` returns the MoE runner, which doesn't forward expert params, so the zero of `w13`/`w2` was a no-op on NVIDIA and raised `AttributeError` on AMD when padded (TP >= 16 without EP).
    - It probed two param names and zeroed weights only. With W4A16 int4 experts the scales start at 1, so padded channels decoded to -8 instead of 0; other layouts (GPTQ/AWQ names) were skipped.
    - Both vendors now zero every param of `self.experts.routed_experts` that carries `fill_on_reload`, the same set and value `begin` zero-fills on reload.
  - AMD now skips the padding under EP, as NVIDIA already does. Before, TP16 + EP on ROCm (reachable after the fix above) built every expert at the padded size.
- `replace_parameter` no longer copies `fill_on_reload` from `new_tensor`, just as it doesn't copy `_ckpt`. A kept parameter keeps its own flag.
- `reload/direct.py`:
  - `record_checkpoint_layout` no longer builds `model._ckpt_padding_fill`.
  - In the same loop that restores loader attributes after the view-back, `begin` zeroes every owned tensor flagged `fill_on_reload`.
  - The delivery contract now says flagged params are zero-filled whole at begin.
- `reload/bake.py` and `test_load_plan.py`: fixes stale comments that said "post-load processing owns padding". `begin` zero-fills only flagged params; other constant writes a loader makes into padding run during the bake and are not redone on replays.

## Tests

- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_direct_reload.py`:
  - A flagged param with padding rows the loader skips, under layout-changing, non-idempotent post-load processing. Its padding is zeroed at begin, and the reload equals a cold start after both a real and a dummy start.
  - A sentinel buffer and an unflagged scale are untouched.
  - The flag survives `replace_parameter`.
  - `MergedColumnParallelLinear` with `padding_size > 0` flags `weight` (and `bias` when present); without padding nothing is flagged. The existing test from #66784 checks that begin zero-fills it and that the reload keeps addresses.
  - Control: an unflagged copy keeps stale bytes.
  - A flagged tensor shared from another model is not zeroed by that model's begin.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py`, on real fp8 `RoutedExperts`:
  - Round-up flags `w13_weight` and `w2_weight` but not the static per-expert scales.
  - Block-aligned TP (`tp_shard_with_padding`) also flags the block scales.
  - An unpadded layer flags nothing.
  - A layer built through `FusedMoEFactory` with `intermediate_size_unpadded` below `intermediate_size` (as Kimi-K3 now passes it) gets that per-partition unpadded size and flags `w13_weight` and `w2_weight` at construction; without the argument the default size is kept and nothing is flagged.
  - The Kimi-K3 call sites themselves are covered by the GPU run (tiny random Kimi-K3, TP2); building `KimiMoE` on CPU is too heavy for a unit test.
- `test_direct_reload.py`: `replace_parameter` doesn't copy a flag from a flagged `new_tensor`, and the kept parameter keeps its own.
  - The existing `test_direct_reload_after_dummy_start_resets_padding` passes unchanged.
- CPU (head node; the `dist_init` tests run with gloo):
  - `test_direct_reload.py`, `test_load_plan.py` and `test_stacked_shard_tracking.py`: 102 passed.
  - `test_fp8_tp_loading.py`, `test_utils.py`, `test_sharded_rdt_plan.py`, `test_triton_w4a16.py` and `qwen4_exp/test_hc_ops.py`: 226 passed, 10 skipped. The 13 failures are `test_hc_ops.py` GPU kernel tests; its padding test passes. The deselected `flashinfer_matches_unsharded` cases need NCCL/GPU.
  - Before the rebase, the 45 test files that build `FusedMoEConfig` or call `FusedMoEFactory` (`tests/kernels/moe`, `tests/lora`, `test_online.py`, `test_reload.py`, `tests/rocm/test_moe_padding.py`) gave the same results on CPU as on main.

## Validation

GPU matrix on GB200. Arm A is main and arm B is this PR, overlaid on the same nightly wheel, in the same job. The first three models ran with A = main `960f5c1bb1` and B = `ed6bef4581`, before the rebase onto main `379a8487a2` (after #66784); the rebase applied those commits unchanged and they don't touch the code paths those models take after it. Tiny Kimi-K3, whose code changed after review, was rerun at the current head `8a7a204650` with A = main `379a8487a2`. Each arm does a real start and a dummy start, then 3 NCCL updates of the same checkpoint per path: through the load plan (baked, then cached) and through `load_weights`, each without sleep and with sleep level 2. After every update, the per-tensor digests are compared with a fresh real start.

| Model (GB200, TP) | Padding exercised | Real start: plan / `load_weights` | Dummy start: plan / `load_weights` | A vs B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b (TP2) | MXFP4 round-up | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | identical |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 block (TP4) | block-aligned TP | 0 / 0 | attn `_k_scale`/`_v_scale` only* / same* | identical |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, shorter plan) | routed round-up | 0 / 0 | engram `embed_tokens` views and `_break_outputs` only† / not run | identical |
| tiny random Kimi-K3 (TP2) | TP round-up, unpadded size passed to the factory | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | identical; two cold starts also identical |

\* The KV scales are not in the checkpoint, so they keep their dummy values (#64352). This is the same on main.
† These are non-weight buffers that hold their dummy-start values, identically in both arms.

**Cold-start A/B.** A = main `960f5c1bb1`, B = this PR on the same commit (nightly wheel). Same node, arms back to back. GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1319 questions. Throughput: `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64.

| Model (hardware, TP) | GSM8K A → B | Throughput tok/s A → B | KV cache A → B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 block (GB200, TP4, Triton) | 0.8954 → 0.8954; swapped: 0.9007 → 0.8984 | 8600 → 8945; swapped: 8788 → 8961 | 7.283M → 7.283M |

The GSM8K gap stays within about 0.5 pt in either order (noise). Throughput is a little higher for B in both orders. This PR only acts at weight-update time, so a cold-start difference isn't expected.

Not covered on GPU: AMD Kimi-K3, which has no hardware on this cluster, and block-TP padding with an explicit `moe_backend`, where the block scales are zeroed (limitation b2).

## Known limitations

- **(a) Performance.** Some loaders pad the source tensor with `torch.cat` before copying, so the plan path still falls back to `load_weights` for those names. That is correct but slower. Affected: DeepSeek-V4/4.1 shared experts, GLM5-Next NoPE `kv_a`, Ling-3, dots3.
- **(b) Bit-identity.** On the plan path, padding the loaders skip is not reset after a dummy start or sleep level 2 unless its layer sets `fill_on_reload`. In this PR `RoutedExperts` and `MergedColumnParallelLinear` (`padding_size`: Kimi-K3 KDA, Qwen4Exp hyper-connection) do. Outputs are unaffected, and each layer can opt in per model later. Today's unflagged cases:
  - DeepSeek-V4/4.1 attention sinks. Their padding is −inf at cold start, so a whole zero fill would be wrong for them.
  - Vocab / `lm_head` padding rows.
  - Inkling padded expert slots and gate.
- **(b2) Loader fills on plan replays.** Some loaders write constants into padding during a load. The load plan runs these writes once, during the bake, and doesn't redo them on replays. This is pre-existing on main, where `padding_fill_params` fills the same params.
  - Flagged `RoutedExperts` params are zeroed at begin, so their padding stays 0 on plan replays. This includes the block scales under `tp_shard_with_padding`, which are 1 at cold start.
  - Unflagged loader fills, such as vocab rows, keep whatever bytes they hold.
  - Outputs are unaffected because the padded weights are 0, but bytes can differ from a cold start.
- **(f) Kimi-K3 pad decision with DP/PCP > 1 and no EP** (hao-aaron/vllm#17, pre-existing on main). The unpadded per-rank size now uses the MoE TP group. Kimi's decision whether to pad, and how far, still uses the attention TP size. So with DP/PCP > 1 and no EP, the padded per-rank size is `256 / (DP*PCP)` rather than the 256 minimum it targets. The validated recipes (TP8xDP2, TP4xDP4) don't pad.
- **(c) Prerequisite #65487.** The begin zero fill can race with side-stream packed NCCL loads, as today's fill can.
- **(e) Padded `MergedColumnParallelLinear` selects `weight`/`bias` by name** (pre-existing). A quantized padded layer (e.g. a W4A16 KDA `in_proj`) would fail at construction, and output-sharded scales would not be flagged. No shipped checkpoint quantizes these layers.
- **(d) Separate issue.** The compressed-tensors MoE `input_scale` destination check is out of scope here.

commits.pr_title: [CI][AMD] Run every AMD step when the ROCm image or AMD CI changes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Changing the files that build the ROCm test image doesn't run all of AMD:

- A `csrc/rocm/` change runs 21 of 256 AMD steps.
- A `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` change (e.g. #66596) runs every AMD mirror through a hardcoded ci-infra rule, but not the 21 standalone AMD steps (`device: mi*`), 6 of them optional. vllm-project/ci-infra#902 extends that rule to every AMD step, and to `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py`, the other file `build.sh` builds the ROCm stack image from.

AMD's run-all list (`amd_run_all_patterns`) only had `csrc/`. The generator also applied CUDA's skip list to it, and that list skips `docker/Dockerfile.*`, `csrc/rocm/` and `cmake/hipify.py`, so adding those files would have done nothing. vllm-project/ci-infra#902 fixes that skip list.

This PR:
- Adds the files that build the ROCm test image to `amd_run_all_patterns`:
  - `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` and `docker-bake-rocm.hcl`
  - `cmake/hipify.py`
  - `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/build.sh`
  - `requirements/rocm.txt` and `requirements/test/rocm.txt`
  - `tools/install_torchcodec_rocm.sh` and `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py`, which `build.sh` copies into the image
- Adds `amd_run_all_exclude_patterns: ["csrc/cpu/"]`.

CUDA's run-all and skip lists are unchanged. Optional steps run on a `Dockerfile.rocm_base` or `therock_wheels.py` change (from ci-infra#902), not on the other files here.

Notes for review:
- **Merge order:** either order works. This can merge before vllm-project/ci-infra#902; the current generator ignores the new key and only gains what CUDA's skip list allows (e.g. `requirements/rocm.txt`).
- **Left out on purpose:**
  - gfx1250 Dockerfiles, which the `ci` image doesn't use; that's why the Dockerfile patterns end in `$`.
  - `run-amd-test.sh` and `amd_ci_*`, which ci-infra already handles for native AMD steps (`AMD_NATIVE_RUNTIME_SOURCE_DEPENDENCIES`).
  - `ci_config_rocm.yaml`.
  - `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`: ci-infra#902 runs every AMD step on it, optional ones too, so an entry here adds nothing; on ci-infra `main` CUDA's skip list (`docker/Dockerfile.`) voids it anyway. `therock_wheels.py` is in both places on purpose: until ci-infra#902 merges, the entry here is what runs AMD on it.
  - `.buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml`: it defines the AMD steps and isn't part of the image. A change there runs only the 2 AMD image steps that run on every build.
  - `tools/ci/rocm_kernel_symbol_map.py`: not part of the test image. The steps in `test_areas/docker.yaml` already list it, so a change there runs its AMD mirror plus those 2 image steps (3 in all).
- **Shared image inputs** (`rust/`, `pyproject.toml`, `vllm/envs.py`, `.dockerignore`) stay off the list: they don't run all of CUDA either, and AMD mirrors inherit the CUDA step's `source_file_dependencies`, so the same steps run on both.
- **Conflict:** #65881 (draft) adds `CMakeLists.txt` to the same list; expect a trivial conflict.

## Test Plan

1. Feed this `ci_config.yaml` to the matching functions `init_global_config` uses, from ci-infra `main` and from vllm-project/ci-infra#902, one changed file at a time.
2. Run the full pipeline generator on this branch with one file changed, with both ci-infra versions, and count the AMD steps it runs.

## Test Result

| changed file | run_all | AMD run-all (ci-infra main) | AMD run-all (ci-infra#902) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm` | False | False | **True** |
| `csrc/rocm/attention.cu` | False | False | **True** |
| `cmake/hipify.py` | False | False | **True** |
| `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py` | False | True | True |
| `requirements/rocm.txt` | False | True | True |
| `tools/install_torchcodec_rocm.sh` | False | True | True |
| `csrc/attention/a.cu` | False | True | True |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` (ci-infra#902 rule, below) | False | False | False |
| `tools/ci/rocm_kernel_symbol_map.py` | False | False | False |
| `.buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml` | False | False | False |
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base_gfx1250` | False | False | False |
| `docker/Dockerfile.cpu` | False | False | False |
| `csrc/cpu/a.cpp` | False | False | False |
| `vllm/envs.py` | False | False | False |
| `docker/Dockerfile` | True | False | False |

Full generator, AMD steps run / not run:

| changed file | ci-infra main | ci-infra#902 |
|---|---|---|
| `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` | 233 / 23 | **254 / 2** |
| `tools/vllm-rocm/therock_wheels.py` | not measured | **254 / 2** |
| `csrc/rocm/...` | 21 / 235 | **189 / 67** |
| `tools/ci/rocm_kernel_symbol_map.py` | not measured | 3 / 253 |
| `.buildkite/hardware_tests/amd.yaml` | not measured | 2 / 254 |

CUDA steps are identical. The 2 left on a stack change are Zen CPU steps, which are not ROCm steps; the 67 on `csrc/rocm/` are those 2 plus the 65 optional AMD steps. `run_all` is the same under both generators, and every listed pattern names a file on `main`. Not yet seen in Buildkite: this PR changes none of the listed files, so the first ROCm-image PR after both merge is the real check.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Ray] Keep EngineCore's SIGTERM handler across ray.init()
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`ray.init()` replaces EngineCore's SIGTERM handler, so a SIGTERM from the frontend skips vLLM's graceful shutdown and Ray's C++ failure handler aborts EngineCore 3 s later. When the abort lands before `RayExecutorV2.shutdown()` kills the actors, the Ray workers outlive the engine and keep their GPU memory. This restores the caller's handler after `ray.init()`.

## Claims

- EngineCore with the Ray backend shuts down through its own SIGTERM handler, aborting requests and killing the Ray actors, instead of `sys.exit()` plus a SIGABRT 3 s later
- No `RayWorkerProc` is left holding GPU memory after a Ray-backend engine is terminated
- Unchanged for callers without a Python SIGTERM handler (plain scripts, in-process `LLM`) and for callers that initialized Ray themselves

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), local, 2 GPUs, same command before and after:

```bash
cd tests
TARGET_TEST_SUITE=MI300 pytest -v -s basic_correctness/models/test_basic_correctness.py -m 'distributed(num_gpus=2)' -k ray
```

| | Result | Leaked `RayWorkerProc` | Shutdown path |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 3 failed, 1 passed (memory-settle timeouts) | 2 (about 137 GiB each) | Ray `*** SIGTERM received`, EngineCore exit -6 |
| After, 10 runs | 4 passed every run, 333-405 s | 0 | vLLM `trigger received signal=SIGTERM` (4/4 per run) |

The `-k mp` cases of the same test still pass (4 passed). A standalone repro without GPUs (Python SIGTERM handler, `ray.init(num_cpus=1)`, SIGTERM to self) shows the same thing: before, the handler is replaced, `SystemExit(15)`, exit -6 after 3 s and 8 orphaned Ray processes; after, the handler runs, `ray.shutdown()` is clean, exit 0, no orphans.

## Details

`run_engine_core` registers vLLM's SIGTERM handler before the engine is built. `RayExecutorV2` then calls `initialize_ray_cluster` -> `ray.init()`, which installs `sys.exit(signum)` as the SIGTERM handler (`ray/_private/worker.py`) and abseil's FailureSignalHandler through the core worker (`core_worker_process.cc`), whose default `alarm_on_failure_secs = 3` aborts the process 3 s after SIGTERM. `RayExecutorV2.shutdown()` joins the monitor thread (up to its 5 s `ray.wait` poll) before `ray.kill()`, so the abort often wins. The fix reads the SIGTERM handler before `ray.init()`, only when this call starts Ray and runs on the main thread, and puts it back afterwards if it is a Python callable. Crash-signal handlers stay with Ray.

Leaked workers then live forever when PID 1 does not reap the killed raylet: Ray workers watch the raylet with `kill(pid, 0)`, which treats a zombie as alive. That is how it showed up on a node whose PID 1 is `sleep infinity`; with a reaping init the workers exit, which is why CI rarely sees it. The DP actor manager's own `ray.init()` in `vllm/v1/engine/utils.py` is not covered here and is being looked at separately.

No open PR restores the handler (searched `ray.init SIGTERM`, `RayExecutorV2 shutdown`); #45328 changes the same shutdown path for a different case.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Lock every render node for multi-GPU DPX jobs
commits.pr_body:
The DPX guard in `run-amd-test.sh` assumed exactly one render device and locked only that one. That rejects multi-GPU DPX jobs, which expose one render node per claimed partition. This change:

- Accepts a render-node count equal to `VLLM_CI_EXPECTED_GPU_COUNT` (`$gpus`), instead of requiring exactly one.
- Checks that each `/dev/dri/renderD*` node is a character device.
- Takes an exclusive `flock` on every node, keeping each descriptor open for the job's lifetime.

The lock runs for any agent queue whose name contains `dpx`. A 2-GPU queue such as `mi300_dpx_2` is covered when its jobs set `VLLM_CI_EXPECTED_GPU_COUNT=2` and the pod has two render nodes. One-GPU jobs still lock their single node. This still guards against a mismatch; for example, a one-GPU job whose pod exposes two render nodes is still refused.

cc: @AndreasKaratzas

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Keep a guard granule after each sleep-mode cuMem reservation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, `hipMemUnmap` and `hipMemSetAccess` fail with `hipErrorInvalidValue` when a `hipHostRegister`'ed buffer starts exactly at the end of the range ([ROCm/rocm-systems#15169](https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/issues/15169), open). Sleep mode creates such buffers itself, so `sleep()` or `wake_up()` can fail at `cumem_allocator.cpp:274` / `:224`. This reserves one extra unmapped granule after each cuMem allocation so nothing can start there, as torch_memory_saver did ([fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver#120](https://github.com/fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver/pull/120)).

## Claims

- ROCm sleep mode no longer fails with `CUDA Error: invalid argument at csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp:274` when a pinned CPU backup (or an RCCL host buffer) lands right after a cuMem allocation
- Costs one minimum-granularity page of address space per allocation (4 KiB on MI300X), no VRAM; the CUDA path is unchanged

## Validation

MI300X (gfx942), local, extension rebuilt from this source with the original flags.

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_sleep_cudagraph_pool_aiter_fused_ar_group_quant` with forked workers (#68027 + #68089) | 4/4 failed at `:274` | 10/10 passed |
| same, `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` | 1 of 8 failed (at `:224`) | 1/1 passed |
| whole `basic_correctness/memory/sleep_mode/test_sleep_mode.py` | | 17/17 passed |
| Standalone HIP repro (no vLLM): host page registered right after a mapped 2 MiB VMM range | `hipMemSetAccess`/`hipMemUnmap` return 1 | with the guard, both return 0 |

## Details

`hipMemUnmap`/`hipMemSetAccess` validate the range with `ValidateSubBufferCoverage` (clr `hip_vm.cpp`), which walks HIP's allocation map past the range end. A `hipHostRegister` buffer that starts exactly there is counted into the covered size, so the check fails silently (no log at `AMD_LOG_LEVEL=1`; the HSA unmap is never called). In vLLM the neighbour is the pinned CPU backup that `CuMemAllocator` mmaps and registers during `sleep()`: `/proc/self/maps` at the failure shows the backup's anonymous mapping starting at the first byte after the failing cuMem range. Forked workers hit it most often because they inherit the parent's address-space layout (it surfaced once #67821 and #68027 made ROCm workers fork), but spawned ones hit it too. `my_malloc` now reserves `alignedSize` plus one minimum granule, and `python_unmap_and_release` frees and re-reserves the same size for the sleep placeholder; other frees release the whole reservation by its base address. `vllm/utils/vmm_driver.py` (extensible KV cache) makes the same HIP calls without a guard; not changed here. #59228 and #65728 touch the same allocator for other issues.

No open PR addresses this (searched `15169`, `hipHostRegister sleep`, `cumem guard`).

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Skip the memory-settle stability wait when the GPU is idle
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, `wait_for_memory_to_settle()` in `tests/utils.py` requires device memory to stay below the threshold for 2 s, so each call costs at least 2 s even when the GPU is idle. It runs before every `VllmRunner`, after every `HfRunner` and after every `tests/models/test_initialization.py` case. This PR makes it return at once when every device is at the ROCm idle footprint.

## Claims

- On ROCm, a settle wait on an idle GPU returns after one reading instead of taking about 2 s. A wait that starts above the idle footprint keeps the 2 s stability window, and the threshold check is unchanged.
- CUDA and XPU behaviour is unchanged: only ROCm passes the new `idle_bytes` argument.
- Expected CI saving: in the logs of one recent job from each of the 40 most expensive AMD groups in vllm/ci (70% of AMD machine-hours), the settle wait took 922 s over 444 calls, 2.6% of job time, and 98% of the calls started with every device at or below 4 GiB. At the run rates of the last 7.65 days, that is about 75 machine-hours a day in those groups, and roughly 100 across AMD CI.

## Validation

Environment: the newest AMD CI image, `rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1bfc0-1ae0-47f3-8907-320230ec2f3d` (amd-ci build 15795, main `b389f03`), with this PR applied as a patch. Before and after ran at the same time in two containers on one MI300X each. One run per row (n=1) on a shared machine.

Commands run:

```bash
pytest -v -s models/test_initialization.py -k "test_can_initialize_large_subset and (PhiForCausalLM or BertModel or Blip2 or Afmoe or Whisper or Moondream)"
pytest -v -s basic_correctness/models/test_basic_correctness.py -k "test_models and Gemma2 and uni"
pre-commit run --files tests/utils.py
```

| Test | Result (before / after) | Settle waits | Time in the wait (before → after) | pytest time (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test_can_initialize_large_subset`, 12 cases | 12 passed / 12 passed | 12 | 24.7 s → 0.7 s | 292.4 s → 272.8 s |
| `test_basic_correctness.py::test_models`, 4 cases (`VllmRunner` and `HfRunner`) | 4 passed / 4 passed | 12 | 24.0 s → 0.0 s | 283.3 s → 259.6 s |
| `pre-commit` | | | | all hooks passed |

The wait time is the sum of `dur_s` in the helper's `Done waiting ...` lines.

A logic check with faked memory readings (not committed) gives:
- Idle (0.56 GiB) and 3 GiB: one reading.
- Steady at 10 GiB (under the threshold, above idle): still the 2 s window.
- 60 → 30 → 0.5 GiB: returns at the idle reading.
- A 64 GiB MI250 with a 0.05 ratio (3.2 GiB threshold): 3.5 GiB does not return early.

Without this PR, the four cases whose behaviour changes fail that check, and the steady case passes.

CI coverage: the helper runs in every AMD job that uses `vllm_runner`, `hf_runner` or the initialization tests. No model output changes.

## Details

- The stability window, added in #45490, waits for VRAM that ROCm releases lazily after a process exits. ROCm's memory reading lags a release, so it can read high after memory is freed, but not low while memory is held. When every device already reads at or below the idle footprint, nothing is resident, so there is nothing to wait for.
- The idle footprint is the 4 GiB bound `wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear` already applies on ROCm, where about 2.5 GiB stays resident on an idle MI300. It is now one constant, `ROCM_IDLE_FOOTPRINT_BYTES`, used in both places.
- The early return also requires every device to be under the threshold, so it never relaxes the threshold. For example, on a 64 GiB MI250 with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`, the 3.2 GiB threshold is below the idle footprint and still applies.
- Limitation: a process left over from an earlier test that starts allocating after an idle reading is no longer waited for. The stability window covered that case only if the allocation started within those 2 s.
- Not validated here: MI355 and MI250 hardware, multi-GPU jobs, and repeated runs. The file rules of 34 of the 251 AMD steps match `tests/utils.py`, so this PR's own CI covers only those; a full AMD run (`/amd-ci run all`) covers the rest.
- Related, not overlapping: #55830 (XPU) scopes the wait to the engine's own devices. It changes the call sites, not these lines.
- Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `wait_for_memory_to_settle` and `stable_duration_s`. None changes the stability window.
- AI assistance: this change and this description were prepared with an AI coding assistant (Cursor). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Skip the Omni audio-in-video host read without audio and video
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Qwen3-Omni's `embed_input_ids` copies `input_ids` to the host on every step with multimodal embeddings, to detect interleaved audio-in-video. Since #64176 the ROCm test image runs with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, so the daily run fails `generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py::test_ppl[aiter_on-False-model_info4-...]` (Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B) on MI355 ([build 103214](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103214/list?jid=01a1e5dc-1b90-43ef-a4e4-79e687b7c2dd&tab=output)) with `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:1874`. This PR reads `input_ids` only when the step can actually hold interleaved audio-in-video. It also builds the Qwen3-Omni encoders' lengths on the host, which removes the remaining per-request encoder syncs, including an unwrapped one that fails every Qwen3-Omni audio request under the sync check.

## Claims

- New helper `may_interleave_audio_video` returns whether a batch can hold interleaved audio-in-video, judged from the modality the encoder gather already tags on each embedding. It needs both audio and video embeddings; untagged embeddings count as possibly interleaved.
- Qwen3-Omni, Qwen2.5-Omni and LFM3-Omni skip the host read of `input_ids` when it is false: image-only, video-only, audio-only and text steps.
- In Qwen3-Omni, the remaining read for steps with both audio and video is now an allowed sync (`gpu_sync_allowed()`), as Qwen2.5-Omni and LFM3-Omni already do.
- Qwen3-Omni encoders (second commit): `max_seqlen` for the vision and audio attention, and the audio tower's chunk and output lengths, come from the CPU-side `grid_thw` and `audio_feature_lengths` instead of GPU tensors. That removes one sync per encoder layer and the audio tower's syncs. It also removes `audio_features.split(audio_output_lengths.tolist())` in `_process_audio_input`, which was not wrapped and failed every Qwen3-Omni audio request under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Qwen3-ASR shares that audio tower and gets the same change. Qwen2.5-Omni's split sizes also come from the host.
- Qwen3-Omni syncs per request, measured with the allow-list disabled:

  | Request | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | image or video | 27 | 0 |
  | audio | 38 | 0 |
  | audio-in-video | 66 | 1 |

  The one left is the interleave read; follow-up #68200 removes it.
- Outputs are unchanged. Each model skips the read only when the old token-based check would have returned "not interleaved" anyway, and the host-side lengths equal the device values (bit-identical outputs below).

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest "tests/models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py::test_ppl[aiter_on-False-model_info4-32-extra_kwargs4]"` (the CI failure) | fails: `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:1874` | passes |
| `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py -k "model_info3 or model_info4"` (Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-Omni, all AITER and eager variants) | — | 12 passed |
| `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation_ppl_test/test_qwen.py -k model_info2` (Qwen2.5-Omni) | — | 6 passed |
| `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_embed.py` (CPU-only, incl. the new `test_may_interleave_audio_video`) | — | 23 passed |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py` (incl. the new `test_qwen3_omni_audio_encoder_has_no_gpu_sync`, which fails if the old mask indexing is restored) | — | 7 passed |
| Qwen3-Omni offline run, 8 prompts in one batch (image, two images, 8-frame video, audio, two audios, a 31.7 s audio, audio-in-video, image+audio), with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | fails at `qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py:1614` | passes, token ids and top-5 logprobs bit-identical to main |
| Qwen3-Omni audio encoder alone, 36 length sets × FLASH_ATTN / TRITON_ATTN / TORCH_SDPA, device lengths vs host lengths | — | bit-identical |
| Multimodal processing tests for Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen3-Omni, Qwen3-ASR and audio-in-video, plus Qwen3-Omni/ASR mrope tests | — | 162 passed |

## Details

- **Root cause:** the interleave check needs the token ids of the multimodal positions, and `input_ids` lives on the GPU. `is_multimodal` is already a host tensor (pinned, from the encoder runner), so the `.cpu()` copy of `input_ids` was the only device read. It ran on every step with multimodal embeddings, although interleaving needs both audio and video in the same step.
- **Fix:** the encoder runners (GPU and CPU) already tag each gathered embedding with its modality through `set_mm_embedding_modality`, which the interleaved merge relies on. The helper uses those tags, so no runner or interface change is needed.
- **Encoder lengths:** vision `max_seqlen` uses the per-frame `cu_seqlens` already built from `grid_thw` in NumPy, as Qwen2.5-VL does. The audio tower takes `feature_lens` and `aftercnn_lens` on the host. It replaces the boolean-mask gather with an `index_select` whose indices are built on the host, so the row order is unchanged. An out-of-tree caller that passes device lengths to `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder` directly would now get a device-mismatch error instead of a hidden sync.
- Qwen2.5-Omni's other audio syncs are inside the transformers audio encoder and stay allow-listed.
- **Steps with both audio and video** still read `input_ids`, since interleaved positions can't be told apart without the token ids. Removing that read would mean threading per-modality masks through `embed_input_ids`, which the modality tags were introduced to avoid.
- The helper lives next to `check_interleaved_audio_video` in `qwen2_5_omni_thinker.py`, which all three Omni models already import from.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this code. #62494 removes a different sync, in the Qwen3-Omni audio encoder.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: B300 PD preset serves the released DSpark draft, align with InferenceX#5108
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This updates the `b300_agentx_pd` preset (added in #67722) for [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#5108](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5108). That PR runs the same B300 Dynamo + vLLM disaggregated AgentX lane with the released DSpark draft `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark`. InferenceX's golden AL curve now comes from that draft.

## Changes

- **Draft revision.** Since #67807, the `spec_decoding` feature names `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark`. The preset still pinned the preview draft's revision `6a2ef20a` on top of it. It now pins the released draft's revision `e4e6e626`.
- **Prefix-match unit.** The released draft adds a sliding-window KV group. If `--prefix-match-unit` differs from that group's block size, vLLM turns off partial prefix-cache hits for the whole hybrid KV cache, and next-turn Mooncake store hits drop. The preset sets 1408, the block size with 4 draft tokens, and 1536 at 1 client, the block size with 7 draft tokens. The previous unit was 128.
- **Tradeoff.** Prefix-cache hits now align to 1408 or 1536 tokens instead of 128, so each turn recomputes up to one more unit of its prompt. Without the matching unit, hits align to the 11264-token scheduler block instead, and the store keeps no partial tails.
- **Runbook.** The runbook names the released draft. The synthetic-acceptance commands use the current golden AL: 3.46 at 4 draft tokens and 4.16 at 7.

## Validation

- From #5068 to #5108, only these two settings change in the InferenceX recipe. This PR changes the same two settings in the preset.
- The preset as the builder renders it (this PR's preview, `presets/b300_agentx_pd.json`) matches the prefill and decode args and env of every #5108 point. The builder leaves out `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE`, `NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE`, `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE` and `VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM` on B300 (it keeps them for NVL4 trays only); the runbook lists them with their values.
- Against the merged #67722 preset, the rendered commands differ only in `--prefix-match-unit` and the draft revision.
- The server logs on the pinned image show the draft group's block size: `kv cache group sizes (1408, 1408, 1408, 11264, 1408)` with 4 draft tokens and `(1536, 1536, 1536, 12288, 1536)` with 7. With the matching unit, the log no longer prints `Disabling fine-grained prefix-cache hits`.
- InferenceX#5108's sweep ([run 44024134778](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/44024134778)) passed at all six points. Its GSM8K evals served the released draft with real block verification: strict match 0.9795 (48 clients), 0.9788 (64) and 0.9788 (264); the 660-client eval is still running.
- `Recipes / Validate` passes.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Decide the sparse MLA prefill route once in the metadata builder
commits.pr_body:
## Overview A sparse MLA prefill runs one of three ways: dense MHA, masked MHA, or sparse MQA (the top-k kernel that decodes use). Today three places each decide part of that choice: - the metadata builder (`use_dense_mha`); - `MLAAttention._use_sparse_mha`, at every layer call; - `SparseMLACommonImpl.forward_mha` (`prefill_max_seq_len <= topk_tokens`). Seven other places read or re-derive it. This PR makes the metadata builder decide once per metadata build and store the result in `SparseMLAPrefillMetadata.route`. Every consumer reads that field. Serving behavior does not change. ## Background: the three prefill routes For causal, sink-free sparse MLA, all three compute the same attention in exact arithmetic: each query attends only to its top-k keys chosen by the indexer. They differ in the kernel, and in rounding and query quantization (sparse MQA can take an fp8 query). Models with learnable sinks (HY-V4) need sparse MQA and force it. | Route | Kernel | Keys per query | When | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `SPARSE_MQA` | Absorbed MLA: q is projected into the latent space and one shared latent KV is gathered by top-k index (the kernel decodes use). Reads the compressed, possibly fp8, cache. | its top-k | The fallback when no other route applies, and always for decodes. | | `DENSE_MHA` | KV is decompressed per head with `kv_b_proj`, then causal MHA with no top-k mask. | all causal keys | Every prefill in the step has `seq_len <= top-k`, so the top-k already contains every causal key and no mask is needed. | | `MASKED_MHA` | Same decompressed MHA on FA4, with a per-query bit mask built from the top-k indices (`_build_topk_mask`, applied through FA4 `mask_mod`). | its top-k | Long prefills where the MHA kernel is faster: SM100 + FA4, a supported head geometry, unquantized KV, DCP = 1, inside the measured `_MASKED_MHA_THRESHOLDS`, and the mask fits the workspace. | The mask in `MASKED_MHA` selects keys; it is not a padding mask. Results agree mathematically across routes, not bitwise (different matmul order and rounding). A step's tokens are laid out as `[decodes | prefills]`, split at `num_decode_tokens`. Decodes always take sparse MQA: with one query per request (plus speculative tokens), decompressing their keys for MHA costs more than it saves, as in every MLA backend. The route only says what the prefill segment takes; `SPARSE_MQA` means it runs in `forward_mqa` like the decodes (in the same call, except under ShardQ, which dispatches the decode and the token-sharded prefill rows separately). It is decided per metadata build from the prefill maxima (longest sequence and longest query, which may come from different requests) and the rules below. A step without prefills has no route, and so does a step on a layer without a prefill backend (for example FlashInfer SM120): there is no prefill metadata, and prefills run sparse MQA as before. ## Before and after Before, the choice is split across three places, and readers re-derive parts of it: ```mermaid flowchart TD B["Builder
use_dense_mha = max_seq <= topk
and not (PCP and DCP > 1)"] L["Layer, every call: _use_sparse_mha()
HiSparse / ShardQ / no prefill -> False
masked = impl.masked_mha_available and DCP <= 1
and thresholds and workspace fits
return (use_dense_mha or masked) and not force_mqa"] F["forward_mha()
max_seq <= topk ? dense : masked"] B --> L L -- True --> F L -- False --> MQA["forward_mqa (all tokens)"] F --> D1["dense MHA"] F --> M1["masked MHA"] B -. reads use_dense_mha .-> IDX["indexer short-prefill skip"] B -. reads use_dense_mha .-> ROCM["ROCm planner"] L -. calls the layer's private method .-> SM90["FlashInfer SM90 planner"] Q["quant-output fusion check
max_seq <= topk"] ``` After, the builder decides once per metadata build; every reader reads `prefill.route`: ```mermaid flowchart TD R["Builder: _prefill_route(), once per build"] --> P["prefill.route"] P --> L2["Layer: route != SPARSE_MQA ? forward_mha : forward_mqa"] L2 --> F2["forward_mha: DENSE_MHA -> dense, MASKED_MHA -> masked"] P --> I2["indexer skip: route == DENSE_MHA"] P --> S2["FlashInfer SM90 / ROCm planners"] P --> Q2["quant-output fusion: route == DENSE_MHA"] ``` ## New structure One enum, one field and one builder method, all added by this PR. The rest of the diff removes or moves code, except the builder's backend-name lookup, the ShardQ split moved ahead of the route decision (so the route sees it), a benchmark override that forces a route, and test updates. - `SparseMLAPrefillRoute`: the three routes above. - Why a new type: the route has three values. Before, they were spread over a builder bool (`use_dense_mha`), a per-layer check (`_use_sparse_mha`) and a length test inside `forward_mha`, and no single value said which path runs. Extending the old bool would need a second bool plus rules about which pairs are valid. - `SparseMLAPrefillMetadata.route`: carries the decision from the builder to every reader. It is a required field, so a builder that forgets to set it fails at construction instead of silently falling back. - `SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder._prefill_route()`: the only place the routing rules live. It applies them in this order; the first match wins: | # | Rule | Route | Why | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, HiSparse, or ShardQ this step | `SPARSE_MQA` | Force-MQA is a user override. Everything else reads its result. Whether a layer has a prefill backend at all is still decided at layer construction, as before; without one there is no prefill metadata and prefills run sparse MQA. - Builders that plan kernels now read the route from the metadata, instead of calling the layer's private `_use_sparse_mha` (FlashInfer SM90) or reading `use_dense_mha` (ROCm). - Serving behavior is unchanged for every model that uses sparse MLA. Only the attention benchmark set them; it now sets `metadata.prefill.route`. - `masked_mha_workspace_fits` moves from the impl (static) to the builder, which owns the workspace, as `_topk_masks_fit`. - The quant-output fusion check now tests `attn_metadata.prefill is not None` before reading the route. - `build_shardq_metadata` takes the split. The route has to know about ShardQ before the prefill metadata is built. - The builder reads the backend name through `get_attn_backend()` from `layer_names[0]`, as it already does for `prefill_backend`. The benchmark's `MockLayer` and five test fakes that stand in for the layer now provide it. **Why behavior is the same.** Before, a prefill ran MHA when `_use_sparse_mha` was true, and `forward_mha` then picked dense when `seq_len <= topk` and masked otherwise. | Case | Before | After PR | | --- | --- | --- | | force-MQA, HiSparse or ShardQ | sparse MQA | sparse MQA | | `seq_len <= topk`, not PCP+DCP | `use_dense_mha` is true, so dense | dense | | `seq_len <= topk`, PCP+DCP | `use_dense_mha` is false, and masked needs DCP = 1, so sparse MQA | sparse MQA | | `seq_len > topk` | masked if eligible, else sparse MQA | the same masked check, else sparse MQA | The masked check now takes three inputs from the builder instead of from each layer: | Input | Before (layer) | After PR (builder) | Why they agree | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | HiSparse | `hisparse_cache is not None` | `hisparse_config is not None` | Sparse models give every sparse MLA impl the top-k buffer (`None` only for full-MLA configs), so every impl registers an index group. The group is a `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup` exactly when `hisparse_config` is set. | | Masked availability | `impl.masked_mha_available` **and** the builder's workspace (`masked_mha_workspace_fits` returned False without it) | the same conjunction, evaluated once when the builder is built: the workspace and `impl.masked_mha_available` of the group's first layer | A builder serves one KV cache group, whose layers share one KV cache spec (dtype included), so one layer's flag is the group's. The workspace follows the global KV dtype and the flag the layer's own; they differ under `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers` and for an MTP draft with its own speculative `kv_cache_dtype` (target bf16, draft `fp8_ds_mla`: the draft keeps sparse MQA, see "MTP draft with its own KV dtype" in Validation). ROCm's impl still sets the flag to False. | | Backend name, head dims | the layer's | `layer_names[0]`'s backend, `get_mla_dims` | One builder serves one backend and one model config. | **Indexer skip under ShardQ.** `should_skip_indexer_scoring` now reads `route is DENSE_MHA`; before, it read `use_dense_mha`, which was not cleared under ShardQ. The two can differ only on a step with ShardQ on, no decodes and every prefill within the top-k. With no decodes, every request is a prefill for the builder, so `build_shardq_split` sees the same or fewer requests with the same `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` and returns None when all are within the top-k (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/shardq.py`). So that step never has ShardQ, and the skip decision is unchanged. One log difference. The warning "top-k mask workspace is too small" used to be evaluated for short prefills, where dense MHA ran anyway, and under `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, where sparse MQA ran anyway (HiSparse and ShardQ already returned before it). It is now evaluated only when masked MHA is a candidate, so it no longer fires for batches it does not affect. **Not covered** - XPU builds its own metadata, treats every token as a decode and never takes the MHA branch. This PR does not change its backend file; XPU hardware was not exercised. - ROCm AITER sparse and FlashInfer SM90 change only mechanically: they read `route` instead of `use_dense_mha` / `_use_sparse_mha`. FlashInfer SM120 has no prefill backend (`supports_dense_mha_prefill = False`), so its prefills have no route and run sparse MQA, unchanged. They were not run on hardware; their CPU-side unit tests are in the table above. - HiSparse and PCP+DCP were checked by the unit test, the exhaustive check and code reading, not end to end. Their rules force sparse MQA. Their inputs (`hisparse_config`, `use_pcp`, `dcp_world_size`) are builder fields that this PR does not change. ShardQ was run end to end (TP4 row above). **Duplicate check.** No open PR moves the route decision. - Each open PR that touches the routing rules would get smaller on top of this one. - vllm-project/vllm#66088 would add its rule once, in `_prefill_route`. - vllm-project/vllm#65403 would pass its new input from the builder. - vllm-project/vllm#60806 would still change `_is_masked_mha_available`. It is still called twice (builder for the global KV dtype, impl for the layer's own), as before; both calls are needed because the two dtypes can differ. - vllm-project/vllm#55758 adds a base-class default for `masked_mha_available` so `_use_sparse_mha` can read it on any impl. This PR moves that read into the builder, which only sees sparse MLA impls; #55758 would no longer be needed for `_use_sparse_mha`. - vllm-project/vllm#66867 (replicated DSA attention, "per-step routing") routes between replicated and TP-sliced attention, not between prefill kernels; it does not overlap. - vllm-project/vllm#66424 and vllm-project/vllm#66454 change which ROCm AITER kernel runs inside a route (the sink fallback and the gfx950 OPUS prefill kernel). They do not read or change the route decision, and do not conflict with this PR. ---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Hy4] Sequence parallelism for iHC
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Apply sequence parallelism to HY4 iHC and normalization to eliminate redundant computation across TP ranks.

Keep iHC residuals token-sharded across decoder layers, using all-gather before attention and MLP and reduce-scatter after their outputs, without changing the existing attention or MoE parallel layout.

Reuse the sequence parallel infrastructure introduced in #66549. The model selects iHC SP on its own eligibility and token threshold, independently of attention ShardQ.

## Claims

- On 8×H200, TP8/DP1/EP8 prefill throughput improves **15.04% / 27.18% / 26.84%** at ISL2048 / 8192 / 32768, with median TTFT **−12.06% / −21.40% / −20.99%**, OSL1 and request-rate infinity.
- At an 8192-token step, each rank processes 1024 target iHC rows. Profiled iHC GPU time falls from **193.600 to 24.366 ms** per step, and the GPU busy interval from **729.533 to 571.312 ms**.
- Preserve global hidden-state rows for MTP and validate odd padding, shared indexers and prefix reuse.

## Validation

Hy4-preview-FP8 ModelOpt MXFP8 weights, Humming BF16 activations, FP32 iHC parameters, `fp8_ds_mla` KV and native MTP3. Default breakable CUDA graphs and serving sequence limits, `max_model_len=262144`. For the performance and evaluation runs, Python source is main `b93d6e4c17` for the baseline and PR commit `a252915fea` for the candidate; both arms reuse native extensions built at `329f93e190`, with Torch 2.14/CUDA13, FlashInfer 0.7.3 and Humming 0.1.19. Source integrity is checked against 3443 Python-file hashes per arm.

The head `f2cead2f46` decouples the iHC SP eligibility from ShardQ and keeps the measured path: ShardQ stays active in this configuration and the threshold remains 1024 tokens. Throughput, profile and GSM8K were not re-run on it.

Each ISL uses same-GPU serial A/B/A, with three measured seeds per arm. Profiling runs separately after throughput. Warmups are excluded. Each client run uses 128/32/16 requests at ISL2048/8192/32768, OSL1 and RPS infinity.

| ISL | A1 req/s | B req/s | A2 req/s | Throughput difference | Baseline drift | Median TTFT difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | 3.4642 | 3.9846 | 3.4632 | **+15.04%** | −0.031% | −12.06% |
| 8192 | 1.3513 | 1.7182 | 1.3508 | **+27.18%** | −0.035% | −21.40% |
| 32768 | 0.3356 | 0.4259 | 0.3359 | **+26.84%** | +0.076% | −20.99% |

All measured requests completed with the expected input/output token counts.

<details>
<summary>Repeated-run throughput ranges</summary>

Three seeds per arm (102/104/106), in req/s.

| ISL | A1 range | B range | A2 range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | 3.4639–3.4648 | 3.9559–4.0015 | 3.4592–3.4654 |
| 8192 | 1.3505–1.3517 | 1.7155–1.7215 | 1.3498–1.3513 |
| 32768 | 0.3356–0.3357 | 0.4256–0.4264 | 0.3358–0.3362 |

</details>

The 8K rank-0 profile covers five steps, each with 78 target layers and one MTP layer:

| GPU work, ms/step | A1 (main) | B (SP) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iHC pre stage 1 | 137.184 | 17.695 |
| iHC pre stage 2 | 21.503 | 2.394 |
| iHC post | 34.913 | 4.277 |
| Communication | 127.334 | 146.762 |
| GEMMs | 212.147 | 212.472 |
| FlashMLA sparse attention | 67.015 | 66.979 |
| ShardQ packing | 37.566 | 37.642 |
| GPU busy interval | 729.533 | 571.312 |

Target RMSNorm inputs are `[1024, 6144]` per rank. Communication calls rise from 161 to 318 per step as the subblock boundaries use all-gather and reduce-scatter.

Default GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, `max_tokens=256`, temperature 0, seed 42): main **0.89613** (invalid 0.00379, 87.311 s) vs SP **0.89234** (invalid 0.00303, 83.910 s).

```sh
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve /gpfs/rd/models/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
  --served-model-name hy4 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8256 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --load-format fastsafetensors --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/tmp/hy4-traces","torch_profiler_record_shapes":true,"torch_profiler_with_stack":false}'

vllm-rs bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8256 \
  --model /gpfs/rd/models/Hy4-preview-FP8 --served-model-name hy4 \
  --tokenizer /gpfs/rd/models/Hy4-preview-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 --prompt-token-ids \
  --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --num-prompts 32 --seed 102 --disable-tqdm
```

Use `(ISL, num_prompts)=(2048,128),(8192,32),(32768,16)` and seeds 102/104/106. Reset the prefix cache between client runs after the recorded warmups.

The initial row-sharding repro on main failed with `('iHC token rows', 255, 128, 255)`. At `f2cead2f46`, both real TP2 generation cases, eager and default graphs, pass together with three sink reload regressions through TP8: **5 passed** (368.91 s). Pre-commit passed, including mypy and CI test tethering.

The TP2 fixture uses a 3073-token prompt and odd 1025-token chunks within `max_model_len=4096`. Each case compares a replicated-row reference with iHC SP, first with attention ShardQ disabled and then enabled. In eager mode, every rank must observe local iHC rows on a step of at least 1024 tokens in both runs, with non-null ShardQ metadata in the second. With the sources of the previous head `fb2c086ca8`, where ShardQ gated iHC SP, the ShardQ-disabled run fails.

```text
(Worker_TP1_EP1 pid=552398) ERROR 11-17 04:11:59 [multiproc_executor.py:1223] AssertionError: ('iHC token rows', 1025, 513, 1025)
================== 1 failed, 17 warnings in 124.14s (0:02:04) ==================
```

**PR, `f2cead2f46`**

```text
================== 5 passed, 17 warnings in 368.91s (0:06:08) ==================
/usr/lib/python3.12/multiprocessing/resource_tracker.py:254: UserWarning: resource_tracker: There appear to be 1 leaked shared_memory objects to clean up at shutdown
  warnings.warn('resource_tracker: There appear to be %d '
```

The `resource_tracker` shared-memory shutdown warning also appears in the earlier main repro log.

</details>

## Details

The local iHC stream owns `ceil(tokens / TP)` rows. Each subblock gathers the normalized hidden input, computes the existing attention/FFN path, and reduce-scatters the partial output before local post-gating. Final normalization is followed by a gather for MTP. Short model batches use the deferred all-reduce with replicated rows. The MoE constructor asserts that the factory honored deferred output reduction through `skip_final_all_reduce`.

Eligibility requires iHC, TP>1, DP1/PP1/PCP1/DCP1 and a step of at least 1024 model token rows. It does not depend on attention ShardQ, since attention and MLP always receive the gathered rows. LoRA, batch-invariant mode, auxiliary-hidden-state speculation and passthrough MoE are excluded. Humming is the measured MoE backend.

iHC SP also applies where ShardQ is disabled or ineligible. The TP2 regression covers that case, and its throughput has not been measured. Validation here covers H200 with FP8 KV. Blackwell and NVFP4-KV validation are pending.

The area search found no separate open HY4 iHC-SP implementation. #66549 provides the shared scheduling pattern, while #67490 enables sink-aware ShardQ in the measured configuration.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Support output logprobs for gpt-oss in the Responses API
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Fixes #61629. Follow-up to #23319, where "logprobs + harmony" was left as a TODO.

`/v1/responses` returned 400 for gpt-oss when `include=["message.output_text.logprobs"]` was set. This adds logprobs for output text in both streaming and non-streaming, kept in parity.

## Design
- `HarmonyParser.process_chunk` already emits one `Segment` per token; `Segment` now carries `token_index`.
- `HarmonyContext` picks logprobs for output-text tokens (final channel + commentary preambles with no recipient, excluding Harmony control tokens), aligned per segment for streaming and grouped per message for the final output.
- Streaming deltas, `output_item.done`, and the final response all convert from those same entries via one helper, so they report identical logprobs.
- Tokens with an empty delta (partial multi-byte characters) are buffered and attached to the next text delta.

## Test Plan
- New unit tests (`test_harmony_logprobs.py`): real gpt-oss tokens fed in one chunk vs 1/2/3/7-token chunks, asserting identical per-message logprobs; control tokens and reasoning excluded.
- New e2e tests in `test_harmony.py`: non-streaming logprobs cover exactly `output_text`; streaming delta logprobs == done-event logprobs == final response logprobs.

## Test Result
Unit tests pass locally. E2E tests need a GPU and have not been run locally.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Re-handshake a pull peer whose connection NIXL reports lost
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In pull mode, invalidate a remote engine as soon as one of its transfers fails with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, so the existing drain, backoff and re-handshake path from #55471 reconnects it. Today the dead peer is kept, because its NIXL metadata stays loaded, and every later read to it fails until a restart.

This is the pull-mode fix from #66795 (by Yongye Zhu, co-author here), split out so it can be reviewed apart from that PR's push-mode changes. It is an alternative trigger to #61500. Related: #59971 (production report), #66011 (see "Interplay with #66011").

## Claims

- A pull that fails with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` (NIXL's `nixlRemoteDisconnectError`) invalidates its remote engine on the next `_cleanup_remote_engines`, even though the engine's metadata is still loaded. Its agents are removed once in-flight reads drain, and the next read re-handshakes.
- Other transfer errors are unchanged: they invalidate the engine only when the metadata probe reports it missing (#55471).
- Push mode is unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit test.** `TestPeerReplacement::test_lost_connection_invalidates_peer_with_metadata`: a read fails with a remote disconnect while the peer's metadata stays loaded. `[True]` fails without the fix (the dead peer is kept) and passes with it. `[False]` checks that another error still keeps the peer.

**End to end** (from #66795, run with an earlier version of this change that matched the error by name instead of `isinstance`; equivalent for NIXL's real exception). MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (NVFP4), disaggregated on B300: 8 prefill workers (DP2/EP2 each) and 1 DEP8 decode worker, NIXL over UCX/RoCE, agentic-coding trace replay at concurrency 480 for 30 minutes:

| run | `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` | requests failed on KV load | failed requests |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 987 | 905 | 1,858 |
| with this fix | 0 | 0 | 10 / 21,512 (empty responses, not KV load) |

TODO before review: re-run the NIXL connector unit suites on this branch.

## Details

**Failure flow** (decode side, pull):

1. D starts a NIXL READ from P's blocks (`start_load_kv` → `_read_blocks`).
2. The UCX endpoint between D and P fails. The READ completes with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`; `_pop_done_transfers` reports the request in `failed_recving` and adds P's engine to `_failed_remote_engines`.
3. `_cleanup_remote_engines` probes `check_remote_metadata` for P's agents. The metadata is still loaded, so P stays valid.
4. NIXL never moves a failed endpoint back to connected, so the next request to P fails at post with the same error. Steps 2–4 repeat for every request routed to P until a restart.

**Fix.** `_handle_failed_transfer` takes the transfer's exception. When it is a `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` (loaded lazily from `nixl._bindings` via `nixl_utils`, like `nixlXferTelemetry`), the engine is recorded in `_disconnected_remote_engines`, and `_cleanup_remote_engines` marks it invalid without the metadata probe. Both pull call sites pass the exception.

**Comparison with #61500.** #61500 invalidates a peer after two failed requests with no completed read in between, for any transport error. This change uses the error code instead:
- A failed endpoint returns `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` on every later post (per #61500's own analysis), so this recovers on the first failure, or at worst on the second, as #61500 does, if the first failure carried a different code.
- An isolated error of another kind keeps the peer, so there is no threshold to tune.
- #61500 would also catch a connection that fails without ever reporting `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`; we have not seen one.

**Interplay with #66011.** While the connection is down, D's heartbeats to P fail too, so P's leases can lapse (default `kv_lease_duration` is 30 s; the re-handshake backoff can reach 60 s). Before this change such requests failed; after it, a request that waited through the outage can be read over the new connection from blocks P has already recycled. #66011 closes that window: it does not credit heartbeat rounds that did not reach every remote rank, so those reads are declined and follow `kv_load_failure_policy`. This should land with or after #66011.

**Not covered:** if the re-handshake's `loadRemoteMD` itself fails, NIXL leaves the agent half-loaded and later loads fail with `NIXL_ERR_INVALID_PARAM` (ai-dynamo/nixl#2437). vLLM cannot clear that state; the fix belongs in NIXL.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add NemotronLabsDiffusion support with tri-mode inference
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add native Nemotron Labs Diffusion 3B/8B text-model support: masked block diffusion and ordinary autoregressive inference. This builds on #48279 and is the foundation for #60287 and #60288; tracking issue #60283 covers the stack.

## Claims

- Load the Ministral backbone and untied diffusion head using checkpoint dimensions and RoPE settings.
- Use causal prompt prefill/block commit and bidirectional masked denoising, with literal per-request temperatures.
- Support ordinary AR through `hf_overrides={"ar_mode": true}`.
- Defer linear speculation as requested in review. There are no changes to `gpu/model_runner.py` or the model-state interface in this version.
- Use the Transformers v5 `PreTrainedConfig` name required by current main.

## Validation

Rebased onto upstream main `1a3a7a8f01a8c1a3184151b8185072efda11daab`.

CPU-only tests of the complete stacked branch: **93 passed, 9 skipped**. This runs the sampling-parameter suite and the Nemotron model unit/configuration suite with CUDA disabled. The nine skips are CUDA/checkpoint-gated cases, not GPU validation.

The applicable full pre-commit suite passed, including type checking, test tethering and forbidden-import checks. GPU-serving and model-quality evaluations have **not** been rerun after this rebase. CUDA/checkpoint-gated tests must not be counted as passing GPU validation.

Historical public 3B results, before this rebase:

| Mode | Correct / total | GSM8K accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Confidence-based diffusion | 1,155 / 1,319 | 87.57% |
| Ordinary AR | 1,182 / 1,319 | 89.61% |

Diffusion was evaluated at `83594fb280`; AR at `0df15ea7e5`. Configuration: official 3B checkpoint, BF16, H100, TP=1, Triton attention, eager backbone, temperature 0, concurrency 8, context 1,024 and maximum 750 generated tokens. Diffusion used block size 32 and confidence threshold 0.9. These are historical scores, not measurements of the new head.

Reproduction commands:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/test_sampling_params.py \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_nemotron_dllm.py -q

NEMOTRON_DLM_MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-3B \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/models/language/generation \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_nemotron_dllm.py -v

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

## Details

The previous implementation, including linear speculation, is preserved at [deferred/nemotron-linear-spec-20261009](https://github.com/sajadn/vllm/tree/deferred/nemotron-linear-spec-20261009). A separate follow-up can restore its speculative sampler, configuration, prefill-logit hook and tests without holding up masked decisions.

The diffusion warmup guard remains because masked diffusion does not support structured-output grammar masks. Vision inputs are outside this change. Mixed-batch logprob bookkeeping and unsupported pipeline-parallel configurations are addressed by #60287, not claimed fixed in this foundation. The original fork's 3B diffusion result of 1,161/1,319 versus this implementation's historical 1,155/1,319 remains unexplained. No new speedup, long-context, quantization or multi-GPU accuracy claim is made.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Generate quantization method, scheme, and linear backend tables
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds two quantization docs pages whose tables are generated from source at docs build time
(`docs/mkdocs/gen_files/generate_quantization_tables.py`), following the existing attention-backend tables. Docs and
docs-build tooling only; no runtime change.

- `docs/features/quantization/formats.md` ("Methods and Schemes"): terms, `--quantization` methods, online shorthands,
  and the scheme names accepted by `--quantization-config`.
- `docs/features/quantization/kernels.md` ("Kernel Backends"): `--linear-backend` values with the platforms and
  quantization types each covers, and the `linear_backend_per_quant` keys.

## Claims

- Every table is read from a registry written as a literal: `method_to_config`, `_ONLINE_SHORTHANDS`,
  `QUANT_KEY_NAMES`, the platform `supported_quantization` allow-lists, `_ONLINE_LINEAR_METHODS` / `_ONLINE_MOE_METHODS`,
  the `_POSSIBLE_*_KERNELS` registries, and `_LINEAR_BACKEND_KERNEL_MAP`.
- Adding a method, shorthand, scheme, dtype, or kernel does not require editing the generator; a value it does not
  recognize is rendered as written in the source. The build fails only when a registry it looks up by name is missing
  or is no longer a literal.
- No hand-written per-row notes. Prose covers terms and how to read the tables.

## Validation

Strict docs build, including the API reference, with no warnings:

```console
$ VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu mkdocs build --strict
# exit 0; formats/ and kernels/ contain no left-over `gen:` marker
```

(`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` is only needed on a GPU host, where the existing argparse generator otherwise resolves the
CUDA platform in a docs environment without torch.)

A local script compared the AST-derived data with the imported objects on CPU: scheme fields for every
`QUANT_KEY_NAMES` / `_WEIGHT_QUANT_KEY_NAMES` entry, shorthand weight keys, the method-to-class mapping via
`get_quantization_config`, the kernel registries, the backend map, and the online-weight column (using
`issubclass(..., OnlineLMHeadMethodBase)` as ground truth). No mismatches. The script is not part of this PR.

`pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, markdownlint, docstring style) passes on the changed files. No model evaluation: docs only.

## Details

**Motivation.** The quantization section had no page listing the method, shorthand, and scheme names, and its
hand-maintained capability tables have drifted (the landing page still lists removed and out-of-tree methods). The
first version of this PR generated one table and kept hand-written per-scheme notes and a hand-written shorthand
table; within two weeks both were stale against `main` and the generator no longer built. This version generates the
enumerable content and removes the notes.

**What is not generated.** Whether a kernel runs on a device is decided by code (`is_supported`, `can_implement`), which
mixes hardware requirements with library availability, so hardware support per kernel is not rendered. "Platforms" in
the method tables means accepted by the platform allow-list at startup.

**Known limits.**

- The `linear_backend_per_quant` keys are not in a registry; the generator reads the string literal each selector
  passes as `quantization=`. A registry in `kernels/linear/__init__.py` would be a better source.
- `lut_b` is shown as its `QuantKey` describes it (codebook as the scale); the page says so.
- The `lm_head` marker in the scheme table relies on the online method class name containing `LMHead`.

**Follow-ups.** MoE backend tables, removing the stale "Supported Hardware" table on the landing page, and fixes to
the per-method pages are separate PRs. No duplicate work: no other open PR adds a quantization docs generator.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Apply DCP config checks to NixlPullConnector
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60189.

`NixlConnector` and `NixlPullConnector` are two names for the same connector, but configuration checks match connector names literally. Using the newer name skips the existing DCP checks and default-setting code.

For example, with DeepSeek-V2-Lite, TP=2, DCP=2, cache block size 16, and `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size` unset:

```text
NixlConnector:     cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = 16
NixlPullConnector: cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = 1
```

The existing code sets this value to the cache block size for NIXL. Changing the connector name should not skip that adjustment.

## Claims

- Handle both names centrally in `KVTransferConfig.has_connector()`, including inside `MultiConnector`.
- Apply the existing DCP checks and default adjustment to both names.
- Preserve valid explicit interleave values, including 1, and reject invalid explicit values under both names. Automatically resolved values are finalized before the block-size check.
- Do not change the DCP implementation or add non-MLA DCP support. Other connector names still match exactly.

## Validation

The refresh preserves #62330's interleave finalization from the global KV cache groups before profiling. Configuration tests use real `KVCacheGroup` and `AttentionSpec` objects from the current interface, and the unsupported non-MLA cases exercise the public `LLM` constructor before model weights are loaded. The obsolete HiSparse warning and its regression test are removed, following #64559. The routed-experts connector restriction and its tests are also removed, following #62056's P/D support; `tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py` now matches main.
